properties.DESCRIPTION: THE RUMFORD NATIONAL GRAPHICS SITE WAS FORMERLY USED BY A POULTRY COMPANY FOR TRUCK MAINTENANCE, AND CURRENTLY USED AS A CHURCH AS OF THIS WRITING.  CHLORINATED SOLVENTS (PCE/TCE) AND PETROLEUM WERE RELEASED INTO FLOOR DRAINS FROM TRUCK MAINTENANCE ACTIVITIES IN THE 1950S-80S, AND EVENTUALLY IMPACTED THE SITE BEDROCK SUPPLY WEL B-100.  INVESTIGATIONS BY RG GERBER AND OTHERS FROM THE LATE 1980S TO 1990S FOUND CHLORINATED SOLVENTS IN BEDROCK MONITORING WELLS.  A GROUNDWATER EXTRACTION AND TREATMENT SYSTEM (GETS) WAS INSTALLED AND OPERATED INTERMITTENTLY FOR ALMOST A DECADE WITH LIMITED IMPROVEMENT IN GROUNDWATER QUALITY.  BY 2012 DEP HAD THE RP BEGIN TO EVALUATE VAPOR INTRUSION, CONDUCT A RISK ASSESSMENT, AND PREPARE AN APPLICATION TO THE VRAP PROGRAM.  RESULTS OF THE VI INVESTIGATION AND RISK ASSESSMENT SHOWED THAT INDOOR AIR AT THE FACILITY WAS NOT IMPACTED BY CVOCS, OFFSITE HOMEOWNERS DOWNGRADIENT WERE NOT IMPACTED, VAPORS COULD POSE A RISK TO CONSTRUCTION WORKERS IN THE AREA OF HIGHEST GROUNDWATER IMPACTS (B-100 AND B-101), AND THAT CONCENTRATIONS OF PCE AND TCE WERE DECREASING AND INCREASING, RESPECTIVELY OVER TIME.  IN THE SUMMER OF 2015 THE DEPARTMENT APPROVED OF AND THE RP DISMANTLED THE GETS SYSTEM, GROUTED AND SEALED B-100, AND ABANDONED THE BEDROCK MONITORING WELLS.  INSTITUTIONAL CONTROLS AND A SOIL MANAGEMENT PLAN ARE IN PLACE WITH A VRAP CERTIFICATE OF COMPLETION.  NO FURTHER ACTION IS EXPECTED UNLESS THE EXISTING BUILDINGS ARE TORN DOWN AND THE SITE IS REDEVELOPED.
properties.SUMMARY:
VRAP COMPLETED THE CLOSURE OF THE LONGSTANDING RUMFORD NATIONAL GRAPHICS SITE IN BELFAST, MAINE. THE SITE OPERATED AS A POULTRY FACILITY AND TRUCK MAINTENANCE GARAGE FROM CIRCA 1955 UNTIL THE 1980¿S, THEN LATER AS STORAGE FOR ROLLED PAPER. HISTORIC SITE OPERATIONS RESULTED IN VOLATILE ORGANIC COMPOUND CONTAMINATION IN THE BEDROCK BOTH ON AND OFF SITE. THE RESPONSIBLE PARTY AND THE DEPARTMENT AGREED TO A REMEDIAL ACTION PLAN AND ADMINISTRATIVE ORDER OF CONSENT IN 1994 THAT REQUIRED THEM TO CONNECT SEVERAL NEIGHBORING PROPERTIES TO THE PUBLIC WATER SUPPLY AND TO INSTALL AND MAINTAIN A GROUNDWATER EXTRACTION TREATMENT SYSTEM (GETS) TO PUMP AND TREAT CONTAMINATED GROUNDWATER. 

THE GETS OPERATED INTERMITTENTLY FROM 1994 TO APPROXIMATELY 2012 WITH SEVERAL PERIODS OF SHUTDOWN DUE TO POWER OUTAGES, SYSTEM ASSESSMENT, UPGRADES, AND FAILS. ALTHOUGH THE GETS HAD TREATED APPROXIMATELY 3,550,000-GALLONS OF WATER, LITTLE PROGRESS HAD BEEN MADE IN RESTORING THE AQUIFER. WITH NO END IN SIGHT AND SEVERE DETERIORATION OF THE GETS, IN 2006 THE RP BEGAN PROPOSING TO AMEND THE REMEDIAL ACTION PLAN (RAP) TO INCLUDE UTILIZING A RISK ASSESSMENT AS AN ALTERNATIVE METHOD OF DETERMINING THE APPROPRIATENESS OF TERMINATING THE OPERATION OF THE GETS. FINALLY IN 2013, THE SITE WAS ENTERED INTO THE VRAP PROGRAM. ADDITIONAL GROUNDWATER, SOIL, SOIL VAPOR AND INDOOR AIR SAMPLING AT BOTH THE SITE AND AT NEIGHBORING RESIDENTIAL PROPERTIES AND A HUMAN HEALTH RISK ASSESSMENT CONCLUDED THAT THE ESTIMATED HEALTH RISKS FROM CURRENT AND FUTURE USERS DID NOT EXCEED ACCEPTABLE LEVELS. THEREFORE, IN 2015, THE GETS WAS DISMANTLED AND MONITORING WELLS WERE ABANDONED. A CERTIFICATE OF COMPLETION WITH A RELEASE FROM THE 1994 AOC WAS ISSUED IN FEBRUARY 2016. THE PROPERTY IS BEING USED AS THE BEACON OF HOPE ON THE HILL CHURCH.

NARRATIVE BY STEVE BREZINSKI:  ON WED. 7/25/01, DEP'S ANN HEMENWAY WAS NOTIFIED OF GASO. CONTAM. SOIL DISCOVERED AND EXCAVATED OUT BY PORTLAND PUMP CO. (PPC) DURING UST FACILITY UPGRADE WORK.  ON 7/26/01 I VISITED FOR MS. HEMENWAY AND CONFIRMED APPROX. 18 YDS OF MILDLY CONTAM. SAND REMOVED TO PUT IN A NEW SIGN-FOOTING AT THE CORNER OF LISBON & UNION STS.  THE SOIL APPEARS TO BE REMAINING FROM THAT DISCOVERED AND MANAGED IN 1989 BY DEP'S BRAD HAHN (P-725-89).  IN OCT. OF 1989 I & HAHN HAD NOTED THAT A L DOGGETT CO. HAD REMOVED THE OLD UST FACILITY AND INSTALLED THE PRESENT FACILITY BUT FAILED TO NOTIFY AND REMEDIATE THE DISCHARGE AS REQUIRED.  DEP DISCOVERED THE CONTAMINATION AFTER THE NEW INSTALLATION WAS IN SO HAD NO OPPORTUNITY TO EVALUATE THE SITE AND DO A THOROUGH CLEAN-UP.  AT THE TIME (1989), WE WERE NOT AWARE THAT THIS SITE WAS IN ZONE-2 OF A MUNICIPAL WELLHEAD PROTECTION ZONE (SEE MAPS).  DEP GEOLOGIST, ALEX PUGH AND I, AGREED TO AN INTERMEDIATE CLEAN-UP GOAL.
   BASED ON THE KNOWN HISTORY AND MY OBSERVATIONS, ON 7/27/01, I ISSUED A VIRGIN LETTER TO THE PPC OPERATOR, FOR RECYCLING THE SOIL OFFSITE @ CRS.  THE SOIL WAS EXCAVATED AND TRANSPORTED BY PORTLAND PUMP.  PORTLAND PUMP WAS ALSO INSTALLING A NEW SUMP OVER AN UST BEHIND THE BUILDING (SEE PHOTOS, THE 7/9/01, FACILITY REG. AMMENDMENT, & THE SITE SKETCH).
   GASOLINE CONTAMINATION IS UNDERSTOOD TO REMAIN ONSITE AND HAS NOT BEEN REMEDIATED TO AN INTERMEDIATE GOAL AT THIS TIME.  I HAVE EXPLAINED THIS TO GETTY'S JIM STEWART AND ADVISED HIM THAT NO FURTHER CLEAN-UP IS REQUIRED IN THE IMMEDIATE FUTURE, THOUGH ANY SOIL DISTURBED SHOULD BE PROPERLY MANAGED AND A CLEAN-UP INITIATED ANY TIME POSSIBLE IN CONJUNCTION WITH OTHER WORK, OR IF CONDITIONS CHANGE AND THREATENED RECEPTORS WARRANT REMEDIAL WORK.  FURTHER REMEDIATION MAY HAPPEN WITH SCHEDULED MDOT WORK IN AUTUMN, 2001.  BASED ON THE AGE, I UNDERSTAND THIS DISCHARGE IS NOT UST INS. FUND COVERABLE AT THIS TIME.

properties.SITE_NAME: MID-COAST SOLID WASTE QUARRY LANDFILL AND TRANSFER STATION
properties.DESCRIPTION: 4 ACRE ACTIVE LANDFILL.  THE AREA KNOWN AS JACOBS QUARRY HAS BEEN USED BY THE TOWNS OF CAMDEN, HOPE, LINCOLNVILLE AND ROCKPORT TO DISPOSE OF VARIOUS TYPES OF SOLID WASTE SINCE ABOUT 1930. TANNERY WASTE WAS DISPOSED OF FOR A WHILE. IN 1983 THE FOUR PARTICIPATING TOWNS DISCONTINUED THE PRACTICE OF LANDFILLING MUNICIPAL SOLID WASTE, HOWEVER, THE QUARRY SITE HAS CONTINUED TO RECEIVE TREES AND BRUSH, CONSTRUCTION DEBRIS, AND OTHER WOOD WASTE. IT HAS BEEN THE TOWNS DESIRE TO KEEP THE SITE AVAILABLE FOR THIS USE, ALTHOUGH DEP PRESSURE TO COMPLETELY CLOSEOUT AND PROVIDE REMEDIAL CLEAN-UP AT THE SITE HAS BEEN MOUNTING OVER THE YEARS. IT WAS RECOGNIZED THAT SURFACE RUNOFF WAS BEING CONTAMINATED. NO FURTHER DISPOSAL OF ANYTHING IN THE QUARRY WAS STRONGLY RECOMMENDED.

THIS SITE PROCESSED WOOL FROM 1970-1981.  WASTEWATER GENERATED FROM THE MANUFACTURING PROCESS WAS DRAINED VIA SUBFLOOR PIPES TO AN INDOOR FILTER PIT, NEUTRALIZED AND DISCHARGED TO 2 OUTSIDE LAGOONS.THE LAGOONS HAD A DISCHARGE TO THE KENNEBEC RIVER, NPDES PERMIT #0000787, AND MAINE DISCHARGE PERMIT #603. HAZARDOUS SUBSTANCES IN THE WASTE-WATER INCLUDED SULFURIC AND OXALIC ACIDS, XYLENE, O-DICHLO-ROBENZENE AND PHENOL. SAMPLING IN 1987 SHOWED LOW LEVELS OF VOCS, SVOCS, AND INORGANICS IN THE LAGOON WATER AND SIGNIF-ICANT LEVELS IN THE SEDIMENTS. SAMPLING IN 1992 FOUND NO VOCS OR SVOCS AND INORGANICS BELOW HEALTH STANDARDS. THE FIRST 2 ROUNDS OF MONITORING HAVE NOT FOUND GROUND WATER CONTAMINATION.THE LAGOONS ARE NOW BEING CLEANED AND CLOSED.

THE SITE HAS BEEN USED FOR VARIOUS TANNING OPERATIONS SINCE THE 1950S. A DRY-CLEANING OPERATION TO CLEAN SHEEPSKIN SHEARLINGS WAS USED FROM 1979-1981 IN THE FINISHING BUILD-ING. THIS PROCESS GENERATED 5-10 GAL/WK PCE. PERSISTENT DETECTION OF PCE IN GROUND WATER SINCE 1988 LED WILTON TANNING TO INVESTIGATE THIS SITE FOR PCE IN 1994.  PCE WAS FOUND IN SOILS BENEATH AND OUTSIDE THE TANNERY IN THE VICIN-ITY OF THE FORMER DRY-CLEANING UNIT. 12 PROBES FOR SOIL SAMPLES, GROUND WATER SAMPLES AND PIEZOMETRIC DATA AT 3 LOCATIONS WERE INSTALLED.  THE CONTAMINATED AREA IS WELL-DEFINED. REMEDIATION STRATEGIES ARE CURRENTLY BEING EVALUATED TO INTERCEPT THE LEADING EDGE OF THE PLUME BEFORE IT REACHES WILSON STREAM. THE AREA IS SERVED BY PUBLIC WATER.

THE PLANT MANUFACTURES AIR CONTROL EQUIPMENT AND HAS OCCUPIED THE SITE SINCE 1968. PLANT OPERATIONS GENERATE ~600 GPD OF WASTEWATER, AND NON-CONTACT COOLING WATER. PROCESS WATER CONTAINS ORGANIC AND INORGANIC COMPOUNDS. A 1983 INSPECTION FOUND DISCHARGED UNTREATED PROCESS WATER DIRECTLY TO THE ENVIRONMENT. WATTS EXCAVATED CONTAMINATED SOIL AND SEDIMENTS AND INSTALLED A WASTEWATER TREATMENT SYSTEM. THEY EXCEEDED NPDES PERMIT LIMITS FROM 1984-1988. IN 1988 METALS, VOCS, SVOCS AND OIL AND GREASE WERE FOUND IN SURFACE WATER, SOIL AND GROUND WATER. REMEDIATION IN-CLUDES REMOVAL OF CONTAMINATED CONCRETE, SOIL, RESTORATION OF AFFECTED WETLANDS AND PUMP-AND-TREAT GROUND WATER UNTIL CONTAMINANT LEVELS ARE AT OR BELOW MEGS. REMEDIATION IS ONGOING.

GTE MANUFACTURES COPPER CLAD STEEL LEAD WIRES, MOLYBDENUM CONDUITS FOR MERCURY SWITCHES, FLATHEADED LEADS AND GLASSWORK FOR LEADS.  THE HAZARDOUS WASTE IS GENERATED FROM DEGREASING AND CLEANING. THE CHEMICALS USED ARE 1,1,1-TRICHLOROETHANE, METHANOL, AND PETROLEUM DISTILLATES (STODDARD SOLVENT). THE STUDY SUGGESTS THAT THE CONTAMINATION OF THE TAYLOR WELL DOES NOT POSE A HIGH RISK TO ANY OF THE OTHERS.

IRVING TANNING PRODUCES FINISHED LEATHER.  PRIOR TO 1990 THE PLANT PROCESSED RAW HIDES THROUGH-THE-BLUE. THEY NOW PURCHASE PRE-TANNED HIDES AND RE-TAN AND FINISH THEM. THE ANNEX DOES THE FINISHING OF THE HIDES. THIS PROCESS REQUIRES USE OF SOLVENTS. THERE IS A SOLVENT STORAGE AREA IN THE ANNEX.  INVESTIGATIONS BY MDEP DISCOVERED FLOOR DRAINS AND A SUBFLOOR PIPE SYSTEM LEADING TO A MANHOLE AND A CULVERT OUTSIDE THE BUILDING.  THE POINT OF DISCHARGE IS UNKNOWN.  ANALYTICAL RESULTS SUGGEST THAT THE PIPES AND MANHOLE CONTAINED TOLUENE, ETHYLBENZENE, XYLENE, 1,3,5-TRIMETHYLBENZENE, 1,2,4-TRIMETHYLBENZENE AND DIISOBUTYL KETONE.  DIISOBUTYL KETONE WAS ALSO DETECTED IN SOIL SAMPLES TAKEN SOUTH OF THE BUILDING.  THE INVESTIGATION IS ONGOING.

EUGENE HACK (TY) OWNS A PROPERTY IN LAMOINE THAT HE BUILT AND LIVED IN FOR SOME TIME.  HE HAS SINCE MOVED TO VA AND NOW HE IS TRYING TO SELL THE LAMOINE PROPERTY.  POTENTIAL BUYERS (THE ALLEYS) FOR SOME REASON HAD THE WATER TESTED AND FOUND THAT IT WAS CONTAMINATED WITH GASOLINE INCLUDING MTBE.  ACTUALLY IT WAS MIMMIE ALLEY THAT CONTACTED ME FIRST.  NEXT PLAYER WAS TY'S REALTOR IN THE PERSON OF GARY FOUNTAIN.  GARY INDICATED THAT I WAS NOT TO GET INVOLVED UNLESS TY ASKED ME TO.  WHEN TY CONTACTED ME, WE DISCUSSED THE FILTER OPTION.  HE WAS NOT HAPPY WITH THIS BECAUSE HE FELT THAT THE VALUE OF HIS PROPERTY WAS COMPROMISED BY THE PRESENCE OF A WATER SUPPLY THAT WAS CONTAMINATED.  (I MUST SAY THAT THE PROPERTY STRIKES ME AS BEING AN EXPENSIVE PIECE OF REAL ESTATE).  WHEN I HEARD ABOUT THE CASE AGAIN A FEW DAYS LATER, TY HAD DRILLED ANOTHER WELL.  HE HAD HIRED CES TO ANALYZE THE PROBLEM AND THEIR RECOMMENDATION WAS TO DRILL ANOTHER WELL 300 FEET AWAY FROM THE ORIGINAL ONE.  THE NEW WELL (THE SECOND ONE) WAS MORE CONTAMINATED THAN THE FIRST.  WE DID A PUMP TEST ON THE NEW WELL AND FOUND OUT THAT IT WAS UP STRIKE FROM THE FIRST WELL.  BY THIS TIME TECH SERVICES HAD ACCEPTED THE CASE AND PAUL BLOOD IS DOING MORE EXPLORATION AND HANDLING DETAILS SUCH AS ISSUING THIRD PARTY DAMAGE CLAIM FORMS.  WE DID INSTALL FILTERS, BUT TY WOULD STILL LIKE A CLEAN WELL.

ON 01/31/96, 1157 HOURS JODY WINN, WHO SHARES A RESIDENCE WITH HER HUSBAND CLIFF, CONTACTED THIS OFFICE ABOUT OIL IN HER WELL.  SHE INDICATED THAT THE ODOR WAS REAL STRONG AT TIMES AND THAT SHE HAD RECENTLY SEEN GLOBULES OF OIL ON TOP OF THE WATER.  THE LATTER TURNED OUT TO BE OIL THAT WAS MOST LIKELY FROM THE VESSEL THAT THE WATER WAS IN.  IT WAS A PLASTIC CONTAINER THAT ONE WOULD USE TO STORE LEFT-OVERS.  HOWEVER, I WAS GETTING A 3-4 PPM HIT WITH THE PHOTON RIGHT OFF THE SURFACE OF THE COLD WATER.  SHE SAID THAT THEY HAD FIRST EXPERIENCED THE ODOR TWO WEEKS EARLIER, AND THAT IT SEEMED TO BE ASSOCIATED WITH RUN OFF FROM  SNOW MELT AND RAIN.  THE AMES' WHO ARE ABOUT 290' EAST OF THE WINNS' HAD EXPERIENCED THE ODOR IN SEPTEMBER-FOUR MONTHS EARLIER.  I SAMPLED BOTH WELLS FOR DROS AND THEY CAME BACK 57 PPB FOR AMES AND 57 PPB FOR THE WINN WELL.  THE ANALYSIS REPORT STATED THAT THE DRO QUANTITATION INCLUDED MATERIALS THAT MIGHT REPRESENT GASOLINE.  I RESAMPLED AND THE RESULTS WERE 160 PPB MTBE AND 96 PPB GRO FOR THE AMES WELL AND 4500 PPB MTBE AND 2400 PPB GRO FOR THE WINN WELL.  NOTE THAT EVERYTHING IS CONSISTENT WITH AN EAST TO WEST GROUND WATER DIRECTION.  ALSO, THIS RESULT INDICATES THAT THE  SPILL DOES NOT PREDATE MTBE, WHICH I BELIEVE CAME INTO BEING IN THE LATE SIXTIES.  (PAUL BLOOD REMARKED ON THE UNUSUALNESS OF HAVING  THOSE LEVELS OF GRO IN THE ABSENCE OF BTEX.)

MEANWHILE, I ESCORTED NORLENS TO THE SITE SO THAT THEY COULD DO THEIR PREINSTALLATION WORK.  ON 3/7/96 BOTH RESIDENCES HAD A TWO FILTER SYSTEM INSTALLED.  THE WINN WELL IS 250 FEET DEEP AND IT WAS DRILLED BY LEON WILLIAMS OF CORINA (278-2353) FOR A PARTY BY THE NAME OF COZAK OR SELMONT.  THE OVER BURDEN IS GENERALLY THIN, AROUND 2-3 FEET AND THE WELLS ARE NOT FAR FROM PUFFER POND.  THERE IS A CLOSED LAND FILL A QUARTER OF A MILE AWAY AND DUE SOUTH OF THE WELLS.  THERE IS AN AUTOMOBILE JUNK YARD A LITTLE FURTHER AWAY THAT IS SOUTH WEST OF THE WELLS.  THE APPARENT GROUND WATER DIRECTION WOULD NOT LIKELY INVOLVE THESE SOURCES.  THERE IS ANOTHER YEAR AROUND RESIDENT LOCATED 300 FEET FURTHER EAST OF AMES.  HIS NAME IS KEN MATSON (924-3722).  HE HAS HAD NO COMPLAINTS ABOUT HIS WATER, BUT I THINK HIS WELL SHOULD BE SAMPLED FOR DRO AND MTBE.  AT THIS TIME (3/20/96) THE ROAD IS CLOSED BECAUSE OF MUD.  KEN HAS AGREED TO LET ME KNOW WHEN WE CAN GET DOWN THERE.

BOTH WINN AND AMES HAVE JUST RECENTLY TAKEN UP YEAR-ROUND RESIDENCE AT PUFFER POND.  THEY WONDER IF THE CONTAMINANT HAS BEEN THERE ALL ALONG AND IT IS BEING DRAWN TO THEIR WELLS BECAUSE OF THE EXTENDED DRAW ON THEM.  THEY ALSO WOULD LIKE TO KNOW IF THE LAKE IS BEING IMPACTED.

properties.DESCRIPTION:
FORMER SITE OF DANFORTH GULF. BETWEEN 1989 AND 1999, A TOTAL OF 9 USTS AND ~3200 YARDS OF CONTAMINATED SOIL WERE REMOVED FROM THE PROPERTY.  THE FORMER GULF  BUILDING DEMOLISHED 9/1999. 
 
AT THE TIME OF THE VRAP APPLICATION, MACHIAS SAVINGS BANK WAS IN THE PROCESS OF PURCHASING THE PROPERTY FROM MR. PHILLIP MORSE AND MR. PETER SHAY, AND WAS PROPOSING TO BUILD A BRANCH AT THE LOCATION.  NO FURTHER ACTION ASSURANCE LETTER ISSUED TO THE BANK ON 11/10/1999, BASED ON SOIL REMOVAL ACTIONS AND THE PLAN TO INSTALL A VAPOR BARRIER AND PASSIVE VENTING SYSTEM BENEATH THE PROPOSED SLAB-ON-GRADE BUILDING.
properties.SUMMARY:
FROM SPILL CLOSURE FORM NARRATIVE (JEAN FLANNERY):

WORK FINALLY BEGAN AT REMOVING THE UNDERGROUND TANKS AT DANFORTH GULF AFTER A LENGTHY ENFORCEMENT PROCESS UNDER THE AUSPICES OF DENISE FOURNIER.  PREVIOUS OCCURRENCES OF VAPOR PROBLEMS IN SURROUNDING BASEMENTS WERE ASSOCIATED WITH THE SLOPPY OPERATION OF THE FACILITY.  LEAKING UST'S WERE ALSO SUSPECT.  AN OLD BOX CULVERT FROM THE TURN OF THE CENTURY RUNS ADJACENT TO THE FACILITY.  THE CULVERT THEN EXTENDS DOWN MAIN STREET TO WHERE IT DISCHARGES INTO BASKAHEGAN STREAM.  SEVERAL BASEMENTS ALONG MAIN STREET DRAIN INTO THIS CULVERT.  ANY LEAKAGE AT THE FACILITY WHETHER FROM INTENTIONAL DUMPING INTO STORM DRAINS OR FROM LEAKING TANKS ENDS UP AS VAPORS IN THESE BASEMENTS.(SEE B-491-95, B-125-95).  RECOGNIZING THE HAZARD, THE DEPARTMENT MADE THE DECISION TO REMOVE THE TANKS AND CONDUCT A CLEAN UP.  DANA GRAY, OWNER OF THE FACILITY, GRANTED PERMISSION TO CONDUCT THE WORK.  WORK STARTED ON SEPTEMBER 22ND.

     SIX TANKS OF UNKNOWN AGE WERE REMOVED AS FOLLOWS: ONE 10K GASOLINE TANK, TWO 2000 GALLON GASOLINE TANKS, TWO 2000 GALLON DIESEL TANKS, AND ONE 500 GALLON KEROSENE TANK.  LEE PHELPS & SONS OF PRINCETON REMOVED THE TANKS.  DAVE BEAUMONT OF MILLINOCKET WAS THE ACTING LICENSED TANK INSTALLER.  BUB SAUNDERS OF SW COLE WAS ON SITE AS THE SITE ASSESSOR.

     A COMBINATION OF BOTH GASOLINE, DIESEL, AND KEROSENE CONTAMINATION WAS DISCOVERED WITHIN THE EXCAVATION.  A SMALL LAYER OF FREE PRODUCT WAS OBSERVED ON THE WATER TABLE AT ABOUT 4-5 FEET.  CONTAMINATION LEVELS EXCEEDED 2500 PPM.  THE ATTEMPT WAS MADE TO CLEAN THE SITE TO A LEVEL OF ABOUT 500 PPM.  THIS WAS ONLY ACHIEVED ON THE SOUTHERLY AND WESTERLY PORTIONS OF THE SITE.  THE NORTHERN PORTION OF THE SITE WAS OF GREATEST CONCERN SINCE IT WAS DOWNSLOPE AND CLOSEST TO THE BOX CULVERT.  FURTHER EXCAVATION IN THIS AREA WOULD HAVE DISRUPTED NUMEROUS UTILITIES.  THE DECISION WAS MADE TO CONDUCT A SMALL SCALE SOIL GAS SURVEY WITHIN THIS AREA TO DETERMINE IF FURTHER REMEDIATION WAS NECESSAR
FLOOR DRAIN(S) ON SITE. NO FURTHER UIC INFO AVAILABLE.

AFTER OBTAINING A WAIVER FROM THE 30 DAY WRITTEN NOTIFICATION REQUIREMENT, KEBO VALLEY GOLF CLUB BEGAN THE REMOVAL OF A 1000 GALLON GASOLINE TANK FROM THE GROUND AT THEIR MAINTENANCE FACILITY ON THE CROMWELL HARBOR ROAD IN BAR HARBOR ON 11/16/96.  G.R. ADAMS JR., INC. (BANGOR, #942-9573) WAS THE LICENSED TANK INSTALLER ON SITE FOR THE PROJECT; DOUG GOTT & SONS, INC. (SW HARBOR, #244-7461) DID THE EXCAVATION; AND S.W. COLE ENGINEERING, INC. (BANGOR, #848-5714) WAS HIRED TO DO A SITE ASSESSMENT.

     THE TANK WAS ASPHALT COATED, HAD GALVANIZED PIPING, AND WAS INSTALLED IN MAY OF 1982.  CONTAMINATION IN THE 2200 TO 3900 PPM RANGE ON A PID METER WAS ENCOUNTERED IN THE SOIL AROUND THE TANK.  THE SIDE WALLS OF THE EXCAVATION WERE A GLACIAL TILL TYPE OF MATERIAL AND GROUND WATER WAS PRESENT IN THE EXCAVATION.  I DID NOT ATTEND THE TANK REMOVAL.  DUE TO VARIOUS OTHER COMMITMENTS AT THE TIME, CLEANUP ON SITE WAS POSTPONED TO A LATER DATE.

DECEMBER 20, 1996 (FRI.):  THE EXCAVATION WAS REOPENED ON THIS DATE.  THROUGHOUT THE DAY, WE REMOVED APPROXIMATELY 208 CUBIC YARDS OF CONTAMINATED SOIL FROM THE ORIGINAL TANK HOLE, WENT SEVERAL FEET INTO THE SIDE WALLS, AND EXCAVATED UNDER THE PUMP ISLAND.  THIS MATERIAL WAS STOCKPILED ON SITE IN AN AREA BEHIND THE MAINTENANCE BUILDING AND WILL BE LAND SPREAD FOR AERATION SOMETIME IN THE SPRING OF 97.  WHEN WE FINISHED DIGGING, THE BOTTOM OF THE EXCAVATION AND ONE SIDE WALL WAS IN THE 200 TO 300 PPM RANGE ON A PID METER.  THREE OF THE SIDE WALLS STILL CONTAINED READINGS IN THE 10,000+ PPM RANGE.  ONE WALL WAS ONLY 10 FEET OR SO FROM THE MAINTENANCE BUILDING AND THE OPPOSITE WALL WAS RIGHT UP AGAINST A WOODED AREA.  A SHALLOW TEST PIT 12 FEET INTO THE TREE LINE INDICATED THAT THE CONTAMINATION HAD SPREAD DOWN SLOPE UNDERGROUND (I.E., 7 FEET BELOW THE SURFACE = 500 TO 600 PPM).

     SOME ADDITIONAL CONTAMINATED SOIL COULD HAVE BEEN REMOVED ALONG THE EDGE OF THE MAINTENANCE BUILDING AND UNDER THE PUMP ISLAND, BUT IT WOULD HAVE BEEN QUITE A PROJECT TO CLEAR CUT THE ADJACENT TREES AND REMOVE THE MATERIAL UNDER THE WOODED AREA.  I FEEL THAT THIS WOULD HAVE CAUSE MORE DAMAGE TO THE PROPERTY THAN IT WOULD BE WORTH.  OTHER THAN THE ACTUAL GOLF COURSE, THERE IS NOTHING DOWNSLOPE THAT WILL BE AFFECTED BY LEAVING THE SOIL IN PLACE.

     THE EXACT SOURCE OF THE CONTAMINATION IS UNKNOWN.  NO CORROSION HOLES WERE OBSERVED IN THE TANK AND SOME OF THE HIGHER PID READINGS WERE FOUND IN THE AREA OF THE PUMP ISLAND.  WHETHER THE PUMP OR PIPING LEAKED PERIODICALLY OVER THE YEARS IS ANYONE'S GUESS.  THIS PARTICULAR TANK WAS USE TO GAS UP GOLF CARTS, LAWN MOWERS, AND ASSORTED OTHER MAINTENANCE EQUIPMENT ON THE PROPERTY.  CONSEQUENTLY, THEY ONLY KEPT TRACK OF THE DELIVERY THAT WERE MADE.

     INITIALLY, WHEN THE CLEANUP GUIDELINES WERE BEING DISCUSSED FOR THIS SITE, I THOUGHT THAT IT WOULD PROBABLE COME UNDER THE B2 STANDARDS, BUT DUE TO THE POTENTIAL FOR A CONFINED SPACE EXPLOSION HAZARD, IT WAS UPGRADED TO THE INTERMEDIATE STANDARD.  HOWEVER, DUE TO THE ASSORTED PROBLEMS MENTIONED ABOVE, INCLUDING A LIMITED STOCKPILE AREA, THE CLEANUP ON SITE WAS LESS THAN IDEAL...IT ENDED UP BEING CLOSER TO THE B2 STANDARD.

     OTHER THEN SPREADING AND TENDING THE 208 CUBIC YARDS OF CONTAMINATED SOIL IN THE SPRING OF 97, I DO NOT ANTICIPATE ANY ADDITIONAL CLEANUP BEING DONE ON SITE.

DISHCARGE POINT IS SEALED
SURVEY:  MAY 2002

ON JUNE 4, 1996 PAT SEAWARD OF THE DIVISION OF TECHNICAL SERVICES RELAYED TO JON WOODARD A REPORT SHE HAD RECEIVED FROM ED YOUNG OF WATER TREATMENT SYSTEMS OF A CONTAMINATED WELL ON BAILEY ISLAND.  MR. YOUNG HAD SMELLED A PETROLEUM ODOR IN THE IRON REMOVAL FILTERS AT A RESIDENCE OWNED BY ANN CHAPLAIN, AND RENTED OUT DURING THE SUMMER. THE PROPERTY MANAGER, BECKY-SUE BETTS OF "YOUR ISLAND CONNECTION", WAS CONTACTED AND MET WITH ON SITE TO TAKE A CONFIRMATORY SAMPLE.  THE WATER WAS SAMPLED FOR BOTH DIESEL RANGE ORGANICS (DRO) AND GASOLINE RANGE ORGANICS (GRO).  THE SITE TESTED POSITIVE FOR GRO AND IT WASI ARRANGED TO HAVE A FILTER INSTALLED.  JOHN DUNLAP AND JON WOODARD RETURNED SEVERAL WEEKS LATER, RE-SAMPLED THE WELL AND SAMPLED SEVERAL OTHERS IN THE AREA.  TWO ADDITIONAL RESIDENCES TESTED POSITIVE FOR GRO AT THAT TIME.  SEVERAL CONVERSATIONS WITH THE LOCAL RESIDENCES AND REVEALED THAT THERE WERE 3 KNOWN FORMER GASOLINE FACILTIES; TWO WITH UNDERGROUND TANKS AND ONE WITH ABOVE GROUND TANKS.  ALL FACILITIES HAD BEEN ABANDONED AND THE TANKS REMOVED A SUBSTANTIAL NUMBER OF YEARS AGO.  

AS THERE WAS NO IDENTIFIED SOURCE FOR THE CONTAMINATION, AND THE THREE BEDROCK WELLS HAVE TESTED POSITIVE FOR PETROLEUM CONTAMINATION WITH 3-5 AT RISK, THE CASE WAS REFERRED TO PAT SEAWARD OF THE DIVISION OF TECHNICAL SERVICES.   PAT LATER IDENTIFIED THE SOURCE AS AN HISTORICAL ABOVE GROUND KEROSENE SPILL.

properties.DESCRIPTION: FORMERLY THE BOAT SCHOOL
properties.SUMMARY:
FORMERLY THE BOAT SCHOOL

 ON 12/11/96 MS. WREN CALLED TO REPORT THAT A NEWLY INSTALLED UST AT THEIR EASTPORT FACILITY HAD LEAKED OIL. THE SCHOOL HAD BECOME AWARE OF A PROBLEM ON 12/3/96 WHEN THE SCHOOL'S HEAD OF MTCE, GARY RAMSDELL, ATTEMPTED TO STICK THE TANK TO DETERMINE THE AMOUNT OF FUEL IN THE TANK AND FOUND BOTH OIL AND WATER IN THE TANK EXCAVATION AS WELL AS THE FILL SPILL BOX. HE REPORTED THIS BACK UP THE LINE OF COMMAND TO MS. WREN, MS. WREN REPORTS THAT SHE CONTACTED BOTH THE INSTALLER, G.R.ADAMS INC., AND THE ENGINEERING FIRM, WOODARD AND CURRAN, AND WAS TOLD THAT IF THE ME. D.E.P. NEEDED TO BE NOTIFIED THAT THESE FIRMS WOULD HANDLE IT. FOR A MORE CONCISE CHRONOLOGY OF TIME AND PERSONS NOTIFIED, PLEASE READ THE ATTACHED NOTES OF MS. WREN AND MR. TOM DUYME, A W.C.T.C. DIV. HEAD.
   ON 12/12/96 I DROVE TO EASTPORT AND INSPECTED THE SPILL SITE. I SAW THAT THE PEA STONE BACKFILL AROUND THE NEW FIBERGLASS TANK WAS FULL OF WATER AND HELD A FLOATING LAYER OF FUEL OIL. I ESTIMATE THAT THE SIZE OF THE EXCAVATION WAS ABOUT 30X20 FEET. MR. RAMSDELL SAID THAT THE SOIL AROUND THE TANK WAS A HARD CLAY. THIS WAS BORN OUT BY THE FACT THAT EVEN AFTER 8 PLUS DAYS NO OIL HAD BROKEN OUT DOWN GRADIENT OF THE TANK EXCAVATION INTO AN INTERMITTENT STREAM THAT DRAINS INTO DEEP COVE. MR. RAMSDELL SHOWED ME WHERE THE LEAK APPEARS TO HAVE OCCURRED. THIS WAS AT THE FILL PIPE AND, MORE SPECIFICALLY, IT WAS BELIEVED THAT THE RUBBER GASKETED FILL CAP HAD NOT BEEN TIGHTLY SEALED. DUE TO THE TIGHT CLAY OF THE EXCAVATION, THE DECEMBER RAINS FILLED THE HOLE LIKE A BATH TUB AND OVERFLOWED INTO THE TANK FORCING OUT AN UNKNOWN AMOUNT OF OIL. THE NEXT DAY JOHN MULLINS, A LICENSED TANK INSTALLER FOR G.R.ADAMS,INC. PUMPED WATER FROM THE TANK AND INSTALLED A FOUR INCH DIAMETER PIPE INSIDE THE SPILL BOX TO ACT AS A RISER PLACING THE FILL COVER ABOVE THE STANDING WATER IN THE HOLE. MR. RAMSDELL HAS CONTINUED TO MONITOR THE TANK FOR A INFLUX OF WATER AND NONE HAS OCCURRED SINCE THE RISER WAS INS
LUST SITE: ALSO WAS AN ABOVE GROUND STORAGE TANK ON SITE. AS OF 2008 THE LOCATION APPEARED TO BE OUT OF BUSINESS

AFTER OBTAINING A WAIVER FROM DEP'S 30-DAY WRITTEN NOTIFICATION REQUIREMENT, G.R. ADAMS JR., INC. (BANGOR; #942-9573), A LICENSED TANK INSTALLER, BEGAN THE REMOVAL OF THREE UNDERGROUND TANKS AT THE AMHERST GENERAL STORE ON ROUTE #9 IN AMHERST ON 5/22/95.  ARNOLD A. FESSENDEN, C.G. (BANGOR; #947-3184) WAS HIRED TO DO THE SITE ASSESSMENT FOR THIS PROJECT AND JORDAN CONSTRUCTION (AMHERST) DID THE EXCAVATION.  THE TANKS INCLUDED: ONE 2000 GALLON SUPER UNLEADED, ONE 3000 GALLON REGULAR UNLEADED, AND ONE 4000 GALLON DIESEL.  ALL OF THE TANKS WERE ASPHALT COATED, HAD GALVANIZED PIPING, AND WERE BACKFILLED WITH SAND.  THEY HAD BEEN INSTALLED IN 1984.  ALTHOUGH NO CORROSION HOLES WERE OBSERVED IN ANY OF THE TANKS OR PROBLEMS FOUND WITH THE PIPING, VARIOUS LEVELS OF CONTAMINATION, UP TO AROUND 2500 PPM ON A PID METER, WERE UNCOVERED AROUND THE FILL PIPES, TANKS, AND PUMP ISLAND.

MAY 23, 1995 (TUES.):  AT 0800 ON THIS DATE, MR. FESSENDEN CALLED OUR OFFICE TO INFORM ME OF THE SITUATION.  IT WAS INDICATED THAT CONTAMINATED SOIL HAD BEEN FOUND DURING THE REMOVAL; WHAT SOME OF THE PID READINGS WERE AROUND THE SITE; AND THAT THERE WAS A WELL APPROXIMATELY 120 FEET AWAY.  A FEW TRUCK LOADS OF SOIL HAD BEEN REMOVED FROM THE GROUND AND WERE STOCKPILED NEARBY.  HE WAS NOW INQUIRING IF THEY COULD BACKFILL THE HOLE OR IF DEP WANTED TO CHECK THE SITE FIRST?

	I THEN PROCEEDED TO AMHERST TO MEET WITH THE CONTRACTORS INVOLVED AND MONITOR THE EXCAVATION.  SINCE THE SURROUNDING AREA IS ON WELL WATER, THIS FACILITY WOULD FALL UNDER DEP'S STRINGENT CLEANUP GUIDELINES.  A LAND SPREADING SITE FOR THE CONTAMINATED SOIL WAS LOCATED ON MR. JORDAN'S PROPERTY IN AURORA.

	EXCAVATION ON SITE RESUMED.  THE SURROUNDING SOIL APPEARED TO BE A TILL TYPE OF MATERIAL AND LEDGE OR BEDROCK WAS FOUND AT AROUND 18 FEET BELOW THE SURFACE.  CONTAMINATION ON THE LEDGE WAS IN THE 700 PPM RANGE ON A PID METER.  SOME GROUND WATER WAS OBSERVED IN THE HOLE, BUT IT CONTAINED VERY LITTLE SHEEN.

properties.DESCRIPTION: PUBLIC WELL FORMERLY IN SERVICE TO "THE ACADEMY" (NOW TORN DOWN AND POSSIBLY STILL IN SEERVICE TO THE LITTLE LEAGUE BALL FIELD. POSSIBLY ALSO DISCONTINUED.
properties.SUMMARY:
ON 11/15, IT WAS REPORTED THAT THE MORSE PATTEN IRVING FUEL TANKS (ACROSS THE STREETFROM THE PUBLIC WATER SUPPLY WELL,  FORMERLY IN SERVICE TO "THE ACADEMY" AND NOW POSSIBLY SERVICING THE LITTLE LEAGUE FIELD,  WERE REMOVED ON 11/13/04.

I VISITED THE SITE 11/15 AND FOUND (4) UNDERGROUND TANKS SETTING ON THE GROUND BEHIND THE FORMER GAS STATION AND FRESH, TAMPED GRAVEL WHERE THE TANKS USED TO BE BURIED.

MR. MORSE MEET ME ON SITE, AND WE DISCUSSED WHAT NEEDED TO BE DONE, AS THE TANKS WERE REMOVED WITHOUT COMPLETING ANY OF THE PAPERWORK.  ALSO, HE DID NOT HAVE A CERTIFIED TANK INSTALLER OR A SITE ASSESSOR PRESENT.

MR. MORSE STATED HE GOT SOME FRIENDS WITH EQUIPMENT TO COME BY ON SATURDAY AND HELP HIM REMOVE THE TANKS.

MR. MORSE STATES HE HAS NO MONEY, BUT I CONVINCED HIM TO GET HIS FRIEND BACK WITH THE BACK HOE TO REMOVE THE PUMP ISLAND AND DIG TEST PITS UNDER THE PUMP ISLAND AND ANOTHER WHERE THE TANKS USED TO SIT. I ALSO ADVISED HE SHOULD NOTIFY THE TOWN FIRE DEPARTMENT AND MARK AND BARRICADE THE TANKS TO PREVENT A EXPLOSION OR FIRE.

TANKS WERE IN EXCELLENT CONDITION (STP-3/ANODES). THE ANODES WERE IN ALMOST NEW CONDITION.
THE TANKS HAD NO SIGNS OF ANY OIL STAINING.

IF CLEAN-UP NEEDS TO BE DONE AFTER TEST PITTING, THE SITE IS CONSIDERED A STRINGENT CLEAN-UP DUE TO A PUBLIC WELL THAT SHOWS UP ON THE GIS MAPS ABOUT 500 FEET AWAY TO THE EAST.

11/18/04

I WAS BACK ON THE SITE YESTERDAY (11/17) AFTER A CALL FROM MR. MORSE. 

THEY HAD COMPLETED WHAT I HAD REQUESTED.

THE PUMP ISLAND WAS REMOVED AND TWO TEST PITS HAD BEEN DUG.

THE TEST PIT UNDER THE NW CORNER OF THE TANK FIELD APPEARS CLEAN (22 PPM PID, SANDY SOIL, NO ODOR).  THE TEST PIT UNDER THE PUMP ISLAND HAD OLD CONTAMINATION THAT IS WELL ON ITS WAY TO BEING REMEDIATED BY MOTHER NATURE. 

THE TOP TWO FEET WERE CLEAN, THEN A CLEAN 4-6 INCH LAYER OF OLD VEGETATION, AND THE NEXT 18" THICK LAYER  WAS ON AVERAGE, CONTAMINATED AT  028 PPM PER PID (MOTTLED GREY TILL, COLOR SLIGHT VARNISH ODOR), THE REMAINING 2 FEET APPEARS CLEAN AT 65 PPM PER PID (LIGHT GREY TO BROWN TILL, NO ODOR).

THE SITE COMES IN AS STRINGENT DUE TO A WELL ACROSS THE STREET THAT ONCE FEED "THE ACADEMY" (THE FORMER LOCAL PRIVATE SCHOOL(?)). THE BUILDING HAS BEEN DEMOLISHED. IN A QUICK WALK AROUND YESTERDAY, THE WELL OR WELL HOUSE WASN'T OBVIOUS.  THE LOCAL NEIGHBORS REMEMBER THE WELL BUT NO ONE CAN REMEMBER IF IT IS STILL BEING USED.  ACCORDING TO ONE GENTLEMAN, IT MAY BE THE WELL THAT FEED THE LITTLE LEAGUE BALL FIELD, BUT HE WASN'T SURE.

I'M NOT CONCERNED ABOUT THE WELL AT LEAST FROM THIS CONTAMINATION, BECAUSE THE CONTAMINATION WOULD HAVE HAD REACHED IT LONG AGO. THERE IS NO EMERGENCY CLEAN-UP REQUIRED HERE.

MR. MORSE HAS PLEADED POVERTY AND HAS NO MONEY TO CONDUCT A SITE ASSESSMENT NOR DO A CLEAN-UP.

ON 6/14/89, GORDON CHEESMAN SAMPLED HIS WELL BECAUSE IT SMELLED AND TASTED LIKE #2 HEATING OIL. NORTHEAST LAB CONDUCTED A HYDROCARBON SCREEN AND DETECTED FUEL OIL AT 1800PPB. MR. CHEESMAN REPORTED THE RESULTS TO DENNY PHILLIPS.  ON 6/30/89 DENNIS RETESTED THE WATER IN THE CHEESMAN WELL. THE TANK WAS SITUATED DIRECTLY ON LEDGE AND THE ORIENTATION OF THE FRACTURES WERE NOTED TO BE DIPPING TOWARD THE WELL. DEP ANAYSIS  SHOWED FUEL OIL AT 990PPB. FILTERS WERE INSTALLED AT THE RESIDENCE IN AUGUST, 1989. A THIRD PARTY DAMAGE CLAIM WAS FILED IN FEBRUARY, 1990.  THE LINE TO THE HEATING OIL TANK HAD BEEN LEAKING FOR SOME TIME.  THE TANK AND CONNECTIONS WERE REPLACED. SAMPLING THROUGHOUT THE NEIGHBORHOOD SHOWS NO OTHER CONTAMINATED WELLS.

ON 10/7/97, 0830 HOURS ARNIE FESSENDEN OF FGES REPORTED THAT THERE WAS CONSIDERABLE GASOLINE CONTAMINATION AT THE TANK REMOVAL TAKING PLACE AT DAGGARTS STORE IN TOPSFIELD.  ON SITE I MET BOB GORDON, WHO IN ADDITION TO BEING THE REQUIRED TANK INSTALLER WAS REPRESENTING J.D. THOMAS.  IT TURNED OUT THAT THE DAGGART USTS BELONGED TO J.D. THOMAS.  WHEN IT BECAME APPARENT THAT WE WERE FACING AN EXTENSIVE CLEAN UP, J.D. THOMAS OPTED FOR DEP TO PAY UP FRONT.

THE FGES PID WAS BEING PEGGED AT 2500 PPM IN OPEN AIR FOR MOST OF THE DIG.  I DID A BAG HEAD SPACE ON SUCH SAMPLES AND GOT READINGS OF OVER 5000 PPM.  THERE WERE A COUPLE OF ABANDONED DUG WELLS ACROSS THE ROAD THAT HAD BECOME SLIGHTLY UP GRADIENT WHILE THE OTHER WAS AROUND 1000 FT AWAY AND SLIGHTLY DOWN GRADIENT.  THE WELL THAT IS CURRENTLY AT RISK BELONGS TO DAGGARTS STORE.  FGES HAS AGREED TO SAMPLE THIS WELL.  THE SOIL WAS SILTY TILL DOWN TO 22 FT WHERE IT BECAME CLAY.  WATER STARTED TO COME INTO THE HOLE AT THIS DEPTH.  THE READINGS BECAME <30 PPM AT 22 FT.  HOWEVER, THE TOTAL AMOUNT OF SOIL REMOVED WAS 3000 YDS.  THERE WERE LATERAL BARRIERS PREVENTING A COMPLETE, STRINGENT CLEAN UP. THE ROAD WAS ON ONE SIDE, A BUILDING ON TWO SIDES AND A WET SWAMP ON ANOTHER ASPECT OF THE HOLE.  GETTING TO CLOSE TO THE SWAMP MIGHT HAVE WASHED CONTAMINATED WATER OFF THE PROPERTY.  THE PROJECT HAS BEEN HANDED OVER TO TECH SERVICES.

AN INTERESTING FEATURE OF THIS DIG WAS THAT THE GROUND WATER LEVELS IN THE ABANDONED DUG WELLS MENTIONED ABOVE WAS ABOUT 5 FT FROM GRADE. YET THE TANK HOLE DIG DIDN'T HAVE WATER UNTIL IT HIT A DEPTH OF 20+ FT. POSSIBLY HAS TO DO WITH LOW HYDRAULIC CONDUCTIVITY.

ON 1/15/96 A PIECE OF ICE FELL FROM THE ROOF AND BROKE THE NIPPLE THAT IS BETWEEN THE TANK AND FILTER.  ALL THE OIL INSIDE THE TANK SPILLED ON TO THE GROUND.  ON 5/13/96 GLEN WALL WENT TO THE SIMMONS RESIDENCE TO DO A SUBSURFACE INVESTIGATION.  THE RESULTS SHOWED A DEFINITE CONTRAST IN CONTAMINENT LEVELS BEWEEN SOIL OUTSIDE OF THE FIELD AND PROXIMAL TO THE SPILL AND SOIL WITHIN OR AT THE DOWN GRADIENT BOUNDARIES OF THE FIELD.

ON 10/1/98, 1125 HOURS, BRUCE BOWMAN REPORTED THAT THEY HAD THEIR WATER ANALYZED IN 1997 AND FOUND THAT THEY HAD GASOLINE CONTAMINATION IN THE WELL OF HIS MOTHER-IN-LAW'S HOUSE.  THAT ANALYSIS RESULT WAS 283 PPB GRO AND MTBE NOT CONFIRMED.  OUR RETEST CAME BACK AT 93 PPB GRO AND 22 PPB MTBE.

THE MOTHER-IN-LAW (MRS. MAMIE BUTTERFIELD) IS CURRENTLY LIVING WITH THE BOWMAN'S BECAUSE SHE SUFFERED A STROKE.  THEREFORE, THE HOUSE IS NOT BEING LIVED IN, BUT IT IS UP FOR SALE.  I HAVE ASSURED THE BOWMAN'S THAT THE DWELLING IS ELIGIBLE FOR CHARCOAL FILTERS AND THAT SUCH FILTRATION (ACCOMPANIED BY QM) WOULD REMOVE THE GRO CONTAMINATION.  ALTERNATIVELY, THE HOUSE COULD BE SUPPLIED BY AN EXISTING WELL (SEE BELOW).

ALTHOUGH I HAVE LABELED THIS INVESTIGATION AS A MYSTERY, THERE IS REASONABLE CHANCE THAT THE CONTAMINATION IS COMING FROM A NOW ABANDONED CN BROWN STATION THAT IS ABOUT 500 FEET FROM THE BUTTERFIELD RESIDENCE.  THEY (CN BROWN) HAD A UST LINE LEAK A WHILE AGO AND SIX FAMILIES WERE PUT ON A REPLACEMENT WELL.  HOWEVER, THERE HAVE BEEN OTHER GASOLINE CONTAINING USTS IN THE AREA SO IT IS SAFER TO CALL IT A MYSTERY.  MR. BERRY (PINE STATE DRILLING) SAID THE WELL WAS 600 FEET NORTH OF THE CN BROWN STATION.  HE ALSO STATED THAT STUDIES HAD INDICATED THAT THE PLUME WAS TRAVELING SOUTH.  MRS. BOWMAN IS GOING TO TALK TO MR. BERRY ABOUT THE POSSIBILITY OF HOOKING HER MOTHER'S HOUSE UP TO THAT WELL.

ON 10-6-95, 1050 HOURS WILLIE WATSON OF WEBBER OIL CALLED TO REPORT AN AST SPILL AT PRAY'S MOBIL HOME PARK (LOT 11) OFF FINSON ROAD.  THE TANK-A 275 AST-HAD BEEN MOUNTED ON PIECES OF WOOD AND IT TIPPED OVER.  THE DISCHARGE CAME FROM THE FILL CAP.  WEBBER PERSONEL ESTIMATED THE SPILL AT ABOUT 20 GALLONS.     THE WEBBER CREW WERE ABLE TO SOAK UP 4 GALLONS WITH SORBENT PADS.  BECAUSE THERE WAS A WELL WITHIN 30 YARDS OF THE SPILL WE (PAUL PRAY AND MYSELF) REMOVED 8 YD3 OF MILDLY CONTAMINATED SOIL.  (THE WELL IS 120 FEET DEEP WITH 25 FEET OF CASING.) THE DIG  GOT INTO SOLID CLAY AT ABOUT ONE AND A HALF FEET DOWN.  HOWEVER THE CLAY WAS DRY BECAUSE OF THE PROLONGED DROUGHT THAT WE HAD BEEN HAVING.  CONSEQUENTLY, WE WERE GETTING PID READINGS OF ARROUND 1000 PPM AT ALL EXTREMITIES OF THE DIG.  WE COULDN'T GO ANY DEEPER BECAUSE OF A WATER LINE.  THE MOBILE UNIT AND THE ROAD LIMITED THE DIG LATERALLY.  PRODUCT MIGRATION MUST HAVE BEEN MUCH FASTER THAN ONE WOULD PREDICT THROUGH SUCH A POROUS MEDIUM (I.E. ONE THAT IS GENERALLY ASSOCIATED WITH A LOW HYDRAULIC CONDUCTIVITY).  HAD IT BEEN SATURATED WITH WATER THE MIGRATION WOULD HAVE TERMINATED AT THE WET LAYER.  THIS CASE HAS BEEN REFERED TO TECH SERVICE.  IT WOULD BE NICE TO KNOW THE DEPTH AND DIRECTION OF THE GROUND WATER TABLE.  MEANWHILE THE ABOVE MENTIONED HOLE, WHICH WAS 2 X 3 X1.25 YD WAS FILLED WITH COMPACTED, CLEAN CLAY TO PREVENT RECHARGE FROM THE SPILL AREA.  

WHEN I ASKED PAUL BLOOD IF HE COULD DETERMINE THE DEPTH AND DIRECTION OF THE OVERBURDEN GROUND WATER TABLE, HE INDICATED THAT IT WOULD PROBABLY REQUIRE A DRILLER AND THE THIS MIGHT COST  AROUND $2000.  LATER I WAS DISCUSSING THE PROCEDURE WITH PAUL PRAY.  MR PRAY SAID THAT HE COULD DRILL A NEW WELL FOR LESS THAN THAT.  HE WAS CERTAIN OF THIS BECAUSE HE HAD DRILL A COUPLE RECENTLY.  PAUL SUGGESTED THAT HE MAY WANT TO DIG FURTHER.  THIS WOULD MEAN MOVING THE MOBILE HOME AND DISRUPTING THE PARKING LOT.  THE ESTIMATE FOR THIS IS ARROUND $15,000.  THE CONVERSATION CAME BACK TO THE COST OF REPLACING THE WELL.  PAUL WILL GET THE FUND APPLICATION TO THE TANK OWNER, DONNA RIZZO, AND HE PLANS ON DOING SOME GEOPROBING-A RELATIVELY INEXPENSIVE PROCEDURE IF WE DO IT OURSELVES.  PAUL'S RESERVATION ABOUT THIS IS THAT IT DOESN'T ALWAYS WORK.  WE SOMETIMES FIND THAT WE CAN'T GET THE POINTS DOWN FAR ENOUGH.

THE EFFORTS TO DATE HAVE BEEN PROVIDED BY PAUL PRAY HIMSELF.  HE HAS A BACK HOE, TRUCK AND A PLACE ON SITE TO TREAT THE CONTAMINATED SOIL.  AS OF NOW, I DON'T THINK PAUL PRAY PLANS ON COLLECTING ANY MONEY FOR HIS EFFORTS.  THE SOIL THAT WE REMOVED WAS GIVING PID HEAD SPACE READINGS (SET POINT 225) OF 1000-1100 PPM.  THE "SHAKING WITH WATER" TEST REVEALED A SLIGHT, MOMENTARY SHEEN.  IT IS POSSIBLE THAT THERE WAS AS MUCH AS A GALLON OF PRODUCT PER YD3.  IT WAS A LONG WAYS FROM BEING SATURATED, THOUGH.

THE SITE IS CURRENTLY VACANT.  THE SITE HAD ASTS CONTAINING K-1 #2 FUEL OIL AND DIESEL MOTOR FUEL.  THE AST FACILITY WAS REMOVED FROM THE SITE IN 1992.  DURING EARTH WORK ON THE SITE NON-AQUEOUS PHASE LIQUID WAS OBSERVED ON THE WATER TABLE.  MDEP WAS NOTIFIED.
SOIL PILE BIO REMEDIATED ON SITE BY EMERY AND GARRETT IN EARLY TO MID 1990'S. LATER USED AS FILL. SEE FILE ORANGE FOR BETHEL FOR RED TOP DINER (NOW BIG APPLE).

APPROXIMATELY 150 GALLONS OF KEROSENE WAS SPILLED WHEN SNOW FELL OFF THE ROOF OF THE HOUSE AND BROKE THE FUEL FILTER OFF HER OUTSIDE OIL TANK.

THE DUNFEES HADN'T LIVED IN THEIR HOUSE VERY LONG BEFORE IT CAUGHT FIRE AND BURNED TO THE GROUND.  ANOTHER ONE WAS BUILT IN ITS' PLACE, SET BACK FARTHER FROM THE ROAD, AND USING THE SAME WELL.  THEY'D ONLY OCCUPIED THE NEW HOUSE FOR 10 MONTHS WHEN THE DUNFEES BEGAN TO NOTICE A TASTE OF PETROLEUM IN THE WELL WATER; CONSULTING WITH NORLEN'S WATER TREATMENT, DUNFEE WAS ADVISED TO HAVE THE WATER TESTED. RESULTS, ATTACHED, SHOWED 31 PPB GRO.  (MY OWN SAMPLING SHOWED THE CONTAMINANT TO BE DRO, AT 230 PPB.)

ACCORDING TO MR. DUNFEE, THE PLACE, YEARS AGO, HAD BEEN A WORKING FARM.  WHEN THEY MOVED INTO THE OLD HOUSE, THERE WAS AN OLD PUMP LYING NEXT TO AN ABOVE GROUND TANK BEHIND THE HOUSE.  HE SAID THE TANK WAS EMPTY, AND HE DIDN'T KNOW IF IT'D CONTAINED GASOLINE OR DIESEL, OR EVEN IF IT'D BEEN BURIED OR ITS' ORIGINAL LOCATION ON THE PROPERTY. HE DID SAY THAT A LOT OF FILL HAD BEEN HAULED ONTO THE LOT DURING LANDSCAPING, AND THAT THE NEW HOUSE'S LOCATION REQUIRED THAT THE WATER LINE BE EXTENDED.  MY GUESS IS THAT EITHER THERE WAS A SMALL LEAK FROM THE EARTH MOVING EQUIPMENT, AND IT FUEL GOT INTO THE WELL, OR CONTAMINTED SOIL WAS ENCOUNTERED AND THE CONTAMINATION FOLLOWED THE WATER LINE BACK TO THE WELL.

ON MAY 24, 1995 WE RECEIVED A CALL FROM MR. RICHARD REIGER OF BELLINGHAM, MA. REPORTING AN OIL SPILL AT HIS CAMP ON THE BOAT LANDING ROAD IN EMBDEN. THE PREVIOUS DAY A NEIGHBOR'S DAUGHTER WAS PLAYING AROUND THE CAMP'S KEROSENE TANK AND BROKE OFF THE TANK'S FEED LINE.  THE PRODUCT FLOWED ONTO THE GROUND UNDER THE CAMP.  EMBDEN HAS PUBLIC WATER PIPED TO THE HOMES AND CAMPS IN THE AREA BUT THIS IS DELIVERED VIA AN ABOVE GROUND PIPE WHICH IS SHUT OFF IN LATE AUTUMN.  ONE OF MR. RIEGER'S NEIGHBORS IS A YEAR ROUND RESIDENT AND JUST DRILLED A WELL WHICH IS 585 FEET DEEP AND 64 FEET UNTIL LEDGE. THIS WELL, OWNED BY MR. & MRS. BILL PRETCSHLER, (566-5762) IS ABOUT 50 YARDS FROM THE SPILL.

I VISITED THE SITE ON THE 24TH AND FOUND THE SITUATION PRETTY MUCH AS MR. RIEGER HAD DESCRIBED.  I ALSO MET MRS. LINDA SMITH (566-0081) WHO ADMITTED THAT HER DAUGHTER BROKE THE FEED LINE.  SOMEONE HAD PLUGGED THE HOLE WITH A STICK AND THE TANK REGISTERED 1/3 FULL.  MR. RIEGER SAID THE TANK WAS THREE QUARTERS FULL WHEN HE WAS LAST AT THE CAMP.  SUBTRACTING FOR KEROSENE USED BEFORE THE SPILL, I ROUGHLY ESTIMATED THAT 75 TO 100 GALLONS WAS LOST.

I INSTRUCTED MR. RIEGER TO EXCAVATE THE CONTAMINATED SOIL AND WE MADE ARRANGEMENTS WITH WASTE MANAGEMENT IN NORRIDGEWOCK FOR FINAL DISPOSAL. THIS WORK WAS DONE OVER THE WEEKEND AND MR. ROGER FILLED SEVEN DRUMS OF SOIL AND ONE DRUM OF LEAVES, STICKS, ETC.

I VISITED THE SITE MAY 31 AND MET MR. PRETCSHLER AND MR. RICHARD BARTLETT WHO IS AN INSURANCE ADJUSTER FOR MR. RIEGER.  THERE WAS STILL A FAINT SMELL IN SOME OF THE CONTAMINATED AREA BUT THE HIGH WATER TABLE MADE ANY FURTHER EXCAVATION IMPRACTICAL.  I LATER TOLD MR. RIEGER TO SPREAD A HIGH NITROGEN FERTILIZER ON THE AREA AND OVERTURN THE SOIL AFTER FOUR TO SIX WEEKS.  THIS WILL AID AND HASTEN BIOREMDIATION OF THE REMAINING SOIL.  THE AREA WILL REMAIN OPEN UNTIL SEPTEMBER.

SINCE MR. PRETCSHLER WILL NOT USE HIS NEW WELL UNTIL LATE FALL, I'LL WAIT UNTIL THEN FOR A SAMPLE ANALYSIS.  DUE TO THE WELLS DEPTH, SEAL AROUND BEDROCK AND NON-USE UNTIL THE LATE FALL, I FEEL THE ODDS ARE GOOD THAT THE WELL WILL REMAIN CLEAN.  HOWEVER, I WILL SAMPLE AS A PRECAUTION.

ALSO KNOWN AS DICK'S MINI MART

THE KEROSENE CONTAMINATION APPEARED SUDDENLY IN MAY 1987, DISCOVERED BY MRS. GREGORY'S PLUMBER, MIKE MCMANN, WHEN HE CAME TO TURN ON THE WATER FOR THE SEASON.  SOON AFTER HE DUG DOWN TO THE WELL CAP TO SEE WHAT WAS WRONG AND CONTACTED PERRY COGBURN OF THE DEP.  THEY DISCOVERED PURE KEROSENE PRODUCT ON THE WATER TABLE, DISSOLVED PRODUCT IN THE WATER, & OIL-SOAKED SOIL SURROUNDING THE WELL CAP.  THE DUG WELL ON THE PROPERTY IS NOT POTABLE WATER.  THE WELL CAP HAD A CRACK THROUGH THE MIDDLE AND WAS VULNERABLE TO CONTAMINATION.  A TWO-CUBIC FOOT, ONE CYLINDER CARBON FILTER UNIT WAS INSTALLED BY WATER TREATMENT SYSTEMS IN LATE JULY, 1987.

BROWN HAD OVERFILLED HER TANK.  MS. GARCIA CALLED IN THE SPILL AND BILLWALLACE OF DEP RESPONSE IN AUGUSTA.  BILL WALLACE ARRIVED W/MS. GARCIA ON 11/7/96.  BILL FOUND THAT THETANK WAS UNDER DAWN'S TRAILER AND IT HAD A NUMBER OF DEFICIENCIES, SUCH AS VISE GRIP PLIERS HOLDING OPEN THE FINEMATIC VALVE, ONE SIDE OF THE TANK W/NO STEEL LEGS HELD UP BY WOODEN CRIBBING, AND AN AUTO JACK HOLDING UP THE REST OF THE TANK. CHRIS SWAIN (287-2651 OF THE MAINE DEP IN AUGUSTA), PHONED TO INFORM ME OF A LOCATION ON CRANBERRY ISLES THAT HAS A DRINKING WATER WELL CONTAMINATED WITH THE GASOLINE ADDITIVE MTBE.  HE SAID THAT THE RESIDENCE OF FREDRICK MOSS ON CRANBERRY ISLES IS REPORTED TO HAVE CONSIDERABLE CONTAMINATION FROM THE ADDITIVE.  I MADE ARRANGEMENTS TO GET TO CRANBERRY ISLES TO SAMPLE THE MOSS'S DRINKING WATER WELL.  ARRANGEMENTS WERE MADE FOR A SEPTEMBER 1ST SAMPLING OF THE WELL FOR MTBE.

TUESDAY SEPTEMBER 1, 1998			MORNING

I TOOK THE MORNING MAIL BOAT TO CRANBERRY ISLES.  WHEN I ARRIVED I WALKED TO THE MOSS RESIDENCE.  I KNOCKED ON THE FRONT DOOR, THEN I TRIED THE BACK DOOR.  THE HOUSE APPEARED TO HAVE BEEN LEFT OPEN.  I WALKED AROUND THE HOUSE AND FOUND AN OUTDOOR WATER FAUCET.  I LET THE WATER RUN AND I TOOK THE WATER SAMPLES.  THE WATER SAMPLES WERE TAKEN TO NORTHEAST LABS IN WINSLOW.  THE WATER SAMPLE WAS ANALYZED THE FOLLOWING DAY.  THE SAMPLE RESULTS INDICATED A CONCENTRATION OF 190 PPB OF MTBE IN THE DRINKING WATER.  THE RESULTS WERE REPORTED TO AUGUSTA.

ON MONDAY SEPTEMBER 21ST  A NORLEN'S WATER FILTRATION SYSTEM WAS INSTALLED IN THE BASEMENT OF THE MOSS RESIDENCE.
ON TUESDAY SEPTEMBER 22ND CHRIS SWAIN AND I WENT TO CRANBERRY ISLES TO RESAMPLE THE MOSS WELL AND CONDUCT FURTHER INVESTIGATIONS.  THIS TIME THE RESULTS CAME BACK AT 140 PPB OF MTBE.  

WE WALKED AROUND THE ISLAND AND SAMPLED AN AREA WHERE THERE USED TO BE OLD TANKS FROM A BULK PLANT.  THE NEARBY WELL, NEAR THE OLD BULK PLANT, DID NOT INDICATE CONTAMINATION OR ANY MTBE.

COMMUNITY ENERGY REPORTED AN OIL SPILL OF 100 GAL OF KEROSENE THAT HAD BEEN DELIVERED TO THE TRAILER OWNED BY STEWART TURNER.  HIS MOTHER,JUNE TURNER, NOTICED STRONG OIL VAPORS LATER THAT DAY.SNOW AND ICE HAD FALLEN OFF THE ROOF AND BROKEN THE FILTER OFF THE OUTSIDE TANK. GLEN WALL INVESTIGATED THE DAMAGE IN THE LATE AFTERNOON AND COMMUNITY ENERGY MADE REPAIRS AND PUT 50 GAL OF OIL TO KEEP THE TRAILER FROM FREEZING. STEWART AND GLEN WALL DECIDED TO CLEAN UP THE SPILL WITH A VAC TRUCK, BUT IT DID NOT WORK.  APPROXIMATELY 12X14 AREA UNDER THE TRAILER WAS OIL STAINED. ON 2/9/98, PLACED PINE SHAVINGS UNDER THE TRAILER AND PLACED A POLY SHEET TO COVER THE OIL STAINED AREA. THE TRAILER WILL HAVE TO BE LIFTED TO DIG OUT THE CONTAMINATED SOIL.

ON 12/29/95, PHIL HINES, A HEATING CONTRACTOR REPORTED THE SPILL OCCURING AT THE HOME OF KAREN BENDER. MR. HINES REPAIRED A LOOSE FITTING BETWEEN THE VALVE AND THE FILTER.  LATER THAT DAY, 40 GAL OF OIL WAS DELIVERED TO THE TANK AND A SECOND LEAK WAS DISCOVERED A THE NIPPLE THAT ENTERS THE TANK.  MR. HINES REPLACED THE NIPPLE. APPROXIMATELY 150 GAL OF OIL HAD SPILLED ON TO THE GROUND.  DEP STAFF DUG A FEW HOLES IN THE SNOW AND FOUND SOIL SATURATED WITH OIL. 15 TONS OF SOIL WAS REMOVED ON 1/2/96 AND TRANSPORTED TO DRAGON CEMENT WITH THE HELP OF SCOTT HORNE, OF HOME CONSTRUCTION.  THE AST WAS NOT MOVED AND THERE IS STILL SOME SOIL CONTAMINATION UNDER THE TANK.

THE CROSS'S CAME INTO THIS PROPERTY AFTER THE SPILL OCCURRED, BUT THE SPILL HAD NOT BEEN REPORTED.  JON ANDREWS RESPONDED AND SET THE CROSSES UP WITH A GAC FILTER. ALEX PUGH WAS BROUGHT IN FOR LONG TERM OVERSIGHT AND AFTER SOME STUDY, HAS DECIDED THAT A LONG TERM FILTER IS MOST APPROPRIATE.

NANCY PEARL, RESIDENT ON THE WILLEY DISTRICT ROAD IN CHERRYFIELD, CALLED TO REPORT A SITUATION INVOLVING HER FATHER'S WELL WATER.  SHE STATED THAT HER FATHER, WHO RESIDES NEXT DOOR TO HER, HAS HAD TO DEAL WITH CONTAMINATED WATER FOR SEVERAL YEARS, POSSIBLY 20 OR SO IN HER ESTIMATION.  SHE BELIEVED THAT THE CONTAMINATION WAS DUE TO A FIRE THAT OCCURRED ON THE PROPERTY AT ABOUT THE SAME TIME AS THE ARRIVAL OF THE CONTAMINATED WATER.  MS. PEARL INFORMED ME THAT THE PREVIOUS HOUSE LOCATED ON THE PROPERTY HAD BURNED.  AT SOME POINT DURING THE HOUSE FIRE UNTIL THE TIME HER FATHER'S TRAILER WAS PLACED ON THE PROPERTY, A SPILL FROM THE FORMER ABOVE GROUND STORAGE TANK HAD OCCURRED.  NIETHER MS. PEARL NOR HER ELDERLY FATHER COULD GIVE A SPECIFIC ACCOUNT AS TO WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED; LET ALONE THE QUANTITY OF OIL THAT MAY HAVE BEEN LOST.
     INVESTIGATION OF THE PROPERTY SHOWN NO EVIDENCE OF OIL SPILLAGE.  THE WELL TO MR. BARNEY'S RESIDENCE IS LOCATED ONLY A FEW FEET FROM THE EXISTING 275 GALLON OIL TANK.  IT WAS IN THIS AREA THAT THE SPILL PROBABLY TOOK PLACE ACCORDING TO NANCY PEARL.  SINCE THE WELL WAS HEAVILY CONTAMINATED WITH FUEL OIL THE DECISION WAS MADE, WITH THE HELP OF PAUL BLOOD OF TECHNICAL SERVICES, TO LOCATE AN AREA FOR A REPLACEMENT WELL.  AN AREA FOR THE NEW WELL WAS LOCATED DIRECTLY BETWEEN THE SMITH'S RESIDENCE AND HIS DAUGHTER. AS OF THE END OF THE YEAR, THE SMITH'S RESIDENCE WAS SUPPLIED WITH CLEAN WATER.  THE WELL HOWEVER WILL BE TESTED FOR FUEL COMPONENTS ON A QUARTERLY BASIS GIVEN THE POSSIBILITY IT SHOULD BECOME CONTAMINATED.

TOWN DUMP. IT MAY HAVE HAD SOME USE BY THE US NAVY. LIMITED INVESTIGATION WORK BY THE DEP IN 1990. NO HIGH RISKS TO NEARBY RESIDENTS FOUND. 2006 SAMPLING FOUND NEW ISSUES WITH WELL WATER AND MORE TO BE DONE IN 2007. MELISSA ROBINSON, RESIDENT ON THE FICKETT ROAD IN MILLBRIDGE, CALLED TO REPORT THAT HER WATER SMELLED LIKE FUEL OIL. SHE STATED THAT THE ODOR BEGAN ABOUT THREE WEEKS AGO. INVESTIGATING THE COMPLAINT I FOUND THAT THE WATER DEFINITELY HAD THE ODOR OF FUEL. LAB ANALYSIS INDICATED 940 PPB DIESEL RANGE ORGANICS. A CLOSE INSPECTION OF THE PROPERTY AND SURROUNDING AREA SHOWED NO SIGN OF ANY SPILLAGE. THE WELL TO THE ROBINSON PROPERTY IS SHARED BY HER BROTHER WHO OCCUPIES A TRAILER IN THE FRONT OF THE PROPERTY NEAR THE ROAD (SEE ATTACHED SKETCH). THE ROBINSON RESIDENCE IS ABOUT 100 FEET FROM THE WELL. THE BEAL RESIDENCE, MELISSA'S BROTHER'S, IS ONLY A FEW FEET FROM THE WELL. THE WELL ORIGINALLY BELONGED TO A DIFFERENT TRAILER AND PROPERTY OWNER ABOUT A YEAR PREVIOUS. THE OIL SYSTEM AND TANK TO THE NEW TRAILER APPEARED VERY SOUND WITH NO SPILLAGE. THE ADJACENT PROPERTY, OWNED BY LYNDON PERRY, ALSO HAD A SOUND OIL SYSTEM WITHOUT ANY EVIDENCE OF SPILLAGE. THE ROBINSON SYSTEM WAS ALSO SOUND. IT MAY BE NOTED THAT THE PERRY WELL LOCATED BEHIND THE RESIDENCE WAS FREE OF HYDRO-CARBONS. IT WAS SUSPECTED THAT THE CONTAMINATION WAS PROBABLY DUE TO SPILLAGE ASSOCIATED WITH THE PREVIOUS PROPERTY OWNERS AT THE FORMER TRAILER SITE. THE WELL IS BURIED AND COULD NOT BE ACCESSED FOR INSPECTION. FURTHER INVESTIGATION AS TO THE SOURCE OF CONTAMINATION WILL BE CONDUCTED BY TECHNICAL SERVICES STAFF IN THE SPRING. 
	FOR NOW THE ROBINSONS AND MR. BEAL HAVE BEEN SUPPLIED WITH A FILTER SYSTEM. PAUL BLOOD OF THE TECHNICAL SERVICES STAFF THOUGHT IT WOULD BE IN THE BEST INTEREST TO HAVE A NEW WELL DRILLED BEHIND THE ROBINSON PROPERTY. ARRANGEMENTS WERE MADE THROUGH LORD WELL DRILLING OF ALEXANDER TO DRILL AT THE END OF JANUARY. FURTHER UPDATES TO THIS REPORT ARE PENDING.

ON 9/2/98, 0945 HOURS AN OIL RELEASE AT THE OFFICE OF BRONSON PLATNER LAW OFFICE WAS REPORTED TO US BY JEFF JOY OF RAY PLUMBING & HEATING.  THE RELEASE CAME FROM SOME VERY OLD 55 GALLON DRUMS THAT HAD BEEN USED TO STORE HEATING OIL.  AT THE TIME THIS SYSTEM WAS CURRENT THE FURNACE WAS FUELED FROM A THREE GALLON BOTTLE THAT WAS MOUNTED NEAR THE HEATING UNIT.  THE BOTTLE WOULD BE FILLED FROM THE 55 GALLON DRUMS AND CARRIED TO THE FUEL STAND NEXT TO THE FURNACE. THIS PREDATES THE FUEL PUMP WITH THE FEED LINE FROM THE SUPPLY TANK.  NEEDLESS TO SAY THE DRUMS HAD NOT BEEN USED AS FUEL SUPPLY TANKS FOR A LONG TIME.  CONSEQUENTLY, NO ONE KNEW WHEN THEY STARTED TO LEAK.  RAY PLUMBING AND HEATING WERE CALLED BECAUSE OF THE ODOR.

THE LIVING (WORK) AREA HAD A READING OF 2-3 PPM WHILE THE BASEMENT (WHERE THE SPILL HAD TAKEN PLACE) WAS 80 PPM INITIALLY.  I OPENED A COUPLE OF WINDOWS ON OPPOSITE SIDES AND CONTINUED THE INVESTIGATION.  THE FLOOR WAS CLAY AND THE FOUNDATION WAS FIELDSTONE.  THERE WAS NO FREE PRODUCT BUT THERE WAS AN AREA 17' BY 15' THAT SEEMED TO CONTAIN PRODUCT.  THE PID READING DROPPED TO 40 PPM OVER A PERIOD OF 40 MINUTES.  I CHECKED A WEEK LATER AND THE READING HAD FURTHER DECREASED TO 25.  HOWEVER, IN EARLY OCTOBER WHEN THEY STARTED TO CLOSE THINGS UP THE ODOR CAME BACK.  TECH SERVICE HAS SINCE INSTALLED A VENTILATION SYSTEM THAT HAS TAKEN CARE OF THE ODOR PROBLEM AND WILL EVENTUALLY REMOVE THE FUGITIVE PRODUCT.
5 ASTS CONTAINING FUEL OIL, DIESEL, AND KEROSENE, 4 OF WHICH ARE APPX. 10,000 GAL. SECONDARY CONTAINMENT PRESENT.

FOLLOWING WRITTEN NOTIFICATION, MARIE NOYES (WIFE OF DECEASED OWNER AMOS NOYES) BEGAN THE REMOVAL OF THREE UNDERGROUND TANKS AT SMITH'S MARKET ON MAIN STREET/ROUTE #193 IN CHERRYFIELD ON 6/30/98.  JOHN SIMS (JONESBORO; #497-5483) WAS THE LICENSED TANK INSTALLER ON SITE FOR THIS PROJECT; KENNETH PERRY (CHERRYFIELD; #564-7326) DID THE EXCAVATION; AND JOE FOWLER (FESSENDEN GEO-ENVIRONMENTAL SERVICES; BANGOR; #947-3184) WAS HIRED TO DO THE SITE ASSESSMENT.

     THE TANKS INCLUDED: TWO 1000 GALLON GASOLINE AND ONE 500 GALLON KEROSENE.  THEY WERE ALL ASPHALT COATED STEEL CONSTRUCTION, HAD GALVANIZED PIPING, AND WERE BACKFILLED WITH NON STANDARD MATERIAL.  ACCORDING TO THE REGISTRATION, ONE 1000 GALLON TANK AND THE 500 GALLON TANK WERE INSTALLED IN OCTOBER 1969.  EXACTLY WHEN THE SECOND 1000 GALLON TANK WAS INSTALLED IS UNKNOWN.  THE FACILITY WAS IN OPERATION FROM 1969 UNTIL IT CLOSED IN 1985.

     CONTAMINATED SOIL IN THE 2500+ PPM RANGE ON A PID METER WAS FOUND AROUND THE TANKS.  SINCE THE SURROUNDING AREA IS ON WELL WATER AND THERE ARE SEVERAL PUBLIC WELLS NEARBY, THE FACILITY WOULD COME UNDER DEP'S STRINGENT CLEANUP GUIDELINES.  IN ORDER TO DETERMINE THE EXTENT OF THE CONTAMINATION, TWO TEST PITS WERE DUG DOWN SLOPE FROM THE TANK HOLE.  IN THE FIRST PIT, BEDROCK WAS UNCOVERED 2.5 FEET BELOW THE SURFACE.  PID READINGS ON THE LEDGE WERE 2500+ PPM.  IN THE SECOND TEST PIT, BEDROCK WAS UNCOVERED 5 FEET BELOW THE SURFACE.  PID READINGS ON THE LEDGE WERE IN THE 10 TO 20 PPM RANGE.

     NO CORROSION HOLES IN THE TANKS OR PROBLEMS WITH THE PIPING WERE OBSERVED.  THE CONTAMINATION MAY HAVE ORIGINATED FROM PUMP PROBLEMS, OVERFILLS, OR A COMBINATION OF THINGS OVER THE YEARS.  MRS. NOYES INDICATED THAT THEY HAVE NOT BEEN ABLE TO USE THE WELL ON SITE FOR THE PAST 5 OR 6 YEARS (THEY CARRY IT IN) AND NO ONE USES WATER ON SITE AT THIS TIME.  GROUND WATER IN THE EXCAVATION CONTAINED A SLIGHT SHEEN.

     THROUGHOUT 6/30 AND 7/1/98, APPROXIMATELY 182 CUBIC YARDS WERE HAULED OFF SITE FOR AERATION.  THAT MATERIAL WENT TO MR. PERRY'S PROPERTY IN STEUBEN.  DUE TO THE LOCATION OF THE ROADBED ADJACENT TO THE TANKS ON ONE SIDE AND THE BUILDING ON THE OTHER SIDE, THEY WERE UNABLE TO REMOVE ALL OF THE CONTAMINATED MATERIAL.  PID READINGS UNDER THE BUILDING WERE IN THE 1700 TO 2300 PPM RANGE.

     RUMOR HAD IT THAT THEY USE TO SPREAD USED MOTOR OIL IN FRONT OF THE GARAGE DOOR ON THE OPPOSITE SIDE OF THE BUILDING IN ORDER TO CONTROL DUST.  A TEST PIT IN THAT AREA TURNED UP PID READINGS IN THE 10 TO 20 PPM RANGE AT MOST.

CONCLUSION:  AS A PRECAUTION, IT WAS REQUESTED THAT FESSENDEN GEO-ENVIRONMENTAL SERVICE SAMPLE SOME OF THE SURROUNDING WELLS.  THE RESULTS ON SMITH'S MARKET TURNED UP 7 PPB AND ON JOHN MURPHY'S WELL WAS 11 PPB ON THE FIRST ROUND AND 9 PPB ON THE SECOND ROUND.  BOTH WELLS ARE BELOW THE ACTION LEVEL OF 25 PPB.  SINCE THE AREA IS ON WELLS, THE CASE HAS BEEN REFERRED TO TECH SERVICES FOR THEIR INFORMATION AND/OR ACTION.

     THE SPREAD SITE WAS CHECKED SEVERAL TIME THROUGHOUT THE SUMMER.  AS OF 8/11/98, THE PID READINGS HAVE DROPPED FROM 2500+ PPM DOWN TO THE 420 TO 750 PPM RANGE.

ON 9/9/98, 1000 HOURS CYNTHEA WILCOX REPORTED A PRODUCT RELEASE IN THE BASEMENT OF HER HOUSE IN CHERRYFIELD.  THE RELEASE WAS COMING IN DROPWISE FASHION FROM A CORROSION HOLE IN THE SPIGOT END OF HER AST.  SHE ESTIMATED THAT SHE HAD LOST 50 GALLONS, BUT I CALCULATED FROM THE AREA AND THICKNESS THAT IT WAS LESS THAN 10.  THE SURFACE THAT THE SPILL LANDED ON WAS A MIXTURE OF BROKEN CEMENT PIECES AND WET CLAY.  IT WAS DIFFICULT TO REMEDIATE SO I SUGGESTED THAT THEY KEEP THE BASEMENT AREA VENTILATED, SINCE THE ONLY PROBLEM CAUSED BY THE RELEASE WAS ODOR.  THE WELL IS CLOSE TO THE HOUSE BUT IT IS DEEP INTO BEDROCK AND THE SPILL AREA IS WET CLAY WITH SURFICIAL GROUND WATER VERY CLOSE TO GRADE THE YEAR ROUND.  I TOLD CYNTHEA THAT IF THE ODOR PERSISTED INTO COLD WEATHER, I WOULD HAVE A VENT SYSTEM INSTALLED.  ON 10/9/98 ROBERT SYPITKOWSKI AND I INSTALLED A VENT SYSTEM THAT IS REMOVING PRODUCT VAPOR WITHOUT COOLING THE BASEMENT AREA.  AS PRECAUTIONARY MEASURES I HAD CYNTHEA APPLY TO THE FUND AND I PUT HER WELL ON QM.

ON 2-19-98, LUCY PERKINS NOTIFIED THE FORT FAIRFIELD FIRE DEPT. OF A SPILL OF KEROSENE AT HER RESIDENCE IN FORT FAIRFIELD. THE FIRE DEPT. LATER REPORTED THE SPILL TO THIS OFFICE. UPON INVESTIGATION, IT WAS ESTIMATED ABOUT 200 GALLONS OF KEROSENE WAS LOST FROM THE OUTSIDE 275 GALLON TANK ON ABOUT 2-12-98. SHE WAS OUT OF FUEL AND DISCOVERED A CRACKED FITTING ON THE TANK DUE TO ICE FALLING OFF THE ROOF. SHE BEGAN TO NOTICE AN ODOR IN THE HOUSE BEGINNING IN THE WEEK OF 2-16-98. AT THIS POINT IT HAD TRAVELLED BENEATH THE PERIMETER SLAB OF THE HOUSE AND GONE INTO THE LIVING AREA. SODERBERG CONSTRUCTION WAS HIRED TO PERFORM THE REMEDIATION. FIRST, ALL CONTAMINATED SOIL THAT COULD BE REMOVED WAS, THEN A RECOVERY WELL WAS INSTALLED OUTSIDE TO RECOVER PRODUCT FROM BENEATH THE SLAB. NEXT, THE LIVING ROOM FLOOR WAS REMOVED AND A SERIES OF VENTS AND SEALS WERE PLACED. THE VENTS WILL CONTINUE TO RUN AS LONG AS THEY DRAW OUT VAPORS AND THE PUMP AND TREAT SYSTEM WILL MOST LIKELY RUN MOST OF THE SPRING. MS. PERKINS WAS ALSO PLACED ON QM.

GARY AT DEAD RIVER CALLED THIS OFFICE ON 3-5-98 TO REPORT A SMALL RELEASE AT MR. BROWN'S HOME. THE COPPER FEED LINE HAD DEVELOPED A PIN HOLE LEAK. MRS. BROWN DETECTED ODORS THAT MORNING. DEAD RIVER RESPONDED AND REPLACED THE COPPER LINE. GARY INDICATED THAT THERE WAS SMALL AMOUNT OF OIL IN THE CRAWL SPACE, WHICH HAS A DIRT FLOOR.
 I MADE A SITE VISIT ON 3-6-98. I FOUND OIL FLOATING ON THE WATER IN THE CRAWL SPACE. IN ADDITION, I FOUND A BASEMENT DRAIN AND OIL IN A DITCH, FIFTY FEET FROM THE HOUSE. I NEXT PLACED PADS ONTO THE OIL AND THEN CALLED DEAD RIVER. I ASKED THEM TO SEND SOMEONE OVER AND I ALSO HIRED THEM TO PICK UP PADS AND REMOVE SOIL. THIS WILL OCCUR NEXT WEEK.
 A CREW FROM DEAD RIVER USED PADS TO RECOVER OIL FROM THE BASEMENT AND DRAINAGE DITCH. THEY DID NOT REMOVE ANY SOIL FROM THE CRAWL SPACE.
 THE DRILLED WELL IS LOCATED BETWEEN THE HOUSE AND THE ROAD.
 SEVERAL MONTHS AFTER MY INITIAL RESPONSE I LEARNED THAT THE AST DEVELOPED A HOLE IN THE BOTTOM SEVERAL DAYS AFTER I LEFT. DEAD RIVER REPLACED THE TANK AND CLEANED UP THAT SPILL, THEY WERE ALREADY ON SITE. THE TANK IS LOCATED IN THE GARAGE AND THE COPPER LINE GOES INTO THE CRAWL SPACE TO THE FURNACE.
 IT APPEARS THAT LITTLE IF ANY OIL SEEPED INTO THE SOIL. MOST OF THE OIL WAS FLOATING ON WATER.
SEE SPILL REPORT P-124-1998. FLOOR DRAIN DISCHARGE POINT NOT KNOWN. MINIMAL UIC INFO AVAILABLE.

FREE PRODUCT WAS FOUND IN MANNING'S WELL, THERE ARE SEVERAL WELLS NEARBY.
ON 6/8/1998 DAVID HATCH OF L.R. FRENCH INC. CALLED THIS OFFICE TO REPORT THAT HE HAD FOUND OIL IN A RESIDENTIAL WELL.  THE WELL IS OWNED BY MR. MANNING AND IS LOCATED ON RTE 129 IN SOUTH BRISTOL, JUST SOUTH OF "THE GUT".  MR. HATCH WAS HIRED TO PUMP THE WELL, BECAUSE IT HAD NOT BEEN USED FOR QUITE SIME TIME.  MR. HATCH DISCONNECTED THE WATER LINE FROM THE PRESSURE TANK AND THEN TURNED ON THE PUMP.  AFTER SEVERAL MINUTES THE WATER TURNED PINK/RED AND WAS OILY.  HE TURNED THE PUMP OFF AT THAT TIME.
I MET MR. HATCH AND WE PROCEEDED TO THE SITE.  WE LOOKED AT THE CURRENT FUEL SYSTEM AND THERE WERE NO PROBLEMS NOTICED THERE.  NEXT WE WENT TO THE BOAT HOUSE/ GARAGE AND CHECKED OUT THE PREVIOUS LOCATION OF THE AST.  WE FOUND WHERE THE TANK HAD BEEN LOCATED AND THE PLYWOOD FLOOR HAD A STAIN ON IT.  HOWEVER, THE DIRT UNDER THE PLYWOOD FLOOR DID NOT HAVE ANY ODORS.  THE ORIGINAL COPPER FEED LINE WAS STILL IN PLACE ANT IT WAS SLEEVED IN A PLASTIC CONDUIT.  I CHECKED SEVERAL OF THE ADJOINING PROPERTIES FOR LEAKS AND COLLECTED TWO WATER SAMPLES.  I FOUND A 275 GALLON TANK THAT HAD BEEN PUSHED INTO BUSHES BETWEEN THE MANNING PROPERTY AND THE KIDDER(COOSE) PROPERTY.  THIS TANK HAD A MAGNETIC PATCH ON THE BOTTOM.
THE WELL AT MANNING'S HAD 1.5" OF OIL FLOATING ON THE WATER COLUMN.  THE STATIC WATER LEVEL WAS 27'.  WE USED A BAILER AND SORBENT PADS TO RECOVER THE OIL.
ON 6-11-1998 I WENT BACK TO SOUTH BRISTOL AND COLLECTED FIVE ADDITIONAL WATER SAMPLES.  I ALSO CHECKED THE FUEL SYSTEM IN FOUR HOMES.

FREE PRODUCT APPEARED IN THE WELL SO IT WAS ABANDONNED AND PLOURDE DRILLED A NEW WELL 125' FROM THE UST.  ON 8/31/97 THE UST WAS REMOVED AND NO CONTAMINATED SOIL WAS OBSERVED.  THE NEW WELL DOES NOT SHOW ANY DETECTABLE LEVELS BUT THE OLD WELL IS STILL CONTAMINATED AND SLIGHTLY EXCEEDS THE DRINKING WATER STANDARD OF 50 PPB.
MYSTERY SPILL, MTBE CONTAMINATION

DURING A NO HEAT CALL, A BROKEN LINE WAS FOUND THE SAME DAY THAT 120 GALLONS OF FUEL HAD BEEN DELIVERED.  THE TANK WAS BURIED IN SNOW AT THE TIME OF THE LOSS.  I EXPECTED TO FIND LOTS OF CONTAMINATED SNOW, BUT WAS ONLY ABLE TO LOCATE A SMALL AMOUNT JUST NEAR THE TANK, SO I FELT THAT THE FUEL MUST HAVE SOAKED IN AT THE EDGE OF THE CONCRETE PAD UNDER THE TRAILER. THERE WERE SEVERAL HEAVY RAINS BEFORE WE COULD MAKE ARRANGEMENTS TO EXCAVATE.  THE SPILL SITE WAS DIFFICULT TO GET TO DUE TO LARGE TREES AND ICY CONDITIONS.  WHEN WE DID EXCAVATE I WAS ONLY ABLE TO LOCATE A SMALL AMOUNT OF CONTAMINATED SOIL.  THE SOIL WAS HEAVY SANDY CLAY UNDER FILL.  CONTAMINATION WAS ALL IN THE TOP 4'.  THERE WAS A COARSE LAYER JUST UNDER THE PAD, BUT CONTAMINATION LEVELS WERE NOT HIGH.  I FEEL THAT EXCAVATION DID NOT LOCATE AS MUCH CONTAMINATION AS EXPECTED FROM THE AMOUNT OF OIL LOSS.  PERHAPS SOME DID WASH AWAY WITH THE RAINS.

ABOUT TWO WEEKS AGO, THEY STARTED PICKING UP TASTE AND ODOR PROBLEMS IN THE WATER, WHICH MIGHT BE GASOLINE.  THE FACILITY IS BRAND NEW (ONLY ONE YEAR OLD) AND EVERYTHING IS DOUBLE CONTAINMENT (TANKS, PIPING, PUMPS).      NOT KNOWING EXACTLY WHAT THE CONTAMINANT WAS IN THE WELL, IT WAS SUGGESTED THAT THEY MAKE ARRANGEMENTS TO HAVE THE WATER TESTED. MANGANESE AND HIGH COLIFORM BACTERIA.  I WAS INFORMED THAT THERE USE TO BE A CHICKEN BARN ON THE PROPERTY AND A.E. ROBINSON DID HAVE A SITUATION THIS PAST WINTER WHERE SURFACE RUNOFF FROM THE YARD GOT INTO THE WELL, SO THAT MIGHT BE THE SOURCE OF THE PROBLEM.  THEY WOULD KEEP ME POSTED.

THE LOCATION WAS AT THE HOME OF STEVEN BENTLEY ON THE OLD FOXCROFT ROAD IN HOULTON. I MET WITH MR. BENTLEY AND JERRY LONDON, A LOCAL CONTRACTOR, AT THE SITE. THE TANK THAT LEAKED WAS A 275 GALLON OUTSIDE TANK. IT WAS ON BEDROCK SO NO SOIL REMOVAL COULD BE PERFORMED. THERE WAS NO TRACE OF FUEL BENEATH THE TANK AND THE WELL WAS LOCATED ABOUT 20' DOWNGRADIENT. THE BENTLEYS WERE PLACED ON QUARTERLY MONITORING. TWO DAYS LATER, MRS. BENTLEY CALLED TO REPORT FUEL IN THEIR WATER. A CARBON FILTER WAS PUT ON THE FOLLOWING DAY.

FORMERLY D&D RESTAURANT

ON 2-28-95, 1745 HOURS WILLIE (WHO WORKS FOR WEBBER OIL) REPORTED THAT A LINE LEAK HAD BEEN FOUND AT BANGOR GARDENS.  I CONTACTED WILLIE FOR MORE DETAILS AND OBTAINED THE FOLLOWING INFORMATION.  HE HAD BEEN CALLED TO THE RESIDENCE (OF OWEN AND CELIA MONDAY) TO INVESTIGATE THE CAUSE OF A STRANGE NOISE THAT WAS ASSOCIATED WITH THEIR OIL BURNER.  THEY (WEBBER PERSONNEL) OBSERVED THE ODOR OF PRODUCT.  SINCE THERE WAS NO OBVIOUS LEAK, WILLIE SUGGESTED THAT THEY PRESSURE TEST THE FUEL LINE.  THE MONDAYS' WERE NOT IMMEDIATELY IN FAVOR OF THIS.  THEY FELT THAT THE ODOR WAS FROM AN EARLIER UST PROBLEM, WHICH IS BEING HANDLED BY OUR DARRYL LUCE.  HOWEVER, PERSISTENCE PREVAILED AND THE TEST WAS DONE.  AS A RESULT THEY COULD SEE FUEL COMING OUT WHERE THE LINE COMES THROUGH THE CEMENT SLAB ON THE INSIDE OF THE HOUSE.  THE VISIBLE PORTION OF THIS PART OF THE SPILL WAS INSIGNIFICANT.  IT IS IMPOSSIBLE TO ESTIMATE THE VOLUME OF SPILLED PRODUCT THAT THE LEAK HAD PRODUCED OVER A PERIOD OF TIME.  THE USAGE AT THE FACILITY IS A LITTLE HIGH AT 1300 GALLONS PER YEAR.  HOWEVER THE UNIT HAS A ROOM ADDED  AND IT IS KEPT AT ABOUT 80 DEGREES BECAUSE THEY RUN A DAY-CARE CENTER FOR SMALL CHILDREN.  HENCE  THE VOLUME OF THE SPILL REMAINS UNKNOWN, BUT IT WAS NOT A CATACLYSMIC EVENT EITHER.

THE UST PROBLEM REFERRED TO ABOVE WAS CAUSE BY AN IMPROPERLY ABANDONED TANK.  AT SOME POINT IN TIME AN ADD-ON ROOM WAS BUILT OVER THE ABANDONED UST, AND THE ADD-ON WAS ON A SLAB WITH A FROST WALL. ON THE AFTERNOON OF 7/29/98 ALEX PUGH (MDEP GEOLOGIST IN AUGUSTA) PASSED ON A WATER ANALYSIS REPORT INDICATING LOW LEVEL CONTAMINATION FROM WHAT MAY BE A PETROLEUM PRODUCT.  THE SAMPLE WAS TAKEN FROM THE WATER SUPPLY (DRILLED WELL) OF SHANE AND LORENE BRAGDEN (P.O. BOX 332, HOLDEN 04429, 989-9746, LOREN'S WORK # 941- 2871).  AT ALEX'S SUGGESTION I TALKED WITH LARRY BOSTON ABOUT THE ANALYSIS.  IT HAPPENED THAT THE UNIDENTIFIED COMPOUND WERE TARGET COMPOUND SO HETL HAD STANDARD CHROMATOGRAMS FOR THEM.  MTBE WAS 1 PPB.  OTHER WATER SOLUBLE COMPOUNDS INCLUDED ISOPROPYL BENZENE (.2 PPB) , BUTYL BENZENE (.06 PPB), 1,2,4 METHYL BENZENE (.2 PPB), SECONDARY BUTYL BENZENE(.08 PPB) AND 4 ISO PROPYLTOLUENE(.08 PPB).  LARRY SAID THERE WAS A BELOW DETECTION HINT OF NAPTHA (<.01 PPB).  SOME OF THE ANALYSIS SUGGESTS GASOLINE CONTAMINATION, BUT THE LOW MTBE SORT OF NULLIFIES THIS CONCLUSION.

ON 7/30/98 I VISITED THE SITE AND SAMPLED THE WATER.  THE WELL IS DRILLED BUT THE DEPTH AND CASING LENGTH ARE NOT KNOWN.  THE WATER IS BOGGY.  IT SMELLS BUT IT DOES NOT GIVE A PHOTON HIT.  I EXPECT THE SMELL IS SULFIDITY-PERHAPS IN THE FORM OF MERCAPTANS.  THE SURFICIAL ACQUIFER IS NEAR GRADE ON THE BRAGDON PROPERTY,  IN FACT A HUNDRED OR SO FEET FROM THE DRILLED WELL IS A SUBSTANTIAL GROUND WATER SEEP.  SHANE SAID THAT THEY HAD LIVED THERE EIGHT YEARS AND NEVER HAD A PROBLEM WITH THE WATER.  THEIR HOUSE CAUGHT ON FIRE ON THE SAME SIDE THAT THE WELL IS ON AND THEY'VE HAD BAD WELL WATER EVER SINCE.  DID THE HEAT FROM THE FIRE DO SOMETHING TO THE GROUT?


OTHER THINGS WORTH MENTIONING- HIS ABUTTER ON THE NORTH SIDE SELL MODULAR HOMES AND HE HEATS THEM WITH KEROSENE FEED FROM 55 GALLONS DRUMS.  SHANE SAYS THAT THEY CARRY FUEL TO THESE DRUMS IN FIVE GALLON PAILS.  HE SAID THAT AT ONE TIME THE ODOR OF SPILLED KEROSENE WAS STRONG.  HE SHOWED ME THE PLACE BUT THERE WAS NO EVIDENCE OF SPILLED PRODUCT AT THAT TIME.  (IT SMELLED LIKE DIRT, WHICH MEANS TO ME THAT THE SOIL HAD NOT BEEN EXPOSED TO PRODUCT FOR A LONG TIME.  THE ABUTTER ON THE SOUTH SIDE PROCESSES FIRE WOOD.  THERE IS A LOT OF SAW CHIPS AROUND AND OF COURSE THE POSSIBILITY OF FUELING SPILLS.  HOWEVER,  I WOULD THINK THAT THE HIGH SURFICIAL GROUND WATER LEVEL WOULD PROTECT THE BEDROCK ACQUIFER FROM SUCH SPILLS. 

THE NEL ANALYSIS INDICATED <5PPB/TRACE OF GRO.  ALL OF THE COMPONENTS (MTBE, BENZENE, TOLUENE, ETHYL BENZENE AND TOTAL XYLENES) WERE BELOW DETECTION.  THE REPORT STATES THAT THE CHROMATOGRAM EXHIBITS THE GENERAL CHARACTERISTICS OF A GASOLINE CONTAMINATION.  AN INTERESTING, POSITIVE OBSERVATION COMING FROM THIS INVESTIGATION IS THAT NEL AND HETL ARE IN AGREEMENT.

properties.SUMMARY:
3/28 2007- MR. GARFIELD FOSS (BUD-ROE, INC), MR. NATHAN WARDWELL (NFSG LLC), AND MS. SARAH WARDWELL APPLIED FOR VRAP PROTECTION FOR THE UNION STREET CITGO STATION.  BASED ON THE RESULTS OF A PHASE I AND PHASE II INVESTIGATION CONDUCTED BY CES, THEY WERE GRANTED VRAP PROTECTIONS WITH THE UNDERSTANDING THAT NO GROUNDWATER EXTRACTION WELLS WOULD BE INSTALLED ON THE PROPERTY IN THE FUTURE AND THAT USE OF THE PROPERTY REMAINS COMMERCIAL.

SPILL NARRATIVE FOR SPILL #B-386-1994:
7/5/1994- FOLLOWING WRITTEN NOTIFICATION, THE CN BROWN COMPANY (SOUTH PARIS) BEGAN THE REMOVAL OF 5 USTS AT THE UNION STREET CITGO.  LEONARD CARR (LC'S TANK INSTALLATION) CALLED THE DEP ON THE SAME DAY TO INFORM US THAT THEY HAD UNCOVERED SOME CONTAMINATED SOIL IN THE EXCAVATION.  PID METER READINGS WERE IN THE 1200PPM RANGE.  DEP'S ASSISTANCE WAS REQUESTED ON SITE.
ARRANGEMENTS FOR REMOVAL/TRANSPORTATION OF CONTAMINATED SOIL AND TREATMENT OF CONTAMINATED GROUNDWATER IN THE EXCAVATION WERE MADE, AND THE TANK REMOVAL RESUMED 7/6/1994. 
7/6/1994- REMOVAL OF THE THREE GASOLINE TANKS RESUMED.  THEY WERE ALL ASPHALT COATED, HAD GALVANIZED PIPING, AND WERE BACKFILLED WITH SAND.  THEIR AGE WAS UNKNOWN.  SOIL CONTAMINATION IN THE EXCAVATION RANGED FROM AROUND 65 PPM IN THE BOTTOM OF THE HOLE UP TO ABOUT 1900 PPM.  THE SURROUNDING SOIL WAS A GLACIAL TILL.  NO CORROSION HOLES IN THE TANKS OR PROBLEMS WITH THE PIPING WERE OBSERVED.  RUMOR HAD IT THAT THE PLUS UNLEADED TANK BEGAIN TAKING ON WATER ~6 WEEKS PRIOR TO THIS DATE AND WAS TAKEN OUT OF SERVICE.  THE PROBLEM WAS BELIEVED TO BE IN THE PIPING.  THEY HAVE HAD SIMILAR PROBLEMS IN THE PAST.  ITW WAS NOW REPORTED TO CONTAIN ~20" OF WATER.  THE OTHER TANKS WERE ALL ACTIVE UP UNTIL CLEAN HARBORS OF MAINE, INC. (PORTLAND) PUMPED THEM OUT ON 7/5/1994.  THEY WERE SCHEDULED TO BE HAULED TO A SITE IN DEXTER TO BE CUT UP FOR SCRAP METAL.
7/7/1994- EXCAVATION OF THE CONTAMINATED SOIL CONTINUED.  ALL OF THE SOIL THAT COULD BE REMOVED AROUND THE TANKS WAS REMOVED.  RATHER THAN UNDERMINE THE ROADBED ALONG THE EDGE OF 14TH STREET, VARIOUS LEVELS OF CONTAMINATION WERE LEFT IN PLACE IN THAT AREA.  THE NEW TANKS ARRIVED AROUND 1200, AND IT WAS DECIDED THAT THE REMAINING TWO 500 GALLON TANKS (#2 FUEL OIL AND WASTE OIL) AND ALL OF THE ASSOCIATED PIPING WOULD NOT BE REMOVED UNTIL AFTER THE NEW TANKS WERE INSTALLED AND IN OPERATION.
7/11/1994- REMOVAL OF REMAINING TANKS.  ACCORDING TO EMERY & GARRETT, THE TWO 500 GALLON TANKS AND AN UNKNOWN 1000 GALLON TANK (LOCATED OUT FRONT) WERE PULLED.  THEY WERE ALL ASPHALT COATED, HAD GALVANIZED PIPING, AND CONTAINED ONE OR MORE CORROSION HOLES.  ADDITIONAL CUBIC YARDS OF CONTAMINATED SOIL WERE EXCAVATED FROM AROUND THE TANKS, PIPING, AND PUMP ISLAND.  IN ALL, ~1575 TONS (1212 CUBIC YARDS) WERE TRANSPORTED TO TILCON IN FAIRFIELD FOR RECYCLING.

properties.SUMMARY:
ABANDONED.

THIS OFFICE RECEIVED A CALL AT 0830 ON 10/1/01 FROM BUB SAUNDERS (FGS/CMT, INC; BANGOR) REPORTING AN OIL SPILL.  HE STATED THAT THEY WERE IN THE PROCESS OF REMOVING TWO UNDERGROUND TANKS AT THE FORMER CLIFTON VARIETY ON ROUTE 9 IN CLIFTON AND HAD ENCOUNTERED SOME CONTAMINATED SOIL.  DEP¿S ASSISTANCE WAS REQUESTED ON SITE.

     PROCEEDING TO CLIFTON, I MET WITH MR. SAUNDERS, DON PAGE (WEBBER OIL COMPANY; BANGOR; #942-5505), AND GEORGE BUTLER (PENQUIS COMMUNITY ACTION PROGRAM; BANGOR; #973-3554).  ALTHOUGH THE TANKS ARE OWNED BY JAMES HODGINS, THEY WERE BEING REMOVED UNDER THE PENQUIS CAP THROUGH WEBBER OIL.  VAUGHN THIBODEAU & SONS (BANGOR; #941-9859) WAS HIRED TO COORDINATE THE EXCAVATION; ED HASKELL (HASKELL ENERGIES COMPANY; AUGUSTA; #622-7561) WAS THE LICENSED TANK INSTALLER ON SITE FOR THE PROJECT; AND FGS/CMT, INC. DID THE SITE ASSESSMENT.

     THE FACILITY HAS BEEN OPERATED AS A COMBINATION COUNTRY STORE AND GAS STATION SINCE SOMETIME IN THE EARLY 1940¿S.  IT WENT OUT OF BUSINESS IN 1998 AFTER MR. HODGINS WAS SHOT SEVERAL TIMES DURING A HOLDUP.  HE IS NOW CONFINED TO A WHEELCHAIR ON THE PROPERTY.  THE TANKS SCHEDULED FOR REMOVAL INCLUDED ONE 4000 GALLON GASOLINE AND ONE 1000 GALLON GASOLINE.

     DURING THE MORNING, TOTAL WASTE MANAGEMENT (HERMON; #848-7600) PUMPED BOTH TANKS OUT AND CLEANED THEIR INTERIOR.  THE 4000 GALLON TANK WAS LOCATED ON THE LEFT SIDE OF THE FACILITY.  IT WAS CONSTRUCTED OF ASPHALT COATED STEEL, HAD GALVANIZED PIPING, AND WAS BACKFILLED WITH SAND.  ACCORDING TO THE REGISTRATION, IT HAD BEEN INSTALLED IN 1973.  DUE TO A HIGH WATER TABLE IN THE AREA, THE TANK WAS ¿ANCHORED¿ BY HAVING CONCRETE POURED OVER THE TOP OF IT.  THIS TANK APPEARED TO BE IN GOOD CONDITION; NO CORROSION HOLES WERE OBSERVED.  THE SURROUNDING SOIL WAS A GLACIAL TILL TYPE OF MATERIAL AND GROUNDWATER, WITH A SLIGHT SHEEN ON IT, WAS FOUND 7 OR 8 FEET BELOW THE SURFACE.  CLAY WAS ENCOUNTERED ON THE BOTTOM OF THE EXCAVATION.

     THE 1000 GALLON TANK EXTENDED UNDER AN ADDITION TO THE BUILDING AND HAD TO BE ABANDONED IN PLACE.  IT WAS CONSTRUCTED OF ASPHALT COATED STEEL, HAD GALVANIZED PIPING, AND WAS BACKFILLED WITH A NON STANDARD TYPE OF MATERIAL.  DURING THE CLEANING, A 3/8 INCH HOLE WAS OBSERVED ALONG THE BOTTOM OF THE TANK.  ACCORDING TO THE REGISTRATION, THIS TANK WAS INSTALLED IN 1947, BUT DUE TO ITS NEWER CONSTRUCTION, IT MAY HAVE BEEN CONFUSED WITH ANOTHER 1000 GALLON TANK THAT WAS REMOVED IN 1986.  THAT TANK WAS BELIEVED TO HAVE BEEN INSTALLED IN 1967.  THE ABANDONED TANK WAS FILLED WITH A FLOWABLE FILL (CONCRETE) BY THIBODEAU.

     CONTAMINATED SOIL, IN THE 2500+ PPM RANGE, WAS FOUND AROUND BOTH TANKS AND UNDER THE PUMP ISLAND OUT FRONT.  THIS MAY HAVE ORIGINATED FROM A NUMBER OF SOURCES OVER THE YEARS, SUCH AS: FROM PREVIOUS TANKS ON SITE; SEVERAL LOOSE PIPE FITTINGS/CONNECTIONS THAT WERE OBSERVED; CUSTOMER SPILLAGE AROUND THE PUMPS; ETC.  SINCE THE SITE AND SURROUNDING AREA ARE ON WELL WATER, THIS FACILITY WOULD COME UNDER DEP¿S STRINGENT CLEANUP GUIDELINES.  DURING THE NEXT FOUR DAYS, AN ESTIMATED 1400 CUBIC YARDS OF CONTAMINATED SOIL WERE HAULED TO THIBODEAU¿S BATCH PLANT FOR PROCESSING.  MATERIAL THAT WAS TRAPPED UNDER THE BUILDING AND IN THE ROADBED UNDER ROUTE 9 REMAINED IN PLACE.  TOWARDS THE END OF THE EXCAVATION, LEDGE WAS ENCOUNTERED IN ONE AREA NEAR THE PUMP ISLAND.

     DUE TO THE AMOUNT OF CONTAMINATION FOUND, THE DRILLED WELL ON SITE, WHICH IS USED BY MR. HODGINS AND A NEIGHBOR BEHIND THE PROPERTY, WAS SAMPLED FOR HYDROCARBONS.  THE TEST RESULTS INDICATED 8.2 PPB GRO, WHICH IS BELOW DEP¿S ACTION LEVEL.  THERE IS ALSO AN OLD DUG WELL ON THE PROPERTY NEAR THE FRONT DOOR, BUT IT IS NO LONGER USED.

10/18/13 RECEIVED A CALL FROM MS. CARLA ALBERT OF ST. FRANCIS COMPLAINING OF A SPILL/OVERFILL OF DIESEL FUEL COMING FROM THE FORMER GAS STATION OWNED BY JOHN VOISINE, KNOWN AS JOHN'S COUNTRY STORE, NOW DOING BUSINESS AS JOE'S COUNTRY STORE.  MS. ALBERT STATED THAT THE NEW STORE OWNER DOES A SLOPPY JOB AND THERE ARE FRQUENT OVERFILLS.  THIS MOST RECENT ONE APPEARS TO SMELL OF DIESEL AND IS SHEENING DOWN THE ROAD SURFACE AWAY FROM THE STORE.

THE STORE, JOE'S COUNTRY STORE IS UST# 9349.  IT HAS 3 - 2,000 GALLON ACTIVE TANKS. THE TANKS HOLD DIESEL, REGULAR UL AND PREMIUM UL.  THERE IS A 4TH TANK THAT WAS USED TO STORE KEROSENE (K-1) BUT IS NOT OUT OF SERVICE (OOS).  THERE IS STATISTICAL INVENTORY ANALYSIS FOR THE FUEL FLOW THROUGH AT THIS FACILITY.

CALLED JOE @ JOE'S COUNTRY STORE @ 398-4172 TO DISCUSS IF THEY HAD EXPERIENCED A FUEL SPILL OR RELEASE IN THE LAST FEW DAYS.  JOE STATED THAT THERE HAD NOT BEEN ANY FUEL SPILL AT HIS FACILITY.  ASKED JOE IF HE AND HIS EMPLOYEES HAVE BEEN THROUGH THE TANKSMART PROGRAM AND GOTTEN CERTIFIED.  JOE STATED THAT HE AND HIS WIFE ARE THE ONLY ONES WHO WORK AT THE GAS STATION AND C-STORE, THEY HAVE OWNED IT FOR ABOUT THREE YEARS AND HAVE BOTH GONE THROUGH THE TANKSMART TRAINING PROGRAM.  I ASKED IF JOE HAD A SPILL LOG FOR SPILL OF 10 GALLONS OR LESS AT HIS FACILITY.  HE DID NOT AND WAS NOT AWARE THAT HE NEEDED TO LOG IN THESE SMALLER SPILLS.  TOLD JOE THAT THE RESPONSE STAFF WOULD BE DOING A FOLLOW-UP ON WEDNESDAY OCTOBER 22ND, TO THE SPILL COMPLAINT AND WOULD FAX A COPY OF A BLANK SPILL LOG FOR HIS USE (PHOTOCOPING).  JOE CALLED BACK A SHORT WHILE AFTER TALKING WITH HIM. APPARENTLY HE HAD A SPILL LOG WITH SOME ENTRIES, BUT APPRECIATES A BLANK LOG FOR USE IN THE FUTURE.

SINCE I FOUND NO MORE SIGN OF CONTAMINATION IN THE HOLE I HAD IT FILLED.  SINCE THE CONTAMINATED SOIL ORIGINATED AT THE FILLPIPE THE PROBLEM WAS LIKELY CAUSED BY A LARGE OVERFILL OR SEVERAL SMALLER OVERFILLS.  ALTHOUGH THERE WAS A HOLE IN THE TANK, IT WAS PLUGGED WITH A PIECE OF CLAY AND THERE WAS NO SOIL CONTAMINTAION AROUND THIS SPOT.  THE SITE ASSESSOR, MICHAEL MILLETT SAMPLED A SEASON RESTAURANT'S WELL THAT WAS WITHIN 100 FEET AND THE RESULTS WERE NEGATIVE.  THE RESULTS OF THE STORE'S WELL ANALYSIS WERE ALSO BELOW THE DETECTION LIMIT.

ON APRIL 2, 2001 AT 1630 WE RECEIVED A CALL FROM PETER REMICK OF ORLAND REPORTING A POSSIBLE WELL CONTAMINATION FROM A LEAK IN HIS BASEMENT TANK'S COPPER FEEDLINE.  THE LEAK WAS DISCOVERED THE PREVIOUS OCTOBER 21, 2000, BUT WAS NEVER REPORTED.  MR. REMICK'S DRILLED WELL IS ALSO LOCATED IN HIS BASEMENT ABOUT TWELVE FEET FROM THE LEAK.  MR. REMICK SAID HIS WATER NOW HAS AN OIL SMELL.
      I VISITED THE SITE THE NEXT MORNING AND FOUND THAT THERE WAS VERY LITTLE SMELL IN THE SOIL WHERE THE LEAK OCCURRED.  SOME SOIL WAS REMOVED AT THE TIME OF THE SPILL.  MR. REMICK THOUGHT THAT ABOUT FIFTY GALLONS OF #2 FUEL LEAKED FROM THE LINE.  THIS ESTIMATE WAS BASED ON DELIVERIES ON SEPT. 21 AND NOV. 16 AND HIS ESTIMATED USAGE.
      I TOOK A SAMPLE FROM THE WELL AND ASKED FOR A SVO ANALYSIS WHICH WAS NON-DETECT FOR THE ANALYZED CONSTITUENTS.  ALTHOUGH THESE CONSTITUENTS ARE FOUND IN FUEL OIL, I ERRED IN NOT ASKING FOR A DIESEL RANGE ORGANICS (DRO) ANALYSIS WHICH WOULD HAVE TESTED FOR THE TOTAL RANGE OF FUEL OIL.  THEREFORE, I TOOK ANOTHER SAMPLE ON APRIL 25 FOR A DRO ANALYSIS BY NORTHEAST LABS.  MEANWHILE, I LEARNED THAT THE REMICK WELL HAD VERY HIGH LEVELS OF MANGANESE AND IRON AND HAD A FILTER FOR THEIR REMOVAL WHICH WAS A FEW YEARS OLD.  OUR OFFICE'S TECHNICAL SERVICE'S GROUP HAD HANDLED A SIMILAR CASE, GREENFIELD B-190- 94, WHERE A COMBINATION OF MANGANESE AND IRON PRODUCED A FUEL OIL SMELL AND CONFUSED THE LAB ANALYSIS.  I INFORMED MR. REMICK OF THIS INFORMATION AND HE REPLACED HIS FILTER WHICH STOPPED THE FUEL OIL SMELL.
      THE DRO ANALYSIS CAME BACK AT 89 PPB OF A WEATHERED FUEL OIL OR DIESEL OIL.  NORTHEAST LABS SAID THERE WERE SOME UNUSUAL CHARACTERISTICS OF THE CHROMATAGRAM ESPECIALLY SINCE THE SVO ANALYSIS WAS COMPLETELY NEGATIVE.  BASED ON THIS, AND A SIMILAR SCENARIO FROM SPILL B-190-94, PLUS THE FACT THAT CHANGING FILTERS THAT REMOVED MANGANESE AND IRON ELIMINATED THE FUEL OIL SMELL MADE ME BELIEVE THAT MR. REMICK'S WELL IS NOT CONTAMINATED WITH FUEL OIL.

GARY'S FUEL CO. CALLED TO REPORT THAT A CUSTOMER, WENDY FINDLAY, 405 FRONT RIDGE ROAD, ORLAND HAD SUFFERED AN OIL SPILL. THEY HAD LOST THEIR HEAT AND THE TECHNICIAN DETERMINED THAT THE OUTSIDE 275 WAS EMPTY. THE OIL COMPANY RECORDS SEEMED TO INDICATE THAT THE TANK SHOULD HAVE HELD AT LEAST 125 GALLONS AT THIS TIME. THE OIL COMPANY THOUGHT THAT DUE TO THE SLOW DRIP RATE THAT THE LOSS HAD OCCURRED OVER A LONG PERIOD OF TIME. THE LEAK HAD OCCURRED AT A TEE FITTING UNDERNEATH SOME PLASTIC BANKING AT THE REAR OF THE HOUSE. THE HOUSE IS ON A SLAB AND THE LEAKING OIL HAD SUNK INTO THE GRAVEL AT THE EDGE OF THE PAD. THE HOUSE IS ON A STEEP SLOPE AND THE GRADE PITCHES AWAY FROM THE ROADWAY AND AWAY FROM OTHER RESIDENCES. THE DRILLED WELL IS ABOUT 150' FEET AWAY AND ABOUT ON THE SAME CONTOUR. I DO NOT THINK THAT IT IS THREATENED. THERE WAS NO ODOR IN THE HOME. IMMEDIATELY BELOW THE SPILL SITE IS THE SEPTIC SYSTEM. SINCE EXCAVATING WOULD THREATEN TO UNDERMINE THE HOUSE AND DAMAGE OR DESTROY THE SEPTIC SYSTEM AND AS I FELT THAT THE WELL WAS NOT THREATENED, NO ACTION WAS TAKEN.

FERN WOOSTER OF THE MUD CREED RD IN HANCOCK CALLED TO REPORT THAT HER WATER HAD THE ODOR OF FUEL OIL.  SHE SUSPECTED THAT THE OIL HAD SOMETHING TO DO WITH THE COPPER LINE BENEATH THE CONCRETE BASEMENT FLOOR SINCE IT FAILED A PRESSURE CHECK.
