APPROXIMATELY 250 GALLONS OF #2 FUEL OIL SPILLED THOUGH A LEAK IN THE LIBRARY'S ABOVE GROUND TANK.  WHEN THE OIL WAS RELEASED IT IMMEDIATELY TRAVELED THOUGH BEDROCK FRACTURES WHERE IT REAPPEARED ABOUT 40 FEET DOWNSLOPE OUT OF AN EMBANKMENT ON THE DORNFIELD PROPERTY. CONTAMINATED SOIL WAS REMOVED AT THE BASE OF THE EMBANKMENT.  OIL WAS DIVERTED AWAY FROM THE DORNFIELD WELL WITH A 25' PIPE AND RECOVERY TRENCH. THE CONTAMINATED SOIL WAS STOCKPILED AND LANDSPREAD ON THE GOTT CONSTRUCTION PROPERTY.
EXCAVATION OF THREE 4000 GAL TANKS FROM FORMER TRENTON GENERAL STORE.

A TANK WITH AN 1 1/4" FILL AND A 3/4" VENT CANNOT BE SUCCESSFULLY FILLED WITH 200 GALLONS OF OIL, AT LEAST WHEN THE VENT IS TURNED DOWNWARD AND ICE BUILT UP AROUND THE END.

RONALD OVERLOCK, DRIVER FOR NEW ENGLAND HEATING, DISCOVERED THIS INCONTROVERTIBLE TRUTH ON THE MORNING OF 1/26/01.  HE SAID HE STOOD AT THE TRUCK AND WATCHED THE METER, SINCE THE TENANT HAD ONLY ORDERED 200 GALLONS OF FUEL.  (JUST BECAUSE A USER SAYS THE TANK WILL ACCEPT 200 GALLONS, DOESN'T MAKE IT SO.) AT OVERLOCK'S BEHEST, TENANT JOSEPH BROWN STATIONED HIMSELF AT THE FILL PIPE TO LISTEN FOR THE WHISTLE; HE SAID HE NEVER DID HEAR ONE AND AT THE 183 GALLON MARK, THE TANK END BLEW OUT. OVERLOCK SAID HE HEARD A LOUD BANG, AND STOPPED PUMPING; AT THE SAME TIME, MR. BROWN CAME RUNNING AROUND THE CORNER, SAYING THERE'D BEEN A LOUD BANG IN THE BASEMENT.

OVERLOCK ENTERED THE BASEMENT AND OBSERVED 3" OF OIL ON THE FLOOR; THE BOILER WAS AFIRE.  HE ORDERED THE OCCUPANTS TO CALL THE FIRE DEPT. AND TO VACATE THE BUILDING. THE BUILDING IS OWNED BY JERRY WOOD OF 8735 WEST RIVERWOOD DR., CRYSTAL RIVER FLORIDA 34428   (352) 795-8895.

THE FIRE DEPT. ARRIVED AND PUT OUT THE SMALL FIRE STILL REMAINING AT THE BOILER.  THERE WAS NOT MUCH OIL REMAINING ON THE CELLAR FLOOR, BUT THEY PUT DOWN SORBENT PADS TO RECOVER WHAT OIL THEY COULD.  THE DISCOVERY OF A FLOOR DRAIN LED THEM TO BELIEVE THAT THE OIL HAD DRAINED FROM THE BASEMENT THAT WAY; BECAUSE THE DRAIN EXITED TO DAYLIGHT NEAR THE RIVER, THE FIRE DEPT. NOTIFIED ME.  

PRIOR TO MY ARRIVAL, THE FIREFIGHTERS CLEARED THE SNOW AWAY FROM THE END OF THE FLOOR DRAIN;  THERE WAS OBVIOUSLY NO WHERE NEAR 220 GALLONS OF OIL THERE.  LIFTING THE COVER OFF THE DRILLED WELL AND SHINING A LIGHT DOWN THE SHAFT, IT APPEARED AS THOUGH A SHEEN WAS ON THE WATER COLUMN. A SAMPLER RUN DOWN THE WELL REVEALED 1/8" OF FRESH OIL ON THE WATER SURFACE.

ON OCTOBER 3, 1998  RESPONSE RECEIVED A CALL FROM THE LEWISTON FIRE DEPT. ABOUT AN OIL SPILL IN THE BASEMENT OF A RESIDENCE AT 143 MONTELLO ST.     APPARENTLY THERE HAD BEEN AN ONGOING LEAK FROM THE UNDERGROUND COPPER FUEL LINE TO THE FURNACE.  THE LINE HAD BEEN CHANGED AND THE LEAK STOPPED PRIOR TO THE NEW HOMEOWNERS BUYING THE HOME.  A MINIMUM OF 70 GALLONS OF OIL HAD SPILLED UNDER THE FLOOR AND WAS NOW SEEPING UP THROUGH CRACKS IN THE FLOOR AND FILLING UP THE BASEMENTS SUMP.  PETER EREMITA (TECH SERVICES) CONDUCTED INDOOR AIR SAMPLING.  FLOOR WAS REMOVED AND GALLONS OF FREE PRODUCT IN A COBBLE LINED PERIMETER DRAIN WERE VACTORED.  FLOOR WAS REPLACED.  NO FURTHER ACTION IS ANTICIPATED FOLLOWING ONE FINAL AIR SAMPLING ROUND.

ON APRIL 7,2001 AT 1050 WE RECEIVED A CALL FROM DAVID SHIBLES OF HARTLAND REPORTING A LEAK FROM HIS OUTSIDE KEROSENE TANK.  HE SAID THE FEEDLINE BROKE AT THE NIPPLE CONNECTION TO THE TANK AND SPILLED ABOUT 100 GALLONS OF FUEL.  HE HAS A DUG WELL WHICH IS ABOUT 100 FEET FROM THE SPILL.
      I ARRIVED ON SITE THAT AFTERNOON AND MET MR. & MRS. SHIBLES.  SOME OF THE OIL HAD FLOWED UNDER A CORNER OF THE TRAILER SO WE REMOVED THE TRAILER'S SKIRTING TO VENT THE FUMES FROM BENEATH THE TRAILER.  DUE TO THE PROXIMITY OF THE DUG WELL I DECIDED TO EXCAVATE AS MUCH SOIL AS POSSIBLE.  ON APRIL 10 I MET A REPRESENTATIVE OF AMES HOME CENTER FROM CANAAN AT THE SITE AND WE ARRANGED FOR EQUIPMENT TO DIG ON APRIL 12.  THE WORK PROCEEDED AS PLANNED AND WE EXCAVATED ABOUT TEN YARDS OF CONTAMINATED SOIL FROM THE SITE.  THE NATIVE SOIL WAS A GLACIAL TILL TYPE.  AMES HAULED THE SOIL TO THE WASTE MANAGEMENT LANDFILL IN NORRIDGEWOCK.
      I EXPLAINED THE INSURANCE FUND TO THE SHIBLES AND HAD THE FIRE MARSHAL'S OFFICE SEND THEM AN APPLICATION.  I ALSO PUT THE SHIBLE'S WELL ON THE QUARTERLY MONITORING PROGRAM.

CIRCA 1988 THE SORRENTO SULLIVAN EDUCATION RECREATION CENTER REMOVED THEIR UNDERGROUND OIL TANK AND INSTALLED A 1000 GALLON ABOVEGROUND TANK, IN A COVERED CONTAINMENT VESSEL,  SO THAT RAIN WATER, ICE AND SNOW COULDN'T BUILD UP INSIDE.  A VERY EFFECTIVE SET UP UNTIL JULY OF 2001, WHEN IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT THE CONTAINMENT STRUCTURE WOULDN'T HOLD OIL, BECAUSE THE GENIUS THAT BUILT IT HAD INSTALLED A VALVED DRAIN IN ONE END.  THE VALVE WAS LEFT OPEN.  FURTHER, THE INSPECTION PORTS AT EACH END OF THE COVER WERE PADLOCKED, AND NO ONE KNEW WHERE THE KEYS WERE.

ON OR ABOUT MONDAY, JULY 9, THERE WAS NO HOT WATER AT THE REC CENTER, SO IT WAS ASSUMED THE OIL TANK WAS EMPTY;  900 FRESH GALLONS WERE DELIVERED.  ON WEDNESDAY THE TANK WAS EMPTY AGAIN. 

SHEENS HAD BEEN REPORTED ON TAUNTON BAY, STARTING SATURDAY, JULY 7, (SEE B-386-01). NO SOURCE WAS IDENTIFIED BY US, THE COAST GUARD, MAINE DMR OR US FISH & WILDLIFE, UNTIL THE EVENING OF 7/11, WHEN A HEAVY CONCENTRATION OF FRESH OIL WAS NOTICED IN A DITCH NEXT TO THE SULLIVAN FIRE DEPT.  CHIEF JOE FONTAINE NOTIFIED THE DEP AND USCG. BY THE TIME I ARRIVED THERE ABOUT 2030, FIRE DEPT. PERSONNEL HAD IDENTIFIED THE SOURCE AS THE TANK AT THE RECREATION CENTER.

THE REASON THE SOURCE HAD NOT BEEN IDENTIFIED EARLIER WAS THAT THE OIL, LEAKING OUT OF THE TANK, EXITED THE CONTAINMENT STRUCTURE THROUGH THE VALVE AND SANK IMMEDIATELY INTO THE GRAVEL.  VERY LITTLE STAINING WAS EVIDENT.   ONCE IN THE SOIL, THE OIL WAS PICKED UP BY THE BUILDING'S PERIMETER DRAIN, AND CONDUCTED TO THE DRAINAGE DITCH WEST OF THE BUILDING AND THEN TO TIDEWATER.   BECAUSE OF THE SUMMER DROUGHT, THE OIL DIDN'T MOVE DOWN THE DITCH VERY FAST, BEING HELD IN THE DITCH POOLS TEMPORARILY.  ONCE AT TIDEWATER, THE OIL POOLED UP, AWAITING THE HIGH TIDE TO TAKE IT AWAY. THE SHEEN ON THE BAY COULDN'T BE TRACED BACK TO A SOURCE, BECAUSE THE FALLING TIDE LEFT NO CONNECTION BETWEEN SHEEN AND SOURCE.

AT ABOUT 2100, I SUMMONED A CREW FROM CLEAN HARBORS, TO DEPLOY A CONTAINMENT BOOM AND WORK THROUGH THE NIGHT SOAKING UP OIL.  AT THAT TIME, I NOTIFIED SETH BARKER OF THE DMR.

LT. MARCEL MUISE OF THE COAST GUARD MSD, IN BUCKSPORT, ARRIVED ABOUT 2130, AND HE CONCURRED WITH MY ACTION PLAN.  BY THAT TIME, THE FIRE DEPT. PERSONNEL HAD THE SPILL UNDER CONTROL.

CLEAN HARBORS WORKED THE REST OF THE WEEK ON THE SPILL.  ON 7/14, THE ENDS OF THE PERIMETER DRAIN PIPES WERE EXPOSED AND CONTAMINATED FILL DUG OUT AROUND THEM.  THE TANK WAS REMOVED FROM THE CONTAINMENT VESSEL AND A CORROSION HOLE DISCOVERED IN THE BOTTOM.  AT THAT TIME, THE DRAIN INSIDE THE CONTAINMENT STRUCTURE WAS DOCUMENTED.

THE FOLLOWING WEEK, CONTAMINATED FILL WAS REMOVED FROM UNDER THE TANK LOCATION, AND TWO RECOVERY WELLS INSTALLED TO COLLECT OIL.  AS OF THE END OF AUGUST, 2001, TEST WELLS HAVE BEEN INSTALLED AND BORINGS HAVE BEEN DONE TO TRY AND LOCATE ANY PLUME OF OIL IN THE GROUND.  SUMMIT ENVIRONMENTAL (795-6009), OF LEWISTON, WILL NEXT BORE HOLES THROUGH THE BASEMENT FLOOR, AND INSTALL A PUMP AND TREAT SYSTEM AT THE DOWN GRADIENT RECOVERY WELL.

MRS. O¿NEILL FOUND OUT THAT THE NIPPLE ATTACHING THE FILTER TO HER OUTSIDE HORIZONTAL 275 AST HAD BROKEN UNDER THE LOAD OF SNOW AND ICE. THE MILFORD FIRE DEPT. WAS CALLED ABOUT 05:00, BUT THEY FOUND LITTLE OIL TO COLLECT. THEY ATTEMPTED TO CONTACT ME THROUGH THE STATE POLICE DISPATCH WHO FAILED TO DO SO. MRS. O¿NEILL THEN REACHED ME AT THE OFFICE ABOUT 0830. I WENT TO THE ADDRESS AND LEARNED THAT WHEN SHE FIRST LOST HEAT SHE CALLED HER OIL COMPANY, MALENFANT FUEL, WHO PUT 100 GALLONS INTO THE TANK. ON THE NEXT MORNING SHE WAS OUT AGAIN, MRS. O¿NEILL ESTIMATES THAT AT A MINIMUM THAT 250 GALLONS WAS LOST. DUE TO THIS WINTER¿S SNOW COVER, THE GROUND IS NOT FROZEN AND THERE WAS NO FREE PRODUCT TO COLLECT AT THAT TIME. HOWEVER THERE WAS AN ODOR PROBLEM INSIDE. MRS. O¿NEILL¿S MOTHER, BARBARA JEWERS, LIVES THERE ALSO. WE DISCUSSED THE EFFECTS OF THE VAPORS AND I RECOMMENDED THAT MRS. JEWERS NOT STAY THERE UNTIL WE COULD CONTROL THE VAPORS. SHE HAS REFUSED TO GO. 
   THE HOME IS A CONVENTIONAL MOBILE HOME ON A SLAB CONNECTED TO A MODULAR HOME ON A FROST WALL. I FOUND OIL STAINED SOIL UNDER THE MODULAR ADDITION AND FREE PRODUCT ON WATER IN AN OPENING IN THE SLAB (IT PROVIDES A PLACE FOR THE TOWN WATER AND SEWER LINES TO PENETRATE THE SLAB). I RECOVERED ABOUT A QUART FROM THIS HOLE. ON THE AFTERNOON OF 3/24/01 TECHNICAL SERVICES INSTALLED A VENT SYSTEM OVER THE SOIL AND COVERED THE SLAB¿S HOLE IN ORDER TO CONTROL THE VAPORS. THIS WAS ONLY PARTIALLY SUCCESSFUL AT FIRST. MRS. JEWER IS NOT BOTHERED BY VAPORS ON THE MODULAR UNIT SIDE BUT THEY CONTINUED TO BE A PROBLEM (HEADACHE) FOR MRS. O¿NEILL. ON THE EVENING OF 3/24/01 THE VAPOR LEVELS WERE AROUND 10 PPM (BY PID WITH A 225 SET POINT). THE VENT SYSTEM EXHAUST WAS AT 300 PPM. ON 3/26 THE EXHAUST WAS DOWN TO 100 PPM, BUT MRS. O¿NEILL WAS STILL BEING BOTHERED OCCASIONALLY BY VAPORS EVEN THOUGH THE PID FOUND NOTHING.
   BY 3/25/01 OIL BEGAN TO BREAK OUT IN THE ROAD DITCH. THE OIL WAS NOT COMING FROM A DRAIN, BUT WAS FLOWING ACROSS A LAYER OF CLAY THAT IS THE NATURAL SOIL OF THIS AREA. A KNOWLEDGEABLE NEIGHBOR SAYS THAT ABOUT 2 FEET OF FILL WAS BROUGHT IN TO RAISE THE SUBDIVISION¿S LOTS ABOVE THE WATER TABLE. DUE TO THE UNSEASONABLY COOL MARCH WEATHER THE OIL IS MIGRATING AT A SLOW RATE. I WILL MAINTAIN SORBENT MATERIALS IN THE DITCH.
   THE SPRING TURNED OUT TO BE VERY DRY AND WE DIDN¿T RECEIVE THE FLUSHING RAINS THAT USUAL. DUE TO THIS WE WERE NOT ABLE TO COLLECT MUCH THROUGH SORBENTS. THROUGHOUT THE SUMMER AND FALL THE SOIL VENTING SYSTEM CONTINUED TO REMOVE OIL. I HAVE ATTACHED A LIST SHOWING THE VAPOR LEVEL IN THE EXHAUST OVER TIME. I EXPLAINED WHAT WAS HAPPENING TO MRS. O¿NEILL AND GAVE HER THE OPTIONS TO ATTEMPT TO EXCAVATE OR ALLOW THE VENT SYSTEM TO CLEAN THE SITE. BY THEN SHE WAS RARELY BOTHERED BY OIL AND ELECTED NOT TO DIG. THE INTENT IS TO CONTINUE VENTING UNTIL THE EXHAUST IS CLEAN. THIS SHOULD BE DONE SOMETIME IN THE YEAR 2002.

ON 3/16/01, 1600 HOURS ED LABLANC OF ROY BROS. REPORTED AN UNDER THE CEMENT FLOOR LINE LEAK AT A HOUSE BELONGING TO CAROL FLANIGAN.  I WENT TO THE SITE AT THE TIME OF THE REPORT AND OBSERVED THAT THERE WAS SOME OIL SEEPING UP THROUGH THE CEMENT FLOOR.  THE BASEMENT SPACE GAVE A PID READING OF 6PPM.  ED SAID THAT HE WOULD DEPLOY SOME SPEEDY DRY.  MY PLAN WAS TO CONTACT CAROL AND DISCUSS OPTIONS FOR DEALING WITH THE SITUATION.  IT DID NOT APPEAR TO BE MUCH OF A PROBLEM AT THE TIME.  HOWEVER, A FEW DAYS AFTER, A LOT OF FREE PRODUCT WAS COMING THROUGH THE FLOOR AND THERE WAS A GALLON OR SO OF PURE FUEL IN THE BOTTOM OF THE CHIMNEY.  THE CHIMNEY HAD BEEN INSTALLED BEFORE THE CEMENT FLOOR HAD BEEN PUT DOWN SO THE GROUNDWATER PUSHED THE OIL INTO THIS SPACE.  THE PLAN CHANGED TO HAVING CLEAN HARBORS TAKE UP SOME FLOOR AND RECOVER PRODUCT.  A REVIEW OF FUEL USAGE FIGURES INDICATED THAT THERE WAS ABOUT 600 GALLONS AT LARGE.  THE PROCEDURE REVEALED THAT A LARGE PORTION OF THE SPILL HAD BEEN DRAINED TO THE SEWER BY AN UNDER THE FLOOR SEWER PIPE.  IT TURNED OUT THAT THEY HAD BEEN REALIZING FUEL ODORS AT THE TREATMENT PLANT FOR ABOUT A WEEK.  FORTUNATELY, THEY DID NOT FEEL THAT ANY DAMAGE HAD HAPPENED TO THE PLANT.  WE REMOVED ABOUT 169 FT2 OF FLOOR, WHICH WILL HAVE TO BE REPLACED.  TECH SERVICE (MSSRS LAVOIE & SELLECK) HAVE INSTALLED A POSITIVE VENTILATION SYSTEM.  HOPEFULLY THERE WILL NOT BE AN ODOR PROBLEM WHEN WE ARE FINISHED.  AN AST FUND APPLICATION REQUEST HAS BEEN SENT TO THE FIRE MARSHAL'S OFFICE.

SOME TIME BEFORE 1/13/99 CARLTON PINNEY OF PENQUIS CAP CONTACTED THIS OFFICE REGARDING A POTENTIALLY HYDROCARBON CONTAMINATED WELL AT THE RESIDENCE OF IRENE VAZQUES IN DEXTER.  (483 N. DEXTER ROAD)  I ASKED IF HE HAD AN ANALYSIS THAT WAS POSITIVE FOR HYDROCARBON AND HE SAID THAT HE DIDN'T.  WE DISCUSSED THE PROCEDURE AND ON 1/13/99 HE CALLED TO SAY THAT HE HAD A POSITIVE TEST.  I ORDERED FILTERS THAT DAY.

THE PROPERTY IS AN OLD FARM AND HAD BEEN USED AS SUCH FOR DECADES.  ACCORDING TO CARLTON THERE ARE NO SIGNS OF USTS, WHICH SOME OLD FARM FACILITIES HAVE HAD.  THE CASE IS BEING REFERRED TO TECH SERVICE.

ON JUNE 20, 2001, THE DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION (DEPARTMENT) RECEIVED A COMPLAINT FROM MS. JEAN GUIDI REGARDING THE DISCHARGE OF GASOLINE AT JORDAN¿S AUTO JUNKYARD, LOCATED ON 18 SNELL HILL ROAD, IN TURNER, MAINE.  THE JUNKYARD, ALONG WITH A TOWING SERVICE, IS OWNED AND OPERATED BY MR. EUGENE JORDAN.  
ON JULY 10, 2001, JON ANDREWS, OF THE DEPARTMENT, TRAVELED TO JORDAN'S JUNKYARD IN AN ATTEMPT TO INVESTIGATE THE PROPERTY.  HE CONTACTED MR. JORDAN BY PHONE AND WAS REFUSED ACCESS TO THE JUNKYARD.  MR. ANDREWS DID NOTE THE PRESENCE OF AN ONGOING OIL RELEASE FROM A SMALL TRAILER AS WELL AS AREAS OF OIL STAINED SOIL THROUGHOUT THE PROPERTY.  
ON JULY 24, 2001, JON ANDREWS CONDUCTED AN INSPECTION OF THE JORDAN JUNKYARD.  THE DEPARTMENT NOTED THAT SOIL GRADING WAS IN PROCESS AT THE SITE AND SEVERAL AREAS OF RECENTLY GRADED SOIL WERE OBSERVED.  THE TRAILER RELEASING OIL TO THE GROUND ON JULY 10, WAS NOW COVERED BY A TARP AND NO STAINING WAS EVIDENT.  THE DEPARTMENT OBSERVED SEVERAL OTHER LOCATIONS EXHIBITING STAINED SOIL, WITH A PARTICULAR CONCENTRATION AROUND THE GARAGE MR. JORDAN USES TO DISMANTLE AUTOMOBILES.  STAINING APPEARED TO BE THE RESULT OF THE SPILLING OF VARIOUS VEHICLE FLUIDS.  SEVERAL HUNDRED WRECKED VEHICLES WERE STORED ON THE PROPERTY AND NO EVIDENCE OF LARGE SCALE WASTE SPILLING OR DUMPING WAS OBSERVED.  MR. JORDAN CLAIMED THAT VEHICLE FLUIDS WERE TYPICALLY COLLECTED FOR RE-USE, OR MADE AVAILABLE FOR THOSE WHO WANTED THEM.
THE DEPARTMENT COLLECTED A WATER SAMPLE FROM THE JORDAN'S ON-SITE DUG WATER SUPPLY WELL, FOR ANALYSIS OF DIESEL RANGE ORGANICS (DRO), GASOLINE RANGE ORGANICS (GRO), AND METHYL TERTIARY BUTYL ETHER (MTBE).  LABORATORY RESULTS INDICATED MTBE AT A CONCENTRATION OF APPROXIMATELY 100 MICRO GRAMS PER LITER (UG/L), BENZENE, ETHYLBENZENE AND TOLUENE CONCENTRATIONS OF APPROXIMATELY 1 UG/L RESPECTIVELY, AND A DRO CONCENTRATION OF 335 UG/L.  A WATER SAMPLE WAS SUBSEQUENTLY COLLECTED FROM THE GUIDI WATER SUPPLY WELL LOCATED APPROXIMATELY

MARY WILKERSON, RESIDENT ON THE OLD COUNTY ROAD IN WEST ENFIELD, CALLED TO REPORT THAT HER WATER HAD AN ODOR THAT WAS BELIEVED TO BE KEROSENE.  IT WAS ALSO STATED THAT SHE LOST SOME OIL FROM THE LINE ON HER HEATING OIL SYSTEM.  INVESTIGATING THE SITUATION I FOUND SOME STAINING AND DEAD GRASS ASSOCIATED WITH THE SPILL.  IT WAS NOT BELIEVED THAT VERY MUCH OIL HAD BEEN DISCHARGED.  THE WELL TO THE RESIDENCE IS LOCATED ONLY A FEW FEET FROM THE SPILL AREA.  THE WELL WAS ALSO A "DUG VARIETY" TYPE WELL MAKING IT SUSCEPTIBLE TO MINOR SPILLAGE.  DIESEL RANGE ORGANIC CONCENTRATIONS IN THE WATER WERE FAIRLY LOW AT 107 PPB.  MS. WILKERSON HAS SINCE BEEN PROVIDED WITH A CHARCOAL FILTER SYSTEM AND PLACED ON THE QUARTERLY MONITORING PROGRAM. IT IS BELIEVED THAT DRO CONCENTRATIONS WILL DECREASE OVER TIME.   AST FUND COVERAGE IS PENDING.

MRS. DOW CALLED TO REPORT OIL CONTAMINATION IN HER WELL. SHE HAD JUST RECEIVED THE RESULTS OF A WATER TEST DONE ON HER WATER ON 10/08/96 BY THE OIL COMPANY, ROY BROS. OIL COMPANY. IT SEEMS THAT THE COMPANY WORK ON HER OIL SYSTEM THE YEAR BEFORE, 10/30/95, AND FOLLOWING THAT SHE BEGAN TO SMELL OIL. THIS IS AN OUTSIDE 275 GALLON OIL TANK WITHIN AN ENCLOSURE. THE COMPANY REPLACED A BROKEN VALVE. WHEN THE TANK WAS FILLED THAT FALL, IT TOOK AN UNUSUALLY LARGE AMOUNT OF OIL, 211 GALLONS. WHEN SHE QUERIED THE COMPANY, THEY TOLD HER IT WAS DUE TO THE PREVIOUS COLD SPRING. THE FOLLOWING FALL THE TANK ACCEPTED 31 GALLONS. SHE BECAME MORE CONCERNED AND THROUGH HER INSISTENCE THE COMPANY SAMPLED THE WELL WATER. ALTHOUGH THE LAB REPORTED A DRO OF 40 PPB (54 PPB TOTAL HYDROCARBONS)(SEE ATTACHED REPORT) TO ROY BROS. OIL ON 10/15/96, MRS. DOW REPORTS THAT SHE WAS TOLD OVER THE PHONE THAT THE RESULTS WERE O.K. MRS. DOW ASKED TO SEE THE RESULTS, WHICH SHE DID NOT RECEIVE UNTIL MAY OF 1997. SHE CONTACTED ME AND I INVESTIGATED AND RESAMPLED THE WELL 5/27/97 WITH A RESULT OF LESS THAN THE DETECTION LIMIT. I DISCUSSED THE CASE WITH PHIL FINLEY OF ROY BROTHERS. I WAS CONCERNED THAT THEY HAD NOT INFORMED MRS. DOW OR THE DEPT. IMMEDIATELY AFTER LEARNING ON THE CONTAMINATED WELL. HE REPLIED THAT SINCE IT APPEARED TO BE BELOW THE DRINKING WATER STANDARD OF 50 PPB HE THOUGHT IT WAS SAFE TO USE AND NEED NOT BE REPORTED. I INFORMED HIM THAT ANY EVIDENCE OF CONTAMINATION WAS EVIDENCE OF A SPILL AND MUST BE REPORTED. IN ANY CASE ROY BROTHERS HAS ACCEPTED THE TASK OF PAYING FOR THE QUARTERLY MONITORING OF THE DOW WELL. THE LAST SAMPLE THAT I HAVE RECEIVED, 9/2/97, SHOWED BELOW DETECTION. AS LONG AS IT REMAINS SO NO FURTHER ACTION IS ANTICIPATED. 
   A SAMPLE TAKEN 12/10/97 REPORTED BACK AS 40 PPB OF DRO. MRS. DOW AND MR. FINLEY WERE ADVISED. TO CONFIRM THIS ANOTHER SAMPLE WAS TAKEN ON 1/6/98 BY TECH SERVICE AID, JIM LAVOIE. ON 1/16 IT REPORTED BACK AT74 PPB. AGAIN I SPOKE WITH MRS. DOW AND MR. FINLEY. ROYBROS./WEBBER OIL AGREED TO INSTALL AN ACTIVATED CHARCOAL SYSTEM AT THE DOW RESIDENCE. MRS. DOW BECAME CONCERNED ABOUT POSSIBLE LOSS OF PROPERTY VALUES AND I CONTACTED THIRD PARTY DAMAGE CLAIMS SO THEY COULD ADVISE MRS. DOW. AT THE PRESENT (4/7/98) THE DOW RESDENCE IS ON FILTERED WATER WITH THE COST BEING BORN BY THE OIL COMPANY.

R.H.FOSTER CO. CALLED TO REPORT THAT THEIR BURNERMAN, TONY NOWELL, WAS AT THE CINDY SMITH RESIDENCE, 10 GROVE ST., KENDUSKEAG, 207-884-6045, AND HAD FOUND THAT THE FUEL LINE FROM THE CELLAR AST TO THE WATER HEATER HAD SPRUNG A LEAK. THE HOME HAS ITS OWN WELL. I WENT TO THE SITE AND MET MR. NEWELL AND MS. SMITH. THE BARE COPPER LINE WAS BURIED IN THE DIRT FLOOR AND CORROSION HAD CAUSED A LEAK. MS. SMITH BELIEVES THAT AT LEAST 200 GALLONS OF #2 WAS LOST. THIS COMES FROM REVIEWING PAST TANK FILL RATES AND IS PROBABLY CONSERVATIVE. THE HOUSE IS AT THE TOP OF A SMALL HILL ON A MAPPED SAND AND GRAVEL AQUIFER IN A CLUSTER OF HOMES ALL ON THEIR OWN WELLS. THE HOME'S CELLAR IS SANDY GRAVEL. MS. SMITH SAYS THAT THEY DID NOT YET SMELL IN THE WELL WATER.
   I TOOK A WATER SAMPLE FROM THE KITCHEN SINK AND IT LATER CAME BACK 76 PPB OF A HEAVY WEIGHT PETROLEUM. A SAMPLE TAKEN BY TECH SERVICES A WEEK LATER CAME BACK NONDETECT.
   THERE WAS LITTLE FUEL ODOR IN THE HOUSE. MS. SMITH AND HER NINE YEAR OLD DAUGHTER HAVE NOT NOTICED ANY HEALTH SYMPTOMS THAT MIGHT BE ASSOCIATED WITH OIL VAPORS.
   BECAUSE OF THE SANDY GRAVEL AND PROXIMITY OF THE SPILL TO THE NATIVE STONE WALL I DID NOT THINK THAT EXCAVATION WAS THE BEST RESPONSE. OUR ENGINEER, ROBERT SYPITKOWSKI, AGREED AND INSTALLED A SOIL VENTING SYSTEM THAT WILL REMOVE SOME CONTAMINATION THROUGH EVAPORATION AND ALSO PREVENT VAPORS FROM CAUSING PROBLEMS.
   ON THE NEXT DAY I RETURNED TO THE SITE WITH PAUL BLOOD OUR GEOLOGIST AND MET WITH MS. SMITH AND HER FATHER, DON BROWN, WHO IS THE ACTUAL OWNER. I EXPLAINED THE AST INSURANCE FUND TO THEM BOTH.
   AFTER THIS VISIT TECHNICAL SERVICES HAS TAKE OVER THE CASE AND SAMPLED ABUTTING WELLS. THE SAMPLES DID NOT INDICATE OIL CONTAMINATION. FOR FURTHER INFORMATION I RECOMMEND REVIEW OF TECH SERVICES RECORDS.

B-145-01   BANGOR   CHAD WHITE RESIDENCE   140 GALLONS #1 LOST FROM OUTSIDE AST DUE TO SNOW 


WEBBER OIL CO. CALLED TO REPORT THAT A CUSTOMER, CHAD WHITE, HAD SUFFERED AN OIL SPILL AT HIS RESIDENCE AT 19 NAYLOR STREET IN BANGOR. THEY HAD A CREW ON SITE. I WENT TO THE SCENE AND LEARNED THAT A BUILD UP OF SNOW AND ICE HAD BROKEN A NIPPLE BETWEEN THE OUTSIDE AST AND ITS FILTER. THEY WERE ESTIMATING A LOSS OF ABOUT 140 GALLONS OF #1 FUEL. THIS NEIGHBORHOOD IS KNOWN AS BANGOR GARDENS AND IS FAMILIAR TO D.E.P. RESPONSE. THE SOIL IS TIGHT CLAY AND THE EX-MILITARY HOUSES ARE BUILT ON 8 FOOT FROST WALLS. FUEL OIL HAD FOUND ITS WAY AROUND THE EAST SIDE OF THE HOUSE AND OUT INTO THE STREET. WEBBER PERSONNEL HAD USED SORBENT PADS TO COLLECT THE OIL THAT WAS EXPOSED. DUE TO THE HEAVY SNOW COVER, THE GROUND AROUND THE HOUSE¿S FROST WALL IS UNFROZEN AND THE OIL HAD MADE ITS WAY INTO THE GRAVEL BACKFILL. HOWEVER THE HIGH WATER TABLE PREVENTED MUCH PENETRATION. BECAUSE THE GRAVEL IS SO CLOSE TO THE HOUSE THE USE OF HEAVY EQUIPMENT IS PRECLUDED AND I ELECTED TO KEEP SORBENTS IN THE RUN OFF AREAS TO COLLECT THAT OIL FORCED OUT BY MELTING SNOW. ON THE FIRST DAY MR. WHITE FOUND LITTLE ODOR IN THE HOUSE BUT TWO DAYS LATER HE REPORTED THAT THE SMELL OF FUEL WAS QUITE STRONG INSIDE. I FOUND THAT OIL HAD FOUND ITS WAY UNDER AN ATTACHED FAMILY ROOM. THIS AREA WAS DRAINED BY A SUMP PUMP, WHICH PUMPED OUT A COUPLE OF QUARTS OF OIL ALONG WITH 50 GALLONS OF WATER WHEN TURNED ON. OUR TECHNICAL SERVICES DIVISION INSTALLED A VENT SYSTEM (ALONG WITH CLOSING OFF AN OPENING UNDER THE KITCHEN CABINETS THAT WAS ALLOWING AIR FROM THE FAMILY ROOM FROST WALL INTO THE MAIN HOUSE) THAT DAY (3/26/01). ON 3/26 I USED A PID TO MONITOR THE INSIDE HOUSE AIR AND GOT LEVELS OF ABOUT 10 PPM. THE WHITES HAVE A YOUNG DAUGHTER, ABOUT 7, WHO SLEEPS ON THE OPPOSITE END OF THE HOUSE. HE SAID THAT SHE WOULD SPEND THE WEEK WITH NEARBY FAMILY.
   I SPOKE WITH MR. WHITE ON 3/27 AND HE FELT THAT THE ODORS WERE ABOUT THE SAME. I ADVISED HIM THAT WE WOULD CONTINUE TO MONITOR THE LEVELS BUT EXPECTED THAT IT WOULD BE MUCH BETTER IN A FEW WEEKS. BY 4/20/01 THE PID COULD NOT DETECT ANY ODORS IN THE RESIDENCE INCLUDING THE ATTACHED FAMILY ROOM. I OFFERED TO HAVE AN INDOOR AIR TEST DONE BUT HE DECLINED. WE LEFT THE VENT SYSTEM IN OPERATION AND WILL CONTINUE TO MONITOR THE EMISSIONS UNTIL 0.0 IS REACHED.

I RECEIVED A PHONE CALL FROM LEANNE CUPP OF THE FOREMOST INSURANCE COMPANY INFORMING ME THAT A CLIENT, ROBERT RIDEOUT, HAD SUFFERED A FIRE AT HIS MOBILE HOME IN BRADFORD ON 12/14/1999. HE HAD TOLD HER THAT HE HAD LOST ABOUT 500 GALLONS OF #1 FUEL OIL WHEN THE FURNACE FELL THROUGH THE FLOOR CAUSING THE DELIVERY LINE TO BREAK.
   I REACHED MR. RIDEOUT AT THE TELEPHONE NUMBER GIVEN ME AND MADE ARRAIGNMENTS TO MEET HIM AT THE SITE. THE TRAILER HOME IS LOCATED ABOUT .3 OF A MILE DOWN THE ISHMUS ROAD WEST OF RT. 11. THIS IS A PRIVATE ROAD MAINTAINED BY MR. RIDEOUT.
   THERE WAS LITTLE LEFT OF THE TRAILER OTHER THAN THE METAL PARTS. FROM THE TWISTED STEEL IT IS APPARENT THAT A PORTION OF THE LEAKING OIL WAS BURNED IN THE FIRE. HE HAD TWO 275 ASTS HOOKED UP TOGETHER. SINCE THE ACCESS TO THE PROPERTY IS SO DIFFICULT HE HAD THE TWO TANKS INSTALLED AND FILLED BEFORE WINTER. MR. RIDEOUT WAS NOT HOME AT THE TIME OF THE FIRE AND THE CAUSE AND DURATION OF THE FIRE WAS NOT KNOWN. HE HAS A DRILLED WELL ABOUT 100' AWAY AND GENERALLY UPGRADE ALTHOUGH THE PITCH IS NOT VERY GREAT. ON THE SOUTH SIDE OF THE TRAILER IS A LAWN AREA THAT IS BISECTED BY A SMALL STREAM. MR. RIDEOUT RELATED THAT AFTER THE FIRE SOME OIL HAD RUN FROM UNDER THE TRAILER DEBRIS OUT ONTO THE LAWN HE HAD TRIED TO PREVENT IT FROM REACHING THE STREAM BY SETTING FIRE TO IT. ON THE DAY I WAS THERE, 1/10/1999, I COULD SEE A SMALL OIL STAIN/BURN SPOT ON THE GRASS NEXT TO THE GRAVEL PAD BUT NO FUEL WAS EVIDENT. I RETURNED ON 1/12/1999 THE MORNING AFTER A .5" RAINFALL AND I COULD NOT SEE THAT ANY FUEL HAD BEEN FLUSHED FROM THE GRAVEL.
   TO REMOVE ALL RISK, IT WAS MY POSITION THAT THE CONTAMINATED SOIL UNDER THE FURNACE AREA SHOULD BE REMOVED TO INSURE THAT THE WELL AND NEARBY BROOK, FORBES BROOK, ARE NOT IMPACTED. WHEN I LAST SPOKE WITH MR. RIDEOUT HE WAS WAITING TO HEAR IF THE INSURANCE COMPANY WAS GOING TO REIMBURSE HIM FOR HIS LOSS. THEY WERE WAITING FOR A FINAL REPORT FROM THE FIRE MARSHAL AND THEIR INSURANCE ADJUSTER. WINTER HAS SET IN NOW AND ACCESS WITH HEAVY EQUIPMENT WOULD BE DIFFICULT.
   THROUGH THE SPRING OF 2000 I RECEIVED NO WORD FROM MR. RIDEOUT AND I FOUND THAT HIS PHONE NUMBER HAD BEEN DISCONNECTED. ON 7/25/2000 I DROVE TO THE FIRE SITE AND FOUND THAT MR. RIDEOUT HAD MOVED ANOTHER TRAILER OVER THE SPOT WHERE THE FIRE OCCURRED. NOT ONLY DID THE NEW TRAILER OBSTRUCT THE SPOT WERE I THOUGHT TO EXCAVATE, THE UNDER GROUND UTILITIES HAD BEEN INSTALLED. I DISCUSSED THE SITUATION WITH MR. RIDEOUT WHO EXPLAINED THAT HE DIDN'T THINK THAT THERE WAS ANY PROBLEM FROM WHAT RESIDUAL KEROSENE REMAINED. THERE WAS NO EVIDENCE OF ANY NEW OIL HAVING WORKED FROM THE GRAVEL PAD AND VEGETATION WAS GROWING ON THE SPOT ON THE LAWN THAT HAD BEEN OIL STAINED AND BURNED. SINCE I BELIEVE THAT THE CHANCE OF OIL CONTAMINATING THE WELL OR BROOK ARE SMALL I HAVE DECIDED NOT TO REQUIRE THAT THE TRAILER BE MOVED AND I AM NOT REQUIRING ANY FURTHER ACTION.

ON 9/12/97, 1420 HOURS NORM GOGAN OF NORLANS WATER TREATMENT SERVICE, INC. REPORTED THAT HE HAD FOUND GASOLINE CONTAMINATION IN THE WATER AT THE BROOKSVILLE POST OFFICE.  HE SAID THAT HE COULD SMELL IT AND THAT ANALYSIS RESULTS WERE 65 PPB GRO WITH NO MTBE.  THE WELL SEEMS TO HAVE PROBLEMS WITH IRON, MANGANESE AND SEPTAGE.  THE ODOR FROM THIS WATER IS OVERWHELMING.  I SAMPLED THE WATER AND IT CAME BACK 120 PPB GRO.  NORM INDICATED THAT HE COULD TAKE CARE OF THE WELL WITH A SERIES OF SYSTEMS.  NAMELY: CHLORINATING, ION EXCHANGE AND CHARCOAL FILTRATION.  NORM ALSO SAID THAT HE HAD BEEN DEALING WITH THE POST OFFICE WELL FOR THE LAST 15 YEARS AND THERE HAS NOT BEEN INDICATIONS OF GASOLINE CONTAMINATION.  HIS PRIOR EXPERIENCE WITH THE WELL HAD INVOLVED DEMINERALIZATION.

THERE ARE TWO OTHER WELLS IN THE AREA.  BUCK'S HARBOR MARKET'S WELL IS ABOUT 30 FEET FROM THE CONTAMINATED WELL AND ONLY SLIGHTLY UP GRADE.  THE SECOND BELONGS TO BUCKS HARBOR INN (A BED AND BREAKFAST).  THIS IS OVER 150 FEET FROM THE POST OFFICE WELL.  BOTH OF THESE ARE CLEAN.  THE POST OFFICE AND THE MARKET WELL ARE ON QUARTERLY MONITORING.  I'VE ASKED THE BED AND BREAKFAST MANAGEMENT TO CONTACT ME IF THEIR WATER SHOWS SIGNS OF CONTAMINATION.  

MR. CONDON OF CONDON'S GARAGE (A FACILITY THAT IS ABOUT 300 FEET FROM THE POST OFFICE) SAID THAT HE HAD USTS THAT WERE REMOVED 15 YEARS AGO.  ALSO, ACCORDING TO MR. CONDON, THERE HAD BEEN USTS AT BUCK'S HARBOR MARKET AND THE POST OFFICE BUILDING-IT WASN'T ALWAYS A POST OFFICE.  SUPPOSEDLY THESE WERE ALSO REMOVED 15 YEARS AGO.  BED ROCK IS NOT FAR FROM GRADE IN THAT AREA.  A DISTINCTION THAT MIGHT BE APPLICABLE IS THE FACT THAT IN JUNE AND JULY SEPTIC LEACH FIELDS WERE DEVELOPED UP GRADE FROM THE POST OFFICE.  I WOULD GUESS THAT THIS ACCOUNTS FOR THE HIGH COLIFORM COUNT AND THE PUTRID ODOR THAT THE WATER HAS.  THE GRO MOST LIKELY EMANATED FROM ONE OF THE USTS THAT HAD BEEN CLOSE TO THE WELL (I.E. EITHER AT THE MARKET OR THE CURRENTLY POST OFFICE BUILDING).  PROVING WHICH ONE WOULD BE A DAUNTING TASK AND LOCATING THE OWNERS WOULD PROBABLY BE EVEN MORE DIFFICULT.  

THE OWNER OF THE BROOKSVILLE POST OFFICE IS KATHERINE BUTLER, P.O. BOX 252, BROOKSVILLE, ME 04617, 207-326-8324.  BUCK'S HARBOR MARKET, CORNFIELD HILL ROAD, 326-8683.  BUCK'S HARBOR INN: PETER & ANN EBELING, P.O. BOX 268, SOUTH BROOKSVILLE MAINE 04617, 207-326-0730.

THE SITE(S) THAT MAKE UP R-001-06 ARE AN EXTENSION OF PREVIOUS DEP SITES (B-416-93, B-476-98).  IN ADDITION TO THE INSURANCE FUND SITE (B-416-93) AND THE MYSTERY SPILL/WELL CONTAMINATION (B-476-98), DEP WAS AWARE OF MULTIPLE ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF GASOLINE CONTAMINATION, PRIMARILY FROM LONG ABANDONED/CLOSED GASOLINE STATIONS ALONG RT. 1.  VINTAGE AIR PHOTO'S IDENTIFIED 4 FORMER GAS STATIONS - NOW A LIBRARY, 2 APT./RESIDENTIAL BUILDINGS, AND A USED CAR BUSINESS.
	DEP DECIDED TO EXCAVATE CONTAMINATED SOILS FROM ALL OF THE POTENTIAL SOURCES UNDER ONE EFFORT, HENCE THE R NUMBER AS OPPOSED TO THE STANDARD SPILL NUMBER.
	PREVIOUSLY, DEP HAD REMOVED SEVERAL THOUSAND YARDS OF CONTAMINATED SOIL FROM 41 MAIN STREET/CILLEY'S USED CARS (FORMERLY A CITGO GAS STATION/SPILL #B-416-93).  THE GOAL FOR 2006 WAS TO CONTINUE MOVING ALONG RT. 1 AND REMOVE THE CONTAMINATED SOILS IDENTIFIED BY GEOPROBE AND/OR OTHER PREVIOUS WORK.
	WORK STARTED AT 40 MAIN STREET, NOW THE PRINCETON LIBRARY, BUT IT WAS A GASOLINE STATION IN THE 1960'S.  ACCORDING TO LOCAL OFFICIALS, THE TANK WAS REMOVED PRIOR TO THE TOWN ACQUIRING THE PROPERTY.  SOME OLD UST PIPING WAS FOUND ABOUT 2 FT. BELOW GRADE, AND WHERE THAT ENDED, CONTAMINATED SOIL BEGAN.  IN ALL, APPROXIMATELY 250 YDS³ WERE REMOVED FROM THIS LOCATION AND LANDSPREAD AT THE PRINCETON AIRPORT.
	FROM THERE, WE MOVED TO 29 MAIN STREET, CURRENTLY KNOWN AS JR. FISHER'S APT. BUILDING.  ACCORDING TO LOCAL HISTORY, THE PROPERTY WAS USED AS A GASOLINE STATION FROM THE 1940'S UNTIL SOMETIME IN THE 1960'S.  GEOPROBING HAD IDENTIFIED A SIGNIFICANT VOLUME OF CONTAMINATED SOIL.  AS WE EXCAVATED BETWEEN THE BUILDING AND ROADWAY, WE ENCOUNTERED HIGHLY CONTAMINATED SOIL, WHICH COULD BE SMELLED FROM QUITE A DISTANCE.  AS THE DIG PROGRESSED, WE CHASED CONTAMINATION UNDER BOTH LANES OF RT. 1.  APPROXIMATELY, 1,230 YDS³ WERE REMOVED FROM THIS LOCATION.
	NEXT WE MOVED TO 21 MAIN STREET CURRENTLY TNT USED AUTO SALES (ABANDONED).  AGAIN, GEOPROBE RESULTS HAD FOUND SIGNIFICANT CONTAMINATION.  ONE OF THE (OLDER) TRUCK DRIVERS REMEMBERED THIS PROPERTY BEING A GASOLINE STATION IN THE LATE 1950'S BEING RUN BY A MAN WITH NO LEGS IN A WHEELCHAIR, POSSIBLY NAMED GETCHELL OR GUPTIL, WHO DIED YEARS AGO.  NO TANKS OR PIPING WAS FOUND, BUT THE CONTAMINATED SOIL RAN ALONG RT. 1 AND DOWN DEPOT STREET FOR ABOUT 50 FT.  APPROXIMATELY 700 YDS³ WERE REMOVED FROM THIS LOCATION.
	THE FOURTH AND FINAL STOP OF THE CLEAN UP PRINCETON TOUR '06 WAS 51 MAIN STREET - NOW BAILEY APT. BUILDING, PREVIOUSLY A VIDEO STORE, AND PRIOR TO THAT A GASOLINE STATION THAT NO ONE REMEMBERED.
	APPROXIMATELY 360 YDS³ WERE REMOVED FROM THIS SITE.  AS WE PROCEEDED NORTHERLY ALONG RT. 1, WE RAN OUT OF CONTAMINATION PRIOR TO HITTING THE FOOTPRINT OF THE CILLEY'S GAS STATION EXCAVATION OF 2 YEARS AGO, INDICATING THAT THE SOIL REMOVED FROM THE 51 MAIN STREET SITE WAS PROBABLY NOT RELATED TO THE CILLEY'S SITE.
	AFTER THIS, WE WENT INTO SITE RESTORATION MODE, WITH THE BIG PIECE BEING REPAVING RT. 1.  BECAUSE WE HAD RIPPED UP MOST OF RT. 1 FROM MILL STREET TO DEPOT STREET (INCLUDING THE PREVIOUS EXCAVATION IN FROM OF CILLEYS), I APPROVED AN OVERLAY OF THE WHOLE SECTION, WHICH PLEASED DOT, THE TOWN, AND LOCAL DRIVERS IMMENSELY.
	THE NEXT PHASE OF R-001-06 IS THE POTENTIAL DEVELOPMENT OF A PUBLIC WATER SUPPLY, WHICH WILL BE DETERMINED DURING THE UPCOMING YEAR (2007).

DEP RECEIVED A REPORT THAT AN OIL SPILL HAD BEEN DISCOVERED AT THIS SMALL FIRE STATION.  IT TRANSPIRED THAT THE 275-GALLON AST AT THE STATION WAS FILLED ON 11/8.  THE FURNACE WAS SERVICED ON 11/13. ON 11/17, FIRE PERSONNEL NOTICED THAT THE FURNACE WAS NOT "FIRING" AND THAT OIL WAS ON THE CONCRETE FLOOR NEAR THE FURNACE.  THE SERVICING OIL COMPANY (KALLOCH) WAS CALLED IN AND DETERMINED THAT THE SAFETY SHUT-OFF CONTROLS HAD FAILED, FLOODING THE CHAMBER WITH OIL AT THE RATE OF 1.3 GAL/HR.  OIL FLOWED ACROSS THE FLOOR TO A 3" HOLE INTO SUBGRADE, AND ALSO UNDER THE WALL SILL.  THE TANK WAS NOW READING 1/2 FULL.  AT THIS POINT KALLOCH NOTICED ADDITIONAL PROBLEMS (HOLES IN THE HEAT EXCHANGER) WITH THE FURNACE AND REMOVED IT.  KALLOCH STAFF USED SORBENTS TO COLLECT SOME OF THE SPILLED OIL.  DEP WAS CONTACTED BY KALLOCH ON 11/22; BY THIS TIME OIL WAS EVIDENT ON A SMALL STREAM RUNNING BEHIND THE FIRE STATION.
SOME OIL WAS COLLECTED OVER THE NEXT SEVERAL MONTHS BY A VARIETY OF METHODS, THOUGH SOME OIL UNDOUBTEDLY REMAINS UNDERLYING THE FIRE STATION (THE DECISION WAS MADE NOT TO DEMOLISH THE BUILDING).  THE ARE IS IN A VILLAGE SETTING WITH SEVERAL PRIVATE WELLS WITHIN 1000'; A DEP GEOLOGIST (ALEX PUGH) WAS ASSIGNED.  NO WELLS HAVE BEEN IMPACTED AT THE TIME OF THIS WRITING (10/2003).  THE IMPACTED (DISSOLVED PHASE) STREAM FLOWS TO A POND USED FOR AGRICULTURAL PURPOSES; THIS SITUATION IS BEYOND DEP REGULATORY CONTROL.
REFERRALS WERE MADE TO DEP ENFORCEMENT/COMPLIANCE STAFF (DISCHARGE AND REPORTING VIOLATIONS) AND TO OSFB STAFF (INSTALLATION/SERVICING VIOLATIONS); IT IS UNKNOWN WHAT ACTIONS MAY HAVE BEEN PURSUED BY THESE UNITS, ATHOUGH AN OSFB INSPECTION TOOK PLACE ON 11/27/2002.  IT WAS EVENTUALLY DECIDED THAT THE TOWN WOULD BE HELD SOLELY LIABLE FOR THIS SPILL EVENT.

ON 5-16-00, JACK CARON CALLED TO REPORT THAT OVER THE WINTER HE HAD DISCOVERED HIS OIL TANK HAD LEAKED. HE WAS UNSURE HOW MUCH WAS LOST. THE WELL WAS WITHIN 15 FEET OF THE TANK. I HIRED A CLEANUP CONTRACTOR TO REMOVE AS MUCH CONTAMINATED SOIL AS POSSIBLE. IT WAS LATER DETERMINED THAT NOT ALL OIL COULD BE RETRIEVED THIS WAY BECAUSE IT HAD TRAVELLED BENEATH THE FOUNDATION OF THE HOUSE. A RECOVERY SYSTEM WAS PUT IN PLACE TO CAPTURE THE REMAINING OIL.

5/9/02, A TECHNICIAN WORKING FOR DEAD RIVER IDENTIFIED THE LEAK IN THE CELLAR WHEN THEY WENT ON A SERVICE CALL.

WHEN I ARRIVED, I FOUND A DIRT FLOOR CELLAR COVERED WITH 16" SLABS OF CEDAR AND HARD WOOD. THE OIL LINE CAME IN THRU AN OPEN WINDOW. AN IMPROPERLY INSTALLED SPLICE IN THE LINE WAS LEAKING.  AN AREA ABOUT 6 FEET IN DIAMETER WAS CONTAMINATED UNDER THE LEAK.

AFTER DISCUSSING THE SITUATION WITH THE OWNER, I CONTACTED A CONTRACTOR TO BEGIN THE CLEAN-UP. 

A VACTOR WAS USED TO REMOVE THE CONTAMINATED SOIL IN THE BASEMENT, BUT THE WATER TABLE WAS ABOUT 18 INCHES BELOW THE FLOOR LEVEL, AND THE FOUNDATION WAS IN POOR SHAPE, WHICH LIMITED HOW MUCH CONTAMINATION WE COULD REMOVE.

BEFORE THE EXCAVATION IN THE CELLAR WAS BACKFILLED, A SECTION OF PERFORATED 4 INCH PIPE WAS INSTALLED AND CONNECTED TO A SOLID PIPE THAT EXTENDS ABOVE THE ROOF. THE PIPE WAS COVERED WITH POLY SHEETS PRIOR TO BACKFILLING AND BRINGING THE CELLAR BACK TO GRADE.

ON 11/23/99 MAINE ENERGY INC. REPORTED AN AST OVERFILL THAT THEY HAD ON 11/16/99 AT THE RESIDENCE OF DIANE EAGAN, WHICH IS AT 232 LAKE SHORE DRIVE IN HOLDEN.  THE VENDER TRUCK WAS AROUND A CORNER FROM THE FILL TUBE AND THE TANK FILLED UP BEFORE IT HAD TAKEN AS MUCH FUEL AS IT WAS SCHEDULED TO TAKE.  CONSEQUENTLY ABOUT TEN GALLONS OF PRODUCT CAME SPRAYING OUT OF THE VENT BEFORE THE DRIVER KNEW WHAT WAS HAPPENING.  A LOT OF THE SPILL LANDED ON OUTDOOR CARPET THAT COVERED A DECK THAT WAS NEXT TO THE FUEL TANK.  SOME OF THE SPILL LANDED IN SOIL THAT WAS NEXT TO THE PAD THAT THE TANK WAS ON, AND SOME OF THE PRODUCT WENT THROUGH THE DECK INTO THE SOIL UNDER IT.  MAINE ENERGY INC. HAD REMOVED 2.5 FT3 OF SOIL FROM THIS AREA NEXT TO THE PAD AND THIS AREA WAS RELATIVELY CLEAN.  MAINE ENERGY TOOK CARE OF THE OIL SOAKED CARPET.  THEY ALSO REPLACED THE AST BECAUSE THE OVERFILL HAD SLIGHTLY DEFORMED THE TANK ENDS, WHICH MIGHT POSSIBLY LEAD TO A CATACLYSMIC SPILL LATER ON.  THE WELL IS ABOUT 30 FEET FROM THE TANK SO A THOROUGH INVESTIGATION WAS NECESSARY.

ON 12/22/99 MAINE ENERGY HAD THE DECK REMOVED AND WE FOUND THAT THE SOIL UNDER IT WAS FAIRLY CONTAMINATED GIVING BAG HEAD SPACE READINGS OF UP TO 900 PPM.  HOWEVER, WE ALSO FOUND THAT THE SURFACE AQUIFER WAS LESS THAN THREE FEET FROM GRADE- A FACT THAT WOULD FURNISH PROTECTION TO THE BED ROCK AQUIFER.  FURTHER MORE THIS AQUIFER SLANTS STEEPLY TOWARDS BREWER LAKE AND THE WELL IS UPGRADE FROM THE SPILL.  THE WELL IS 160 FEET DEEP WITH 20 FEET OF CASING, WHICH MEANS THAT THERE IS AT LEAST 16 FEET OF SATURATED OVERBURDEN.  THE RELATIVELY HIGH HEAD-SPACE READINGS WERE PROBABLY DUE TO THE HIGHLY ORGANIC NATURE OF THE SOIL.  THIS TYPE OF SOIL HAS A HIGH AFFINITY FOR OIL SO ANY AMOUNT THAT CAME THROUGH THE DECK WOULD BE SUBSTANTIVE TO THE SOIL INSTEAD OF EVAPORATING.

THE PLAN IS TO PUT THE WELL ON QUARTERLY MONITORING.  IT IS CONCEIVABLE THAT DIGGING INTO THE SATURATED ZONE COULD DO MORE HARM THAN GOOD.  WHEN I TALKED TO DIANE ABOUT QM AND THE SURFICIAL GROUND WATER SHE SAID THAT HER PROPERTY HAS GROUND WATER SEEPS EVEN DURING DRY SEASONS.

properties.SUMMARY: SEE RECORD #9723.

ON 4/7/00, 1515 HOURS THIS DEPARTMENT WAS ADVISED OF A CONTAMINATED WELL IN HANCOCK.  THE PROPERTY IS A RENTAL FACILITY THAT BELONGS TO KAREN AND RONALD THOMAS.  IT IS LOCATED AT THE INTERSECTION OF ROUTES 1 AND 182.  THE BUILDING IS NOT FAR FROM THE TIDEWAY MARKET, WHICH IS A FACILITY THAT HAS MARKETED MOTOR FUEL FOR SEVERAL DECADES.  KAREN HAD AN ANALYSIS FROM BINAX/NEL THAT INDICATED 67PPB DRO.  ADDITIONALLY, THE ANALYSIS SUGGESTED THAT THE CONTAMINANT MIGHT BE GASOLINE.  A GRO ANALYSIS REVEALED 40 PPB GRO, 4.6 PPB MTBE, 1 PPB BENZENE, <1PPB ETHYL BENZENE.  THIS PROFILE SUGGESTS A LOT OF SMALL SURFACE SPILLS RATHER THAN A RELEASE FROM A UST.  OUR PAUL BLOOD SAID THAT WHEN CONTAMINATION COMES FROM AN UNDERGROUND SOURCE THE CONCENTRATION OF THE GRO CONSTITUENTS (E.G. MTBE, BENZENE, ETC.) ADD UP TO THE GRO CONCENTRATION, THE SOURCE IS UNDERGROUND.  CONVERSELY, WHEN IT DOESN'T THE SOURCE IS FROM SURFACE SPILLS.  FILTERS AND QM HAVE BEEN ARRANGED.

 ON 10/16/01 RAY MURPHY, WHO SCULPTS LOGS WITH A CHAIN SAW ON ROUTE 1 IN HANCOCK, REPORTED THAT HE HAD SEVERAL FEET OF OIL IN A WELL AT HIS HANCOCK PROPERTY.  ON THE FOLLOWING DAY JOHN SELLECK AND I WENT TO THE SITE PREPARED TO DEAL WITH A SUBSTANTIAL VOLUME OF OIL.  WE MANAGED TO REMOVE THREE GALLONS OF PINK HEATING OIL FROM THE SURFACE OF THE WELL. THERE WAS NO MORE PRODUCT AVAILABLE AT THAT TIME. WHILE WE WERE USING A BAILER WE NOTICED SMALL RODENT PARTS WERE COMING UP.  ALSO THERE WAS A DISTINCT SEPTIC ODOR COMING FROM THE WELL.  I DISCUSSED THIS PROBLEM WITH RAY AND WE DECIDED THAT PUMPING THE SURFACE WITH A TRASH PUMP MIGHT TAKE CARE OF THE DEAD ANIMAL PROBLEM.  IN THE PROCESS OF USING THE TRASH PUMP HE ALSO RECOVERED MORE OIL.  SUBSEQUENT TO THIS, TECH SERVICES (ALAN INGRAM AND JIM LAVOIE) CLEANED THE WELL WITH TERGITOL, TREATED IT WITH CHLOROXS AND REMOVED THREE WELL VOLUMES.  THEY INDICATED THAT THERE WAS STILL AN ODOR OF PRODUCT IN THE WATER.  OUR FIRST IMPRESSION WAS THAT SOMEONE HAD POURED PRODUCT DOWN THE WELL, BUT THE PERSISTENCE OF PRODUCT ODOR AFTER THE ABOVE MENTIONED PROCEDURE SUGGESTS THAT THE ACQUIFER HAS BEEN IMPACTED BY A SPILL.  THERE WERE NO OBVIOUS SURFACE SPILLS BUT A DIFFERENT MOBILE HOME HAD JUST BEEN INSTALLED AND THE AREA HAD BEEN BACK FILLED WITH CLEAN GRAVEL.  RAY HAD OVERSEEN THIS PROCESS AND HE HAD NOT OBSERVED A SURFACE SPILL.

AS OF 11/13/01 THE WELL DOES NOT HAVE A PUMP.  WHEN RAY GETS THE WELL OPERATIONAL AGAIN WE WILL HAVE FILTERS INSTALLED AND PUT THE WELL ON QUARTERLY MONITORING.  THE WELL IS OVER SIX HUNDRED FEET DEEP AND HAS ELEVEN FEET OF CASING. THE TOP OF THE CASING IS AT THE BOTTOM OF A FOUR FOOT DEEP HOLE FORMED BY A CEMENT WELL TILE THAT IS THREE FEET IN DIAMETER.
THE PROJECT CONSISTS OF SIX LOTS ON 33.16 ACRES ADJACENT TO THE SABLE OAKS GOLF COURSE IN SOUTH PORTLAND.

THE PROJECT COSISTS OF ATHLETIC FIELDS, AN ACCESS DRIVE, A PARKING LOT, AND A 4000 SQ FT MULTI-PURPOSE BUILDING.

ON DECEMBER 28, 2001 AT 1400 WE RECEIVED NOTICE FROM MR. ROGER GRINDLE  OF HANCOCK REPORTING THAT HIS DRILLED WELL WAS CONTAMINATED WITH #2 FUEL OIL.  NORTHEAST LABS DID THE ANALYSIS AND FOUND A CONTAMINATION LEVEL OF 240 PPB OF WEATHERED FUEL OIL.  MR. GRINDLE SAID HIS BASEMENT FEEDLINE WAS BURIED IN CONCRETE BUT HE HAD IT DISCONNECTED IN THE PAST WEEK AND AN AIR PRESSURE TEST SHOWED NO DROP AFTER A COUPLE DAYS.  HE ALSO SAID THAT THE HANCOCK BAPTIST CHURCH WAS LOCATED NEXT DOOR AND THEY HAD A BURIED TANK LESS THAN 100' FROM HIS WELL.  THE TANK WAS NOT REGISTERED.  THE CHURCH HAS A SMALL MEMBERSHIP AND HAD JUST RE-OPENED TWO OR THREE YEARS AGO.
        I CONTACTED REVEREND WILLIAM SOMMERVILLE AND MET HIM AND PARISHIONER ROSE KIEF AND FOUND THAT THE TANK WAS INSTALLED IN THE EARLY 1960'S AND WAS LIKELY A 275 GALLON BASEMENT TANK.  I TOLD THEM THE TANK WAS ILLEGAL AND DUE TO THE CONTAMINATED WELL THE TANK MUST BE REMOVED AS SOON POSSIBLE.  THEY AGREED BUT SAID THE CHURCH DIDN'T HAVE MUCH MONEY.  I TOLD THEM THAT THEY WERE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE TANK REMOVAL COSTS BUT THEY COULD FILE FOR INDIVIDUAL INABILITY TO PAY  WHICH, IF ELIGIBLE, WOULD PAY THE UP-FRONT CLEANUP COSTS.  WE MADE ARRANGEMENTS FOR LOCAL CONTRACTOR RUDY BAGLEY TO EXCAVATE THE TANK AND I HIRED FESSENDEN ENVIRONMENTAL TO DO A SITE ASSESSMENT TO DOCUMENT WHETHER THE TANK WAS LEAKING.  WE SCHEDULED THIS WORK FOR JANUARY 2 AFTER ONE POSTPONEMENT DUE TO SNOW.
         WE DUG AS SCHEDULED AND REMOVED THE 275 GALLON BASEMENT TANK AND FOUND TWO LARGE PENCIL SIZE HOLES AND HALF A DOZEN OTHER HOLES.  ADAM MEYER OF FESSENDEN FOUND SOIL CONTAMINATION AND WE REMOVED FORTY-TWO YARDS OF SOIL TO LANE'S ASPHALT BATCH PLANT IN ELLSWORTH FOR STOCKPILING UNTIL THEY USE IT IN THE SPRING.
          WE CONTINUED DIGGING THE NEXT MORNING BUT WE REMOVED ONLY TWELVE YARDS OF CONTAMINATED SOIL.  THE BEDROCK MADE A NINETY DEGREE VERTICAL RISE OF ABOUT ONE FOOT.  THIS RISE DAMMED THE OIL FLOW ON TOP OF THE LEDGE BUT THE PRODUCT LIKELY ENTERED THE BEDROCK AT THIS FRACTURE.  THIS FRACTURE WAS ALSO IN A DIRECT LINE WITH MR.GRINDLE'S DRILLED WELL.  WE PUT A FILTER ON THE WELL AND PLACED THE HOME ON QUARTERLY MONITORING.  THE CHURCH HAS NO WELL.

CONTAMINATION AT 8PPB WAS FOUND WHEN THE GOVERNOR ARRANGED FOR A NUMBER OF WELLS TO BE SAMPLED FOR MTBE.  RESAMPLE RESULTS WERE 2.4 PPB. NO OBVIOUS SOURCE EXCEPT THE HOME'S DRIVEWAY, THE ROAD AND A GRAVEL PARKING AREA ACROSS THE STREET AT LONGFELLOW'S NURSERY. ALL ARE W/IN 100' OF WELL. MOBIL PIPELINE BEHIND THE PROPERTY DOWNHILL FROM THE WELL. REF TO TECH SVS & QUARTERLY SAMPLING.

THE DEAD RIVER CO. CALLED TO REPORT THAT AN OIL SPILL HAD OCCURRED AT UNCLE JAY'S HOUSE OF PIZZA, 173 ELLSWORTH RD., IN BLUE HILL. THEY HAD RESPONDED TO A "NO OIL" CALL AND DISCOVERED A HOLE IN THE FURNACE FEED LINE. THIS LINE HAD BEEN LAID IN A GROOVE BETWEEN THE CELLAR WALL AND THE POURED CONCRETE FLOOR. THIS GROOVE WENT DOWN TO BARE SOIL. SO WHILE THE LINE WAS FAIRLY WELL PROTECTED FROM IMPACT DAMAGE, IT RESTED IN A CONSTANTLY MOIST ENVIRONMENT AND EVENTUALLY ROTTED. DEAD RIVER CO. HAD REVIEWED THE BUSINESS'S OIL RECORDS AND THEY BELIEVE THAT THE LOSS IS IN THE NEIGHBORHOOD OF 200 GALLONS. THEY ALSO TOLD ME THAT THE NEIGHBOR, RAYMOND ROBERTSON, WAS RUMORED TO HAVE OIL IN HIS WELL.
   I MADE ARRANGEMENTS TO MEET THE PIZZA HOUSE OPERATOR, JAY MARSH, AT THE SCENE THE NEXT MORNING, 11/28. HE DID NOT APPEAR, BUT I EXPLORED THE OUTSIDE AND LATER THE CELLAR WHEN THE EMPLOYEES ARRIVED. THERE WAS NO FREE OIL TO BE FOUND BOTH IN THE CELLAR AND DOWN HILL. THERE WAS A SLIGHT OIL ODOR IN THE TANK AND BOILER AREA OF THE CELLAR, BUT IT WAS NOT NOTICEABLE IN THE DINING AND WORK AREAS.
   I WENT NEXT DOOR AND MET WITH MR. ROBERTSON. HE SHOWED ME A GALLON PICKLE JUG OF WATER HE HAD DRAWN FROM HIS WELL BEFORE MY ARRIVAL. IT HAD A 1/2" OF RED OIL ON ITS SURFACE! HE HAD ALREADY SENT A WATER SAMPLE INTO A LAB FOR TESTING AND WHEN IT WAS LATER REPORTED IT SHOWED 3600 PPM, NOT A SURPRISE.
   I TOOK A WATER SAMPLE FROM THE RESTAURANT WELL WHICH I LEARNED WAS ON THE NORTHEAST SIDE OF THE BUILDING (MR. ROBERTSON BEING ON THE SOUTHWEST). THE LAB LATER REPORTED IT "NON-DETECT" FOR DIESEL RANGE ORGANICS. I HAD IT PUT ON QUARTERLY MONITORING. I DISCUSSED THE PROBLEM WITH PAUL BLOOD, OUR TECH SERVICES DIVISION GEOLOGIST. HE RECOMMENDED THAT MR. ROBERTSON BE PLACED ON A FILTER SYSTEM AND THAT THE WELL BE USED AS A RECOVERY WELL AT THE SAME TIME. HE WOULD HAVE THE TECH SERVICES TECHNICIANS RECOVER THE OIL ON A REGULAR BASIS. HE ALSO HAD THEM SAMPLE OTHER WELLS IN THE AREA.  THEY WERE CLEAN.
   MR. ROBERTSON HAS NOT BEEN SATISFIED WITH THE FILTERED WATER AND HAS REQUESTED THAT A WELL BE DRILLED FOR HIM. HE HAS ABOUT THREE ACRES OF LAND AT HIS HOME AND MR. BLOOD IS LOOKING INTO THE FEASIBILITY OF LOCATING A CLEAN WELL THERE.
   IN CONVERSING WITH MR. ROBERTSON I LEARNED THAT MR. MARSH WAS NOT THE OWNER OF THE PIZZA BUILDING. I CONFIRMED THAT PETER CLAPP OWNED IT. I SPOKE WITH MR. CLAPP BY PHONE AND EXPLAINED THE CIRCUMSTANCES. HE EXPRESSED CONCERN FOR THE NEIGHBORS' WATER AND I ASSURED HIM WE WERE INVESTIGATING THAT. I EXPLAINED THAT AS THE OWNER OF THE TANK, HE APPEARED TO BE THE RESPONSIBLE PARTY AND EXPLAINED THE AST INSURANCE FUND TO HIM. I ALSO NOTIFIED THE FIRE MARSHAL'S OFFICE OF THE SPILL AND REQUESTED THAT MR. CLAPP BE SENT AN APPLICATION.
   THE TECH SERVICES GROUP WILL CONTINUE TO WORK ON THIS PROBLEM AND FURTHER QUESTIONS SHOULD BE DIRECTED TOWARD THEM.

properties.DESCRIPTION:
FULLER'S MARKET INC. IS A REGISTERED UNDERGROUND OIL STORAGE FACILITY (#638) USED FOR MARKETING AND DISTRIBUTION OF PETROLEUM TO THE PUBLIC.  THE FACILITY IS LOCATED ON THE HALLOWELL-LITCHFIELD ROAD IN WEST GARDINER.  WALTER AND PAMELA LONGFELLOW HAVE OWNED AND OPERATED THE FACILITY SINCE 2000.  THE FACILITY IS LOCATED IN A SENSITIVE GEOLOGIC AREA BECAUSE IT IS SITED WITHIN 300 FEET OF THREE PRIVATE WATER SUPPLIES.  
THE FACILITY INCLUDES FOUR UNDERGROUND TANKS: THREE 4,000 GALLON GASOLINE TANKS AND ONE 3,000 GALLON DIESEL TANK.  THE GASOLINE TANKS WERE INSTALLED IN 1988 AND ARE CONSTRUCTED OF CATHODICALLY PROTECTED STEEL. THE DIESEL TANK, INSTALLED IN 1991, IS JACKETED.  ALL FOUR TANKS ARE DOUBLE-WALLED BUT DO NOT HAVE ELECTRONIC MONITORING OF THE INTERSTITIAL SPACE.  INSTEAD, THE OWNER USES MONTHLY PRODUCT INVENTORY RECONCILIATION AND ANNUAL STATISTICAL INVENTORY ANALYSIS TO MEET LEAK DETECTION REQUIREMENTS. SITE VISIT: MAY 2009: THERE IS A SINGLE WALLED KEROSENE ABOVE GROUND STORAGE TANK (AST) AND ADJACENT DISPENSER. NO WEATHER PROTECTION AND NO SECONDARY CONTAINMENT.
properties.SUMMARY:
ON NOVEMBER 21, 2001, MR. LONGFELLOW OBSERVED A WEEP OF PRODUCT AT THE BASE OF GASOLINE DISPENSER #2 AND REPORTED IT TO THE DEPARTMENT.  A CERTIFIED UNDERGROUND STORAGE TANK INSTALLER DISCOVERED THAT THE FILTER ABOVE THE CHECK VALVE HAD A PINHOLE LEAK IN IT AND HAD BEEN LEAKING FOR AN UNKNOWN PERIOD OF TIME.  THE FILTER WAS CHANGED AND THE LEAK WAS ABATED.  THE DEPARTMENT CONDUCTED SOIL AND GROUNDWATER SAMPLING IN AUGUST 2002 AND DISCOVERED THAT GASOLINE CONTAMINATION WAS PRESENT IN GROUND WATER.  LABORATORY ANALYSIS DETECTED TBA, AN OXYGENATE AND RELATIVELY RECENT ADDITIVE TO GASOLINE, INDICATING THAT THE CONTAMINATION PROBABLY RESULTED FROM THE 2001 DISPENSER LEAK.  
SAMPLING OF WELLS FOR THE MARKET AND TWO ADJACENT PROPERTIES IN AUGUST 2002 SHOWED THAT NONE OF THE WALLS WERE CONTAMINATED WITH GASOLINE, EXCEPT THAT THE MARKET'S WELL SHOWED 1.5.PPB OF MTBE.  THE WELL DOES NOT REQUIRE TREATMENT; HOWEVER, THE DEPARTMENT HAS BEGUN A HYDROGEOLOGICAL INVESTIGATION TO DETERMINE THE EXTENT OF THE GASOLINE IMPACT TO GROUNDWATER AND DETERMINE CLEANUP ACTIONS NEEDED TO PROTECT DRINKING WATER SUPPLIES THAT ARE AT RISK.
IN NOVEMBER 2002, SIX MONITORING WELLS WERE INSTALLED AROUND FULLERS MARKET, TO ASSESS THE CHARACTERISTICS AND ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY OF SOILS AND GROUND WATER.
BETWEEN 9/22 AND 9/29/2004, 1346 TONS OF CONTAMINATED SOIL WAS REMOVED FROM THE SITE, AND TRANSPORTED TO COMMERCIAL PAVING CO., INC.
SITE VISIT: MAY 2009: THERE IS A SINGLE WALLED KEROSENE ABOVE GROUND STORAGE TANK (AST) AND ADJACENT DISPENSER. NO WEATHER PROTECTION AND NO SECONDARY CONTAINMENT.

ON 2/27/02,1015 HOURS WE WERE NOTIFIED OF AN ONGOING GASOLINE SPILL AT PIPERS COUNTRY STORE ON ROUTE 222 IN LEVANT.  THE BANGOR AND LEVANT FIRE DEPARTMENT WERE ON SCENE TO PROVIDE PUBLIC SAFETY AND DYSARTS WERE ON THEIR WAY TO STOP THE LEAK AND RECOVER PRODUCT.  THE RELEASE WAS TO THE DIKE AREA, WHICH DID NOT HAVE A ROOF.  THE ABSENCE OF A ROOF ALLOWED WATER TO ACCUMULATE AND THIS FORMED ICE, WHICH EVENTUALLY CAUSED THE WATER DRAIN VALVE TO CRACK.  THIS PART OF THE STORAGE SYSTEM CONSISTED OF TWO 5K ASTS INSIDE OF A DIKE. 

DYSARTS ARRIVED WITH PUMPS AND TANKERS AND PROCEEDED TO STOP THE RELEASE BY REMOVING PRODUCT FROM THE LEAKING TANK.  NEXT THEY RECOVERED THE GASOLINE THAT HAD GONE INTO THE DIKE.  FOUR INCHES OF PRODUCT ON THE SEGMENT OF THE DIKE INVOLVED FIGURED TO BE ABOUT 128 GALLONS.  AFTER THIS THEY PUMPED OUT THE CONTAMINATED WATER, FLUSHED WITH MORE WATER AND PUMPED AGAIN.  THIS WAS ALL DONE THROUGH HOLES THAT HAD BEEN POKED THROUGH THE ICE.

MEANWHILE THE LEAKER'S SISTER TANK(A 5K SUPER UNLEADED) WAS SITTING THERE WITH IT'S WATER DRAIN VALVE TRAPPED IN THE ICE.  THIS WAS FREED UP WITHOUT INCIDENT BY USING WARM WATER.  THIS APPROACH PRODUCED LESS RISK THAN TRYING TO CHIP THE ICE AWAY FROM THE VALVE.  ALSO, MEANWHILE, THE AREA WAS MONITORED WITH AN EXPLOSIMETER.  THERE WERE A COUPLE OF TIMES WHEN THE SPACE NEAR THE BOTTOM REACHED 10% LEL.  BUT THESE EPISODES PASSED QUICKLY BECAUSE OF A BRISK BREEZE.  THE FIRE FIGHTERS FOAMED THE SPILL AREA BEFORE LEAVING.  THIS REDUCED THE LEL TO ZERO.  IT WAS STILL ZERO THE FOLLOWING DAY.

MCKUSICK PETROLEUM OF DOVER FOXCROFT CALLED TO REPORT AN OUTSIDE HOME HEATING OIL SPILL AT THE RESIDENCE OF PAT MICHAUD ON THE COOLEY ROAD.  IT WAS STATED THAT THE FITTING TO THE TANK BROKE OFF FROM THE SHIFTING SNOW SPILLING AN UNDETERMINED AMOUNT OF FUEL.  INVESTIGATION OF THE SITE SHOWN LITTLE EVIDENCE OF OIL.  I WAS A BIT CONCERNED SINCE THE WELL TO THE RESIDENCE WAS ONLY ABOUT 30 FEET AWAY.  MR. MICHAUD INSISTED THAT HE HAD LITTLE OIL IN THE TANK.  BEFORE LEAVING I EXPLAINED TO HIM ABOUT THE AST FUND COVERAGE.  I ALSO INFORMED HIM THAT IF HE SHOULD HAD ANY ODORS IN HIS HOME OR HIS WATER HE SHOULD NOTIFY US.

B-448-98:  CHARLIE ADAMS OF A-A CONTRACTORS CALLED TO REQUEST A WAIVER OF THE 30-DAY REMOVAL NOTICE TO REMOVE A 10000 GALLON #2 UST AT THE WEATHERBY SCHOOL IN HAMPDEN. THE SCHOOL DISTRICT WAS TRYING TO GET THEIR USTS REMOVED AND REPLACED BEFORE THE START OF THE SCHOOL YEAR. I AGREED.
   ON 7/7 IN THE AFTERNOON THE TANK WAS REMOVED. THE TANK WAS UNIFORMLY PITTED WITH MUCH ADHERED SOIL. HOWEVER I DID NOT LOCATE ANY HOLES THROUGH VISUAL EXAMINATION. THE SOIL AND WATER IN THE HOLE SHOWED NO EVIDENCE OF A LEAK. THE COPPER FEED LINES HAD BEEN SLEEVED IN PVC PIPING AND WERE REMOVED.

 B-482-02: THIS OFFICE RECEIVED A CALL AT 1230 ON 9/17/02, FROM TODD (A.L. DOGGETT, INC.; GRAY) REPORTING AN OIL SPILL.  HE STATED THAT THEY WERE IN THE PROCESS OF REMOVING THE ABOVEGROUND STORAGE TANK SYSTEM AND ASSOCIATED UNDERGROUND PIPING AT THE FORMER NEALLY'S CORNER STORE AT THE JUNCTION OF THE KENNEBEC ROAD AND ROUTE 69 IN HAMPDEN AND HAD ENCOUNTERED GASOLINE CONTAMINATED SOIL.  DEP'S ASSISTANCE WAS REQUESTED ON SITE.

     PROCEEDING TO HAMPDEN, I MET WITH TODD AND WENT OVER THE SITUATION WITH HIM.  IN PREPARATION TO INSTALLING A NEW UNDERGROUND TANK AT THE FACILITY, THEY HAD REMOVED A 4000 GALLON AST OUT BACK AND WERE DIGGING UP THE OLD PIPING ON THE LEFT SIDE OF THE STORE (BETWEEN THE BUILDING AND ROUTE 69) WHEN THE CONTAMINATION WAS DISCOVERED.  UPON INVESTIGATION, IT APPEARED THAT THE CAUSE OF THE LEAK WAS DUE TO LOOSE FITTINGS ON THE PIPING.  THIS WAS IN AN AREA WHERE FOUR UNDERGROUND TANKS HAD BEEN REMOVED IN 1988 (SEE CASE # B-448-88).  AT THAT TIME, THERE WAS VERY LITTLE EVIDENCE OF CONTAMINATION AROUND THE TANKS.  WHATEVER SPILLED, APPARENTLY OCCURRED AFTER THOSE TANKS WERE REMOVED.  IT WAS INDICATED THAT THE BANK HAD FORECLOSED ON THE PROPERTY AND IT HAD BEEN OUT OF SERVICE/VACANT SINCE SOMETIME IN 1997 OR 1998.  TODD WAS NOT SURE WHEN THE PUMPS AND PUMP ISLAND HAD BEEN REMOVED.  BY THE TIME I ARRIVED AT THE FACILITY, A.L. DOGGETT HAD REMOVED ALL OF THE PIPING FROM THE GROUND AND HAD PILED IT BEHIND THE STORE.  IT WAS RUSTY AND APPEARED TO BE GALVANIZED FOR THE MOST PART.  SOME OF THE SECTIONS WERE WRAPPED WITH A BLACK PROTECTIVE COATING, FOR WHATEVER REASON.  SEVERAL LOADS OF CONTAMINATED SOIL WERE ALSO PILED TO THE RIGHT OF THE STORE PENDING DISPOSAL ARRANGEMENTS.

     I WAS INFORMED THAT MARK ARSENAULT HAD JUST PURCHASED THE PROPERTY FROM THE BANK AND WAS IN THE PROCESS OF UPGRADING THE FACILITY PRIOR TO OPENING.  UP TO THIS POINT IN TIME, HE HAD NOT OPERATED THE STORE OR THE GASOLINE SUPPLY SYSTEM.  AND THE KICKER IS...THAT THE BANK HAD CERTIFIED THE PROPERTY AS CONTAMINATION FREE (BASED ON A PHASE I SITE ASSESSMENT), WHICH IT WAS NOT.  SINCE THE SURROUNDING AREA IS ON WELL WATER, THIS SITE WOULD COME UNDER DEP'S STRINGENT CLEANUP GUIDELINES.  WHEN MR. ARSENAULT ARRIVED ON SCENE, WE BRIEFLY DISCUSSED WHAT NEEDED TO BE DONE FOR A CLEANUP.  THROUGHOUT THE DAY ON 9/17/02, 9/18/02, AND 9/19/02, APPROXIMATELY 1176 CUBIC YARDS OF CONTAMINATED SOIL WERE REMOVED ALONG THE SIDE OF THE BUILDING AND ACROSS THE FRONT YARD TO THE OPPOSITE RIGHT HAND CORNER OF THE BUILDING.  THIS WAS QUITE A BIT MORE MATERIAL THAN ANY OF US EXPECTED.  ALL OF THE SOIL WAS TAKEN TO VAUGHN THIBODEAU & SON'S BATCH PLANT IN PROSPECT FOR PROCESSING.  PID METER READINGS ON THE SOIL RANGED FROM A LOW OF 8.9 PPM UP TO A HIGH OF 5894 PPM.  MOST OF THE CONTAMINATION WAS REMOVED, EXCEPT WHERE IT EXTENDED INTO THE ROADBED UNDER THE KENNEBEC ROAD AND UNDER THE STORE'S FOUNDATION.  CLAY WAS FOUND ALONG THE SIDE WALLS AND ON THE BOTTOM OF THE EXCAVATION, WHICH HELPED TO CONTAIN THE OIL IN THE IMMEDIATE AREA OF THE STORE.  AS A PRECAUTION, THE DRILLED WELL FOR THE FACILITY HAS BEEN PLACED ON QUARTERLY MONITORING FOR ONE YEAR.  SAMPLE ANALYSIS RESULTS FROM 11/18/02, INDICATED THAT NOTHING WAS DETECTED DOWN TO THE REPORTING LIMIT.

properties.SUMMARY:
AFTER OBTAINING A WAIVER FROM THE 30-DAY WRITTEN NOTIFICATION REQUIREMENT, JAMES HARVEY (STOCKTON SPRINGS; #567-4236) BEGAN THE REMOVAL OF TWO UNDERGROUND GASOLINE TANKS AT FRANKFORT GENERAL STORE ON ROUTE #1A IN FRANKFORT ON 6/1/98.  DON BUBAR (G.R. ADAMS JR., INC.; BANGOR; #942-9573) WAS THE LICENSED TANK INSTALLER ON SITE FOR THIS PROJECT; G.R. ADAMS JR., INC. DID THEIR OWN EXCAVATION; AND JOE FOWLER (FESSENDEN GEO-ENVIRONMENTAL SERVICES; BANGOR; #947-3184) WAS HIRED TO DO THE SITE ASSESSMENT.

     BOTH TANKS WERE 4000 GALLON CAPACITY.  THEY WERE ASPHALT COATED STEEL CONSTRUCTION, HAD GALVANIZED PIPING, AND WERE BACKFILLED WITH NON STANDARD MATERIAL (GRAVEL).  ACCORDING TO THE REGISTRATION, THEY WERE INSTALLED IN MARCH 1972 WHEN THE FACILITY WAS FIRST ESTABLISHED.  THE TANKS WERE THEN USED UP UNTIL ABOUT 10 YEARS AGO WHEN THEY WERE TAKEN OUT OF SERVICE.  MR. HARVEY PURCHASED THE PROPERTY IN 1994, BUT NEVER USED THE TANKS.

     JUST PRIOR TO THEIR REMOVAL, THE FIRST TANK CONTAINED 18 INCHES OF WATER AND THE SECOND CONTAINED 6 INCHES OF WATER.  HOWEVER, NO CORROSION HOLES IN THE TANKS OR PROBLEMS WITH THE PIPING WERE 
OBSERVED.  THE SURROUNDING SOIL WAS A CLAY-SILT TYPE OF MATERIAL AND GROUND WATER IN THE EXCAVATION DID NOT HAVE A NOTICEABLE SHEEN.  MINOR CONTAMINATION, IN THE 15 TO 150 PPM RANGE ON A PID METER, WAS FOUND AROUND THE TANKS.  CONTAMINATION IN THE BOTTOM OF THE HOLE WAS IN THE 2500+ PPM RANGE.

     SINCE THERE IS A PUBLIC WELL NEARBY, THIS FACILITY WOULD COME UNDER DEP'S STRINGENT CLEANUP GUIDELINES.  ARRANGEMENTS WERE MADE TO HAUL THE CONTAMINATED MATERIAL TO MR. HARVEY'S PROPERTY ON THE BOG HILL ROAD IN SEARSPORT FOR AERATION.  ALTHOUGH I WENT OVER THE "INITIAL CLEANUP ACTION AGREEMENT", LUST INSURANCE FUND PROCEDURE, AND THE "WE PAY FIRST/YOU PAY FIRST" OPTION, MR. HARVEY WAS NOT SURE DURING THE CLEANUP IF HE WOULD APPLY TO THE FUND OR NOT.  IT WOULD DEPEND ON THE TOTAL COST.

     SOIL IN THE PIPING TRENCH AND UNDER THE PUMP ISLAND WAS IN THE 2500+ PPM RANGE.  THROUGHOUT 6/1-2/98, APPROXIMATELY 204 CUBIC YARDS WERE HAULED OFF SITE FOR AERATION.  THE CONTAMINATION APPEARED TO HAVE ORIGINATED FROM THE PUMP ISLAND, FLOWED DOWN THE PIPING TRENCH, AND ENTERED THE TANK HOLE.  DUE TO THE LOCATION OF THE ROADBED OUT FRONT (I.E., ON ONE SIDE OF THE PUMP ISLAND) AND THE BUILDING ON THE OTHER SIDE, THEY WERE UNABLE TO REMOVE ALL OF THE CONTAMINATION.  PID READINGS ALONG THE ROADBED WERE 2500+ PPM AND UNDER THE BUILDING, THEY WERE AROUND 2300 PPM.

     SINCE THE PID NUMBERS WERE NOT DROPPING OFF AS WE EXCAVATED AWAY FROM THE PUMP ISLAND AND WE WOULD NOT BE ABLE TO RECOVER ALL OF THE CONTAMINATION DUE TO THE PRESENCE OF THE ROADBED AND BUILDING, PLUS THERE WAS SOME CONCERN AS TO HOW MUCH MATERIAL THE SPREAD SITE COULD HANDLE, THE DECISION WAS MADE TO DISCONTINUE THE EXCAVATION AT THIS TIME.  IT WAS FELT THAT THE MOST HEAVILY CONTAMINATED SOIL AROUND THE PUMP ISLAND (THE CENTER OF THE PROBLEM) HAD BEEN REMOVED.

CONCLUSION:  SHOULD DOT EXCAVATE INTO THIS SECTION OF ROAD OR THE OWNER DECIDE TO REMOVE THE BUILDING, THAT WOULD BE A GOOD TIME TO GO BACK IN AND RECOVER SOME ADDITIONAL CONTAMINATION.  IN THE MEANTIME, THE CASE HAS BEEN REFERRED TO TECH SERVICES FOR THEIR INFORMATION AND/OR ACTION.

     THE SPREAD SITE WAS CHECKED SEVERAL TIMES DURING THE SUMMER AND AS OF 10/20/98, ALL OF THE PID READINGS WERE 0.0 PPM.

properties.SUMMARY:
FOLLOWING WRITTEN NOTIFICATION, RALPH CARR (MEDFORD; #732-5604) BEGAN THE REMOVAL OF TWO 500 GALLON GASOLINE TANKS AT CARR'S GARAGE ON ROUTE #116/155 IN HOWLAND ON 10/2/98.  DAVE BEAUMENT (BEAUMENT GENERATOR; E. MILLINOCKET; #746-5459) WAS THE LICENSED TANK INSTALLER ON SITE FOR THIS PROJECT; KING BROS TRUCKING (W. ENFIELD; #732-3641) DID THE EXCAVATION; AND JOE FOWLER (FESSENDEN GEO-ENVIRONMENTAL SERVICES; BANGOR; #947-3184) WAS HIRED TO DO THE SITE ASSESSMENT.

THE TANKS WERE ASPHALT COATED STEEL, HAD GALVANIZED PIPING, AND WERE BACKFILLED WITH NON STANDARD MATERIAL.  EXACTLY WHEN THEY WERE INSTALLED IS UNKNOWN.  THE FACILITY WAS ESTABLISHED IN THE 1920'S AND WAS USED TO FUEL MODEL T'S AT THAT TIME.  IT WAS THEN ABANDONED ABOUT 40 YEARS AGO.  WHEN MR. CARR BOUGHT THE PROPERTY IN 1974, THE TANKS WERE PRESENT ON SITE, BUT HE NEVER USED THEM.  SOIL SURROUNDING THE EXCAVATION WAS A COMBINATION CLAY-TILL TYPE OF MATERIAL.  ALTHOUGH THE FIRST TANK WAS FULL OF WATER WHEN IT WAS UNCOVERED, IT CONTAINED 8 OR 9 CORROSION HOLES UP ON ITS SIDE.  CONTAMINATED SOIL IN THE 2500+ PPM RANGE ON A PID METER WAS FOUND UNDER THE TANK.  GROUND WATER IN THE EXCAVATION CONTAINED A SLIGHT SHEEN.  THE SECOND TANK WAS HALF FULL OF WATER.  IT ALSO HAD SEVERAL CORROSION HOLES AND CONTAMINATED SOIL AROUND IT.  A LOCAL CONTRACTOR WAS CALLED IN TO REMOVE THE WATER.  

RUMOR HAD IT THAT DOT WANTED TO WIDEN THE CORNER AT THAT INTERSECTION ABOUT 5 YEARS AGO IN ORDER TO BETTER ACCOMMODATE TRAILER TRUCKS MAKING RIGHT HAND TURNS.  A TEST PIT OR TWO WAS DUG ON MR. CARR'S PROPERTY AND THE TANKS, PLUS CONTAMINATED SOIL, WERE DISCOVERED AT THAT TIME.  THE PIPING WAS REMOVED AND THE TANKS WERE COVERED UP.  BASED ON THAT INFORMATION, DOT APPARENTLY DECIDED TO LEAVE THE CORNER ALONE.

SINCE THE TANKS WERE LONG OVERDUE FOR REMOVAL AND WE WERE BEYOND THE 9/30/98 DEADLINE FOR ANY TYPE OF INSURANCE FUND COVERAGE, I DID NOT GET INTO THE "WE PAY FIRST/YOU PAY FIRST" AGREEMENT.  PLUS I DID NOT FEEL THAT THE CLEANUP WOULD EXCEED HIS POTENTIAL DEDUCTIBLE (I.E., $12,500), EVEN IF HE COULD APPLY TO THE FUND.

MOST OF HOWLAND IS ON TOWN WATER, BUT DUE TO A PUBLIC WELL NEAR MR. CARR'S PROPERTY, THIS FACILITY WOULD COME UNDER DEP'S STRINGENT CLEANUP GUIDELINES.  AFTER APPROVING A LAND SPREAD SITE IN ENFIELD, KING BROS TRUCKING BEGAN HAULING THE CONTAMINATED SOIL.  THEY WERE PRETTY MUCH LIMITED IN WHAT COULD BE EXCAVATED DUE TO THE PRESENCE OF THE BUILDING ADJACENT TO THE ROAD AND THE ROADBED OUT FRONT.  WE REALLY DID NOT WANT TO UNDERMINE EITHER ONE.  CONSEQUENTLY, SOME CONTAMINATION IN THE 2500+ PPM RANGE REMAINS IN THE SIDE WALLS.  SOIL IN THE BOTTOM OF THE EXCAVATION WAS CLAY AND AT 8 OR 9 FEET BELOW THE SURFACE IT WAS CLEANED DOWN TO AROUND 100 PPM.

TOWARDS THE END OF THE EXCAVATION, A THIRD (UNKNOWN) 1000 GALLON GASOLINE TANK WAS UNCOVERED NEAR A RAMP FOR THE GARAGE.  IT WAS ASPHALT COATED STEEL, HAD GALVANIZED PIPING, AND WAS BACKFILLED WITH NON STANDARD MATERIAL.  WHEN IT WAS INSTALLED IS UNKNOWN.  IT CONTAINED VERY LITTLE WATER AND WAS EASILY REMOVED FROM THE GROUND.  ALL OF THE TANKS WERE SCHEDULED TO BE CUT UP FOR SCRAP METAL.  APPROXIMATELY 112 CUBIC YARDS WERE HAULED OFF SITE FOR AERATION.

CONCLUSION:  IF THE BUILDING IS EVER TORN DOWN AND/OR THE ROADBED IS OPENED UP, I AM SURE THAT THERE WILL BE SOME ADDITIONAL CONTAMINATED SOIL TO BE REMOVED.

PAT SEAWARD, DEP TECH SERVICES, REPORTED AN INCIDENT OF POTENTIAL GASOLINE CONTAMINATION AT THE SUBJECT LOCATION.  THE SUSPECTED SOURCE WAS A VEHICLE LEAK.  I WAS NOT INVOLVED AS NO ACTIVE SOURCE WAS DISCOVERED REQUIRING REMOVAL.  TECH SERVICES HAS OVERSIGHT OF THIS CASE.

JON ANDREWS AND I RESPONDED TO INVESTIGATE.  THE OWNER, DAVID FOLSOM CONFIRMED THAT LIN-COR (BUTCH SANBORN) HAD BEEN ON SITE PREPARING 500 CARS FOR CRUSHING.  THERE WERE NO LIN-COR EMPLOYEES ON SITE WHEN DEP DID THE INITIAL INSPECTION OF THE AREA. A PILE OF CAR BATTERIES WAS ON THE GROUND.  A LARGE PAY LOADER WITH FORK TINES WAS STAGED IN THIS AREA TO MOVE THE CARS AROUND.  THE UNIT WAS LEAKING HYDRAULIC FLUID BADLY AND A POOL OF THE OIL WAS OBSERVED ON THE GROUND BENEATH THE LOADER.

HE WAS TOLD THAT THE SPILLED GASOLINE AND OIL WOULD HAVE TO BE EXCAVATED TO MINIMIZE THE IMPACT TO GROUNDWATER.  THERE ARE TWO HOMES NEARBY AS WELL AS A DUG WELL ON SITE THAT SERVES THE BUSINESS. MARK NYSTROM DISCOVERED A LINE LEAK NEAR HIS TANK. THE PRODUCT WAS MOSTLY ABSORBED BY A WOODEN FLOOR AND A SILL. HE PLANNED TO TAKE THE HOUSE DOWN TO BUILD A NEW ONE IN JANUARY. BILL WALLACE AGREED TO LEAVE THE SOIL IN PLACE UNTIL THEN. MR. NYSTROM INSTALLED A RAIN GUTTER AND SOME PLASTIC TO KEEP WATER AWAY FROM THE SPILL AREA. A WATER SAMPLE TAKEN FROM THE WELL TESTED NON-DETECT.

THE HOUSE WAS TORN DOWN IN AUGUST. PERMISSION WAS GIVEN BY DEP SOLID WASTE STAFF FOR MR. NYSTROM TO BURN THE <1 CU YD OF CONTAMINATED WOOD DEBRIS ON SITE PROVIDED THE ASHES WERE BURIED AT LEAST 18" BELOW GRADE (BUT NOT IN THE WATER TABLE) AND A LOCAL FIRE PERMIT WAS OBTAINED. CONTAMINATED SOIL WAS REMOVED BY THE BUILDING CONTRACTOR, GEORGE C. HALL & SONS, INC.
FOUR APPROX 30000 GALLON UPRIGHT PETROLEUM TANKS: TOTAL ESTIMATED STORAGE: 120000 GALLONS.

ICE FELL OFF THE METAL ROOF AND SHEARED OFF THE NIPPLE ATTACHED TO THE OUTSIDE AST.  THE OWNER HEARD THE LOUD BANG AND CHECKED THE TANK OUT 20 MINUTES LATER. SHE THEN CALLED THE LOCAL FIRE DEPT. THE FIRE DEPT. DID WHAT THEY COULD TO STOP THE LEAK AND CONTAIN THE OIL. DE ARRIVED SOMETIME THE NEXT DAY AND SHOVELLED CONTAMINATED SNOW INTO SEVERAL OPERPACK DRUMS. THERE WAS ANOTHER OUTSIDE TANK AT THIS LOCATION AND IT WAS COMPLETELY BURIED IN SNOW AND ICE. THIS TANK ALSO DEVELOPED A LEAK LATER THAT SPRING ( THE SNOW AND ICE LOAD BROKE THE FITTING ON THIS OUTSIDE AST. THIS RESULTED IN A RELEASE OF ABOUT TEN GALLONS OF OIL, ACCORDING TO THE HOMEOWNER JULIE LIBBY.)
 THE OIL FROM THIS FIRST SPILL EVENTUALLY BROKE OUT ON THE GROUND SURFACE DOWNSLOPE FROM THE HOME. THERE WAS A PERIMETER DRAIN THAT DISCHARGED AT A SMALL ROCK FLOWER GARDEN. THIS AREA IS EFFECTED BY THE OIL AND MAY OR MAYNOT REQUIRE EXCAVATION. THE DUG WELL THAT SERVES THIS HOME IS LOCATED SEVERAL HUNDRED FEET AWAY.

ON THE MORNING OF 4/18/97 KELLEY RICHARDSON CALLED TO REPORT THAT THEY HAD OIL IN THEIR WELL.  SHE WENT ON TO EXPLAIN THAT THEY HAD A LINE LEAK  ON THEIR AST SYSTEM LAST FALL.  SHE WENT ON TO EXPLAIN THAT THEY HAD NOT INVOLVED US AT THE TIME BECAUSE SHE HAD BEEN TOLD THAT IT WAS NOT A GOOD IDEA TO GET US INVOLVED.  THEY WENT AHEAD AND HAD NORLENS INSTALL A TWO CANISTER, CHARCOAL FILTER.  SHE WAS CALLING BECAUSE THE OIL WAS COMMING THROUGH THE FILTERS.   I EXPLAINED THE SERVICES THAT WE PROVIDE AS WELL AS THE ADVANTAGES TO REPORTING SUCH EVENT IN A TIMELY MANNER.  

I VISITED THE SITE AND FOUND THAT THERE WAS FREE PRODUCT ON THE WELL.  THE PRODUCT WAS SLOW TO SEPARATE FROM THE WATER.  THIS SUGGESTED TO ME THAT IT WAS QUITE WEATHERED.   ALSO, THERE WAS NO INDICATION OF PRODUCT AT SPILL LOCATION.  I DISCUSSED THE AST FUND AND SUGGESTED THAT THEY APPLY.  ON THE FORM APPLICATION  TO THE FIRE MARSHALL'S OFFICE I EXPLAINED THE CAUSE FOR THE LATE REPORT.  I HAD NORLENS REPACK THE FILTERS.  

FROM THE HISTORY OF THE WELL, THERE IS REASON TO BELIEVE THAT THE CASING IS NOT WELL GROUTED.  WHEN THE SURFICIAL GROUND WATER TABLE IS HIGH AND THE WELL GETS PUMPED HARD THE WATER AT THE TAP BECOMES BOGGY IN TASTE.  ALSO, UNDER THESE CIRCUMSATNCES THEY GET HIGH BACTERIA COUNTS.  I MENTIONED REGROUTING  TO PAUL BLOOD.  PAUL INDICATED THAT IT WAS NOT A GOOD IDEA TO SPEND MONEY ON A WELL THAT HAD FREE PRODUCT IN IT.  RIGHT NOW (5/12/97) THEY ARE NOT DRINKING THE WATER BECAUSE OF A HIGH E. COLIE COUNT.  I'M WAITING ON THE QM REQUEST TO SEE WHAT THE TIME SCHEDULE IS ON THE REPLACMENT WELL.

WELL ALSO SAMPLED IN YANKEE GROCER SPILL

ON 10/30/00, 1430 HOURS PHYLLIS SIMPSON REPORTED THAT THEY HAD AN OIL RELEASE IN THEIR BASEMENT AND THAT THEY COULD SMELL OIL IN THEIR WATER.  THE RELEASE CAME FROM THE FURNACE FEED LINE WITHIN A FOOT OF THE BURNER GUN.  THE PRODUCT LANDED ON THE DIRT FLOOR, WHICH WAS A HARD PACKED, ORGANIC SOIL.  THE SOIL LAYER AT THE SPILL SITE WAS ABOUT TWO AND A HALF FEET THICK OVER THE BEDROCK.  IT GAVE BAG HEAD SPACE READINGS BETWEEN 200 AND 300 PPM FROM TOP TO BOTTOM.  ALTHOUGH I DON'T HAVE A GOOD HANDLE ON THE AMOUNT OF THE RELEASE, I WOULD SAY THAT IT WAS AT LEAST FORTY GALLONS AND THAT THE SOIL NEAR THE SPILL HAD RETAINED LESS THAN A GALLON OF PRODUCT.  THIS MEANS THAT ABOUT FORTY GALLONS (POSSIBLY MORE) WENT INTO THE BEDROCK.  THE BEDROCK WAS HIGHLY FRACTURED, SHALE FORMATION.  IT SEEMED POSSIBLE THAT THE STRIKE DIRECTION MIGHT CARRY THE SPILL PAST THE WELL, WHICH WAS ONLY ABOUT FIFTY FEET FROM THE SPILL.  THE DIP AND THE DEGREE OF CROSS FRACTURING WAS UNCERTAIN.  I COULD NOT SMELL PRODUCT IN THE WATER AND THERE WAS NO FLOATING LAYER ON THE WELL WATER.  HOWEVER, AN ANALYSIS REVEALED 300 PPB AND A FEW DAYS LATER OUR PID COULD PICK IT UP IN A HEADSPACE.

FILTERS, AST FUND APPLICATION AND QUARTERLY MONITORING HAVE BEEN ARRANGED.

ON 4/9/01, 1625 HOURS BOB MARQUIS OF MARQUIS HEATING REPORTED THAT JIM ALEXANDER HAD AN AST NIPPLE LEAK AT HIS RESIDENCE IN GREENFIELD.  THE AST WAS LOCATED CLOSE TO THE GARAGE, WHICH WAS ON A CEMENT SLAB AND THE HOUSEHOLD WELL WAS 30 FEET FROM THE AST ON THE OTHER SIDE OF THE GARAGE.  I WAS ABLE TO ARRANGE A SITE VISIT THE FOLLOWING MORNING. THE SOIL AT THE SPILL SITE (E.G. UNDER THE NIPPLE THAT HAD CRACKED) WAS VERY POROUS AND THERE WERE NO PUDDLES OF PRODUCT.  HOWEVER, A BAILER INDICATED THAT THERE WAS OVER THREE FEET OF FUEL OIL ON THE WELL.  I CALLED JOHN SELLECK (ONE OF OUR TECH SERVICE TECHNICIANS) AND JOHN CAME OUT WITH A PUMP THAT WAS CAPABLE OF REMOVING OIL FROM THE SURFACE OF THE WATER.  WE RECOVERED TWENTY GALLONS ON THAT OCCASION AND ANOTHER TEN ON SUBSEQUENT VISITS. FILTERS WERE INSTALLED ON 4/27/01 AND THE WELL IS ON QM.  BEDROCK IS FIVE FEET FROM GRADE AT THIS LOCATION.  WE DON'T KNOW IF THE ACQUIFER HAS BEEN IMPACTED OR IF THE PRODUCT WENT DOWN THE CASING.  MAYBE QM DATA WILL GIVE US A CLUE.  THE CASE HAS BEEN REFERRED TO TECH SERVICE.

GARY'S FUEL SERVICE CALLED TO REPORT THAT A CUSTOMER, KEN POTTER, RR#2 BOX1280, RT. 46, BUCKSPORT, HAD LOST ABOUT 150 GALLONS OF TRAILER MIX. THE OUTSIDE 275 AST HAD RUSTED THROUGH AND BECAUSE THE TANK WAS ENCLOSED IN A PROTECTIVE SHELTER, THE OWNER DID NOT NOTICE A LEAK UNTIL THE FURNACE STOPPED RUNNING. SINCE THE SHELTER HAD KEPT THE GROUND FROM FREEZING, THE GROUND HAD ABSORBED THE FUEL OIL. THE TANK IS ON THE UPHILL SIDE OF HIS MOBILE HOME. THE TRAILER SITS ON A GRAVEL PAD THAT IS ABOUT ONE FOOT THICK. THE NATIVE SOIL IS A ROCKY TILL THAT MR. POTTER SAID THE CONTRACTOR WHO INSTALLED THE SEPTIC SYSTEM CALLED HARD PAN. THIS IS EVIDENCED BY THE FACT THAT THE LEACH FIELD IS ELEVATED ABOVE GRADE. THE DRILLED WELL IS ABOUT 75 FEET UP GRADE. MR. POTTER BELIEVES THAT IT IS 10-14 FEET TO BEDROCK. SURPRISINGLY THERE WAS NO EVIDENCE OF OIL IN THE GRAVEL UNDER THE TRAILER NOR WAS THERE ANY ODOR. 
   SINCE I BELIEVE THAT THE OIL IS NOW IN THE DEPRESSION CONTAINING THE TRAILER SLAB, THE BEST COURSE OF ACTION IS TO DUE NOTHING. I FEEL THAT ANY ATTEMPT TO DIG FOR THE CONTAMINATION WOULD BE FUTILE UNLESS THE TRAILER IS MOVED. ALSO THE REMOVAL OF THE HARD PAN COULD ALLOW THE OIL ACCESS TO THE BEDROCK.
   THIS WAS DISCUSSED WITH MR. POTTER AND WE BOTH AGREED THAT A WAIT AND SEE POSTURE WAS BEST.

ON THE MORNING OF 2-7-01 MRS. ZIMMERMAN HAD RUN OUT OF FUEL OIL. SHE HAD ARRIVED HOME THE NIGHT BEFORE. HER SON IN LAW HAD USED A SNOW BLOWER AND ACCIDENTALLY BROKE THE COPPER LINE AND FITTINGS FROM THE OUTSIDE AST. THE TANK HAD RECENTLY BEEN FILLED BUT WAS NOW EMPTY.  BEFORE DEP ARRIVAL THE TANK HAD BEEN REPAIRED. THE SPILLED KEROSENE HAD NOT PENETRATED THE FROZEN GROUND. HOWEVER, THE GROUND UNDER THE TRAILER WAS NOT FROZEN. BART NEWHOUSE, OF DEP, USED A SNOW-BLOWER TO REMOVE THE TOP THREE FEET OF SNOW. THE OIL CONTAMINATED SNOW WAS ABOUT THREE INCHES THICK DIRECTLY ON TOP OF THE GROUND. ENVIRONMENTAL PROJECTS WAS HIRED TO SHOVEL THE SNOW INTO DRUMS. IN ADDITION, THEY REMOVED ABOUT SIX TONS OF SOIL FROM UNDER THE TRAILER.

IT WAS REPORTED THAT THE FUEL LINE DEVELOPED A LEAK BENEATH THE HOUSE SPILLING A SUBSTANTIAL AMOUNT OF FUEL.  IT WAS ESTIMATED THAT OVER 400 GALLONS WERE RELEASED.
     INVESTIGATION SHOWN THAT THE SITE IS SITUATED ON A SAND & GRAVEL AQUIFER MAKING CLEAN UP A RELATIVELY HIGH PRIORITY.  MS. MITCHELL'S WELL IS ALSO LOCATED ONLY A FEW FEET FROM THE SPILL AREA.  IT MAY ALSO BE NOTED THAT THE SPILL TOOK PLACE DIRECTLY BENEATH THE HOUSE MAKING EXCAVATION IMPOSSIBLE.  BECAUSE OF THIS DILEMMA TECHNICAL SERVICES STAFF WILL BE CONSULTED.

SCOTT VICNAIRE, CONCERNED RESIDENT ON SHAW HILL ROAD IN ETNA, CALLED TO REPORT THAT A LAB ANALYSIS OF HIS DRINKING WATER HAD LOW LEVELS OF GASOLINE.  IT WAS STATED THAT HE SUSPECTED THAT HIS NEIGHBOR DUMPED SOME GASOLINE DOWN HIS WELL.  INVESTIGATION OF THE INSIDE OF THE WELL CASING RULED IT OUT HOWEVER.  THE LOW LEVELS OF GASOLINE WERE PROBABLY DUE TO SELF CONTAMINATION.  IT MAY BE NOTED THAT THE WELL IS LOCATED VERY CLOSE TO AN ACTIVE GARAGE.  THE CASE WAS HANDED TO TECHNICAL SERVICES STAFF FOR FURTHER INVESTIGATION.

ON 10/28/96, 1820 HOURS CHRIS MARTIS CONTACTED ME TO SAY THAT HER AST HAD TIPPED OVER ABOUT 2.5 WEEKS AGO AND THAT HER WELL WAS CONTAMINATED.  SHE INDICATED THAT SHE HAD CALLED HER FUEL DELIVERY  COMPANY AND THEY DIDN'T HAVE A PLAN AS TO WHAT TO DO.  THE FUEL COMPANY DID MANAGE TO RIGHT THE AST SO THAT IT WOULD CONTINUE TO FUEL THE FURNACE-I ASSUME IT WAS THE FUEL COMPANY BECAUSE WHEN I GOT THERE THE TANK WAS TIED TO A TREE AND ALSO SUPPORTED BY TWO BY FOUR LUMBER.  I TALKED WITH THE FUEL VENDER AND LET THEM KNOW THAT CALLING US IS ALWAYS A GOOD PLACE TO START.  I LEARNED THAT THERE ONLY FUNCTION WAS TO DELIVER FUEL.  ANY OTHER TASKS WERE SUB CONTRACTED.

MY FIRST SITE VISIT WAS ON 10/30/96.  CHRIS HAD LEFT A SAMPLE OF HER WATER OUT-SINCE SHE WOULD NOT BE HOME DURING THE DAY- FOR ME TO CHECK OUT.  I COULD NOT SMELL ANY FUEL IN IT.  HOWEVER, WHEN I PUT A SAMPLER INTO THE WELL IT CAME OUT WITH ALMOST 2 FEET OF NEAT PRODUCT.  I CONTINUED BAILING UNTIL THERE WAS NO MORE TO RECOVER.  THE AMOUNT OF RECOVERED PRODUCT AT THAT TIME WAS ABOUT EIGHT GALLONS.  I VISITED THE NEARBY NEIGHBORS (THERE WERE THREE OF THEM) AND TALKED ABOUT QUARTERLY MONITORING.  I TALKED WITH CHRIS THAT EVENING AND ASKED IF SHE COULD RUN WATER THROUGH HER HOSE OUT SIDE.  I HAD HER RUN IT INTO THE ROAD DITCH, WHICH IS A RESPECTABLE DISTANCE FROM ANY WELLS.  SHE AGREED TO DO IT.  I ALSO DISCUSSED WHAT WAS GOING TO HAPPEN.  NAMELY, THERE WOULD BE SOME DIGGING, WE WOULD CONTINUE TO REMOVE FREE PRODUCT FROM HER WELL, WE WOULD PUT FILTERS ON, SHE WOULD BE ON QUARTERLY MONITORING AND SHE WOULD HAVE AN OPPORTUNITY TO APPLY TO THE AST CLEAN-UP FUND.  

THE NEXT DAY PHIL AND I PUMPED ANOTHER SEVEN GALLONS FROM THE WELL.  I BAILED IT ON SEVERAL, SUBSEQUENT OCCASIONS AND THE AMOUNT OF RECOVERY DROPPED SHARPLY.  THE THIRD BAILING PRODUCED ABOUT A QUART, THE FORTH ABOUT A CUP WHILE THE FIFTH AND SIXTH WAS A FEW MILLILITERS AND NONE DETECTED RESPECTIVELY.  MEANWHILE, ON 11/07/96,  WE DUG OUT 10 YD3 OF MILDLY CONTAMINATED SOIL.  THE HOLE WAS 2.5W X3.5L X1.3H YARDS AND THE HIGHEST READING WAS 1000 PPM.  THE EDGES TO THE HOLE WERE BELOW  DETECTION AND THE BEDROCK READ 220-300 IN THE MIDDLE OF THE SPILL AREA AND 50-100 AT THE EDGE OF THE HOLE.  ALSO ON 11/7/96 I ASKED NORM (OF NORLENS) TO CONTACT CHRIS ABOUT INSTALLING A FILTER.  

THE EXCAVATOR WAS H.E. BRIDGES.  ALSO, DOUG MARTIN OF MARTINS HEATING WAS ON SITE.  HE WAS THERE TO DEAL WITH THE AST REPLACEMENT.  HE WAS RETAINED A LITTLE LONGER SO THAT HE COULD HELP US DEAL WITH A PROPANE GAS TANK IN THE EVENT THAT IT HAD TO BE MOVED FOR THE SAKE OF THE EXCAVATION.

THE TERRAIN ON THAT PART OF FOGLER ROAD HAS A STEEP TOPOGRAPHICAL GRADIENT.  THE DIRECTION OF THIS GRADIENT IS ALMOST PERPENDICULAR TO THE SPILL AND THE WELL.  A REASONABLE EXPLANATION SEEMED TO BE THAT THE WELL WAS DOWN STRIKE FROM THE SPILL.  THE EXCAVATION REVEALED THAT THIS WAS INDEED THAT CASE.  FURTHERMORE, THE BEDROCK WAS 4 FEET FROM GRADE AT THE MOST AND 2.5 FEET AT THE CLOSEST.  TWO OF THE WELLS AT RISK ARE DOWN GRADIENT TOPOGRAPHICALLY.  HOPEFULLY THE STRIKE WILL PROTECT THESE WELLS.  THE DIP SEEMED TO BE VERTICAL, BUT IT MAY HAVE BEEN UPGRADIENT.  THE ROCK WAS SO SOFT THAT IT WAS HARD TO TELL.

ON APRIL 8, 2001 AT 1345 WE RECEIVED A CALL FROM SHELLY YANKOWSKY REPORTING A KEROSENE SPILL FROM AN OUTSIDE TANK AT HER HOME ON MERRYMAN RD. IN GLENBURN.  THE HEAVY WET SNOW BROKE OFF THE FILTER AT THE NIPPLE CONNECTION TO THE TANK CAUSING A SPILL OF ABOUT 175 GALLONS OF KEROSENE.  THEY HAVE A DRILLED WELL ABOUT TWENTY FEET AWAY FROM THE SPILL.
    I MET THE YANKOWSKYS, LOCAL CONTRACTOR MILTON KNOWLES AND L.A. PEARSON OIL AT THE SITE THAT AFTERNOON.  THE BUILDING HAS A CRAWLSPACE AND FROST WALL AND I FOUND SOME CONTAMINATED SOIL INSIDE THE CRAWLSPACE.  WE SHOVELLED THE SNOW AWAY FROM THE FILTER AND FOUND THAT THE SOIL WAS PRETTY CONTAMINATED.  WE AGREED TO REMOVE THE TANK AND EXCAVATE THE SOIL AND HAUL IT TO SAWYER'S THE NEXT MORNING WHICH WAS MONDAY.
     WE MET AS SCHEDULED AND L.A. PEARSON REMOVED THE OLD TANK AND CONTRACTOR MILTON KNOWLES EXCAVATED SIX YARDS OF CONTAMINATED SOIL AND WE ALSO REMOVED SOIL FROM THE CRAWLSPACE.  THE CONTAMINATED SOIL WAS BROUGHT TO SAWYER'S LANDFILL FOR DISPOSAL.  PEARSON OIL ALSO INSTALLED THE NEW TANK IN THE CRAWLSPACE.  I ADDED THE YANKOWSKY'S WELL TO THE QUARTERLY MONITORING PROGRAM AND HAD THE FIRE MARSHALL'S OFFICE SEND THEM AN AST INSURANCE APPLICATION FORM.

ERICK HOCHE CALLED TO REPORT THAT A CUSTOMER'S BASEMENT TANK HAD LEAKED. THE TANK WAS AT THE HOME OF EDMOND MATTHESON, MAIN STREET, DENNYSVILLE. MR. MATTHESON WAS DECEASED AND THE HOME WAS NOW OWN BY ROBERT MCGLAUFLIN OF SOUTHWEST LAKEWOOD, WASHINGTON. THE SPILL HAD BEEN DISCOVERED EARLIER IN THE WEEK AND BY THE TIME I WAS NOTIFIED, THE OLD TANK HAD BEEN REMOVED AND WHAT OIL WAS ON THE FLOOR HAD BEEN CLEANED UP BY MR. HOCHE'S COMPANY. 
   I MET MR. HOCHE AT THE SITE THAT AFTERNOON. THE HOME IS LOCATED ON THE WEST SHORE OF THE DENNYS RIVER AND MAIN STREET. THE 275-GALLON TANK WAS LOCATED IN A SECTION OF THE BASEMENT THAT HAS A CONCRETE FLOOR AND NO SURFACE DRAINS WERE FOUND. I SAW NO EVIDENCE OF THE OIL HAVING REACHED THE RIVER. MR. HOCHE SAID THAT UPON HIS ARRIVAL, THERE WAS A SMALL PUDDLE OF OIL IN THE NORTHWEST CORNER OF THE ROOM. HIS COMPANY PROVIDES OIL FOR THE HOME AS WELL AS BURNER SERVICE AND HE FELT THERE SHOULD HAVE BEEN BETWEEN 160 AND 170 GALLONS IN THE TANK. HE ESTIMATED THAT IT WAS NOT MORE THAT FIVE GALLONS, THIS WAS COLLECTED WITH SORBENT PADS. THERE HAD BEEN A LOT OF WOOD SCRAPS ON THE FLOOR THAT HAD SOAKED UP OIL. HIS COMPANY REMOVED THIS WOOD AND COVERED THE STAINED CONCRETE WITH SPEEDI-DRI. THIS WILL RECOVER SOME OF THE OIL THAT HAD CAUSED THE STAIN. I BELIEVE THAT THE REMAINING OIL HAD SEEPED THROUGH THE FLOOR IN THE NORTHWEST CORNER AND HAD BEEN ABSORBED BY THE SOIL UNDERNEATH. IT WOULD BE UNLIKELY THAT THIS OIL COULD REACH THE RIVER OR CAUSE ENVIRONMENTAL HARM. FURTHER CLEANUP IN THE BASEMENT SHOULD CONSIST OF REMOVING THE SPEEDI-DRI AFTER IT HAS ABSORBED THE AVAILABLE OIL IN THE CONCRETE AND VENTING THE BASEMENT. THE VENTING WILL TAKE CARE OF THE REMAINING ODOR. THE SPEED AT WHICH THE VENTING WILL ACCOMPLISH THIS WILL DEPEND A GREAT DEAL ON THE TYPE OF WEATHER. DRY AIR OBVIOUSLY WILL GET THE JOB DONE MUCH FASTER THAN HUMID AIR. HOWEVER, ONCE SOME SIMPLE FANS HAVE BEEN INSTALLED, I'D EXPECT THAT THE ODOR PROBLEM WOULD BE CONTROLLED IN A FEW WEEKS.
   THERE IS ANOTHER ISSUE AND THAT IS THE WELL. IT IS A DRILLED WELL ON THE FRONT LAWN AND IS ONLY 10 FEET OR 12 FEET FROM THE SPILL SITE. HOWEVER THE GROUNDWATER TABLE (WHICH IS EFFECTIVELY THE RIVER LEVEL) SHOULD PROTECT THE WELL FROM DRAWING IN ANY OIL NOT BOUND TO SOIL PARTICLES. MR. HOCHE THINKS IT'S LIKELY THAT THE SOIL IN THE AREA IS CLAY. I WOULD RECOMMEND THAT THE WELL BE PLACE ON QUARTERLY MONITORING WHERE THE WATER IS SAMPLED EVERY THREE MONTHS.
