properties.SUMMARY:
IN 2012, WHILE INVESTIGATING RELEASES AT THE ABUTTING CUMBERLAND FARMS (SEE SPILL REPORT # P-761-2012), THE MEDEP CONDUCTED AN INTERVIEW AT ANGELONES PIZZA AND DISCOVERED THAT THE RESTAURANT WAS FORMERLY A MOBIL GAS STATION. THE MEDEP NOTED THAT FORMER ON-SITE USTS WERE REMOVED FROM THE SITE IN 1969-1970. THE MEDEP NOTED EVIDENCE OF FORMER DISPENSER ISLAND ALONG WASHINGTON AVENUE AND OCEAN AVENUE. THE MEDEP CONCLUDED THAT THAT BASED ON THE PRE-1991 DATE OF THE UST REMOVAL, A UST CLOSURE ASSESSMENT WAS NOT REQUIRED AND THAT A PHASE II ESA WOULD BE PRUDENT PRIOR TO SITE REDEVELOPMENT.

IN 2017, AN ENVIRONMENTAL RECORDS REVIEW AND CITY FILE SEARCH (ERR) WAS COMPLETED FOR THE SITE. THE ERR IDENTIFIED THE HISTORICAL USE OF THE PROPERTY AS A GASOLINE STATION WITH UNDERGROUND STORAGE TANKS (USTS), AND TWO ABUTTING PROPERTIES AS GASOLINE STATIONS. BASED UPON THAT INFORMATION THE PROPERTY WAS IDENTIFIED AS HIGH RISK DUE TO THE POTENTIAL FOR PETROLEUM-IMPACTED SOIL, SOIL VAPOR, AND GROUNDWATER BENEATH THE SITE.

A PHASE II ENVIRONMENTAL SITE ASSESSMENT (ESA) WAS COMPLETED TO ADDRESS THE HIGH RISK STATUS PRESENTED IN THE IN THE 2017 ERR. DURING THE PHASE II ESA, PETROLEUM HYDROCARBONS WERE IDENTIFIED IN THE SITE SOILS AT CONCENTRATIONS BELOW REGULATORY GUIDELINES. NAPTHALENE, C9 ALIPHATICS, AND THE CHLORINATED SOLVENT TETRACHLOROETHENE (PCE) WERE IDENTIFIED IN SUB-SLAB SOIL VAPOR, AND ONLY NAPTHALENE AND C9 ALIPHATICS EXCEEDED THE REGULATORY GUIDELINES FOR RESIDENTIAL USE.

THE 2018 PHASE I ESA COMPLETED BY ST.GERMAIN IDENTIFIED THE PETROLEUM IMPACTS TO SOIL AND SOIL VAPOR, AND THE PCE IMPACTS TO SOIL VAPOR AS A RECOGNIZED ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITION (REC). NO FURTHER INVESTIGATION WAS RECOMMENDED SINCE THE PHASE II ESA INVESTIGATION CONDUCTED IN 2018 ADEQUATELY ADDRESSED THE IDENTIFIED REC. THE 2018 PHASE I ESA DID RECOMMEND THE FOLLOWING
- INSTALLATION OF AN ENGINEERED VAPOR BARRIER AND/OR A PASSIVE OR ACTIVE SUBS LAB DEPRESSURIZATION SYSTEM FOR ANY OCCUPIED STRUCTURE INTENDED FOR COMMERCIAL OR RESIDENTIAL USE.
- IF CONTAMINATED SOIL OR GROUNDWATER ENCOUNTERED DURING ANY FUTURE SITE WORK, A QUALIFIED ENVIRONMENTAL PROFESSIONAL, OR THE MEDEP SHOULD BE CONTACTED TO DETERMINE THE PROPER MANAGEMENT OF THE CONTAMINATED MEDIA.

AN APPLICATION TO VRAP WAS COMPLETED BY ST.GERMAIN ON BEHALF OF THE NEW SITE OWNER QUATTRUCCI AND ROUDA, LLC IN SEPTEMBER 2018. BASED UPON THE 2018 VRAP APPLICATION THE MEDEP REQUIRED AN EMMP, AND THIS REPORT DOCUMENTS THE ACTIVITIES UNDERTAKEN IN GENERAL COMPLIANCE WITH EMMP.

THE SITE HAS BEEN REFERRED TO MARK WOODRUFF OF THE DIVISION OF TECHNICAL SERVICES AS THERE IS A DRINKING WATER WELL ON SITE.

NO FURTHER ACTION BY THE DIVISION OF RESPONSE SERVICES IS NECESSARY IN THIS MATTER.

properties.SUMMARY:
A PHASE I ESA WAS COMPLETED BY RANSOM IN NOVEMBER 2018 AS PART OF THE CITY OF HALLOWELLS BROWNFIELDS ASSESSMENT PROGRAM. THE PHASE I ESA IDENTIFIED RECOGNIZED ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS
(RECS) IN CONNECTION WITH THE SITES FORMER USE AS AN AUTOMOTIVE SERVICE GARAGE. IN ADDITION, POTENTIAL
ENVIRONMENTAL CONCERNS WERE IDENTIFIED WITH THE ABUTTING, UPGRADIENT PROPERTY TO THE NORTH, BUTLER
MACMASER AUTOMOTIVE MACHINING. ALONG WITH THE INFERRED USE OF SOLVENTS WITHIN A MACHINE SHOP, THIS
ABUTTING PROPERTY WAS IDENTIFIED AS A RESOURCE CONSERVATION AND RECOVERY ACT (RCRA) GENERATOR. THE
PHASE II ESA WAS DESIGNED TO COLLECT SUFFICIENT DATA TO CONFIRM OR DISMISS THE RECS IDENTIFIED DURING THE
PHASE I ESA, TO IDENTIFY POTENTIAL EXPOSURE RISKS, AND TO EVALUATE THE SUITABILITY OF THE SITE FOR POTENTIAL
COMMERCIAL REDEVELOPMENT.

DURING THE COURSE OF THE PHASE II ESA, RANSOM OVERSAW THE ADVANCEMENT OF FIVE SOIL BORINGS, FOUR TEST
PITS, ALONG WITH THE INSTALLATION OF FOUR TEMPORARY MONITORING WELLS AND TWO SOIL VAPOR SAMPLING POINTS.
DURING THIS TIME, RANSOM COLLECTED SOIL, GROUNDWATER AND SOIL VAPOR SAMPLES FOR LABORATORY ANALYSIS.

VANDALISM CAUSED THE DISCHARGE OF APPROXIMATELY 150 GALLONS OF KEROSENE.  THE TANK FROM WHICH THE OIL WAS RELEASED HAD BEEN TAKEN OUT OF SERVICE THE PREVIOUS YEAR IN FAVOR OF A HEAT PUMP.  THE FIROMATIC VALVE WAS CLOSED AND THE MONITOR HEATER WAS REMOVED, BUT THE SUPPLY LINE WAS NOT PLUGGED.  THIS IS A PART TIME RESIDENCE SO SAID VANDALISM OCCURRED WHEN THE HOMEOWNER WAS AWAY, WHO RETURNED TO DISCOVER KEROSENE COVERING HALF OF THE SQUARE FOOTAGE OF THE FIRST FLOOR.  THE FIROMATIC WAS OPENED WHICH RELEASED FUEL FROM THE TANK THROUGH THE SUPPLY LINE, DEPOSITING IT INTO THE INTERIOR OF THE HOME.  SPILLED PRODUCT AFFECTED ENGINEERED FLOATING FLOOR, MULTIPLE SUB FLOORS, JOISTS AND SPRAY INSULATION BEFORE MIGRATING THOUGH A CONDUIT IN THE CLOSET FLOOR INTO THE DIRT FLOOR CRAWLSPACE BELOW.  OIL TRAVELED INTO THE BATHROOM BELOW THE TUB THROUGH THE CLOSET UNDERNEATH THE STAIRS AND AFFECTED SHEETROCK, SILL PLATES, AND PARTITION WALL FRAMING THROUGHOUT THE LIVING ROOM AND INTO THE KITCHEN.  REMOVAL OF CONTAMINATED MATERIALS WAS A SIGNIFICANT UNDERTAKING WHICH INCLUDED FLOORING/SUBFLOORING, SHEETROCK, AND SPRAY FOAM INSULATION.  JOISTS AND OTHER STRUCTURAL AND PARTITION MEMBERS WERE ENCAPSULATED TO MAINTAIN THE BUILDING'S INTEGRITY.  IN THE CRAWLSPACE, APPROXIMATELY SIX TONS OF SOIL WERE REMOVED FROM THE CENTER OF THE SPACE WHICH CONSTITUTED THE MAJORITY OF THE CONTAMINATION.  THE LOGISTICS WERE CHALLENGING DUE TO MULTIPLE SUPPORT COLUMNS AMID OR ADJACENT TO THE SPILL AREA.  PERFORATED PIPING WAS INSTALLED AND STUBBED OUT FOR A DEPRESSION SYSTEM, THEN CONCRETE WAS POURED OVER THE ENTIRE AREA TO SUPPRESS VAPORS.  AFTER SOME NEW JOISTS AND A NEW SUBFLOOR WERE INSTALLED, THE SPRAY FOAM WAS REPLACED ON THE UNDERSIDE OF THE FIRST FLOOR.  OUR DIVISION OF TECHNICAL SERVICES PROVIDED EXTENDED INDOOR AIR QUALITY MONITORING.  NO FURTHER DIVISION OF RESPONSE SERVICES ACTION NECESSARY.

THE RESTAURANT HAS CHANGED OWNERSHIP AND NAMES THROUGHOUT THE YEARS BUT HAS OPERATED AS A RESTAURANT DATING BACK TO 1968. PRIOR TO 1968, THIS PORTION OF THE SITE OPERATED AS A SARDINE FACTORY WHERE THE SALTING, SMOKING AND CANNING OF FISH TOOK PLACE DATING BACK TO THE LATE 1800S. A MANUFACTURED GAS PLANT (MGP)
WAS HISTORICALLY LOCATED IN WHAT IS NOW THE GRAVEL PARKING LOT AT 171 WATER STREET. THE MGP OPERATED FROM THE LATE 1800S TO CIRCA 1930. A GASOMETER WAS PRESENT AT THE CURRENT LOCATION OF THE RESIDENTIAL PROPERTY DURING THE OPERATION OF THE MGP. ADDITIONALLY, ON THE 1933 SANBORN FIRE INSURANCE MAP, AN
UNDERGROUND STORAGE TANK (UST) IS DEPICTED TO THE SOUTH OF THE RIGHT-OF-WAY (ROW) ACCESS ROAD THAT EXTENDS ACROSS THE SITE KNOWN AS BUCKNAM PLACE.
properties.SUMMARY:
RANSOM COMPLETED AN ASTM COMPLIANT PHASE I ESA FOR THE SITE IN OCTOBER 2019. THE PHASE I ESA IDENTIFIED RECOGNIZED ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS (RECS) IN CONNECTION WITH THE SITE INCLUDING THE HISTORICAL OPERATIONS AS AN MGP AND THE PRESENCE OF A UST AS DEPICTED ON THE 1933 SANBORN FIRE INSURANCE MAP.

ACTIVITIES CONDUCTED DURING THE PHASE II ESA INCLUDED THE COMPLETION OF A GEOPHYSICAL SURVEY TO CLEAR THE PROPOSED BORING LOCATIONS OF POTENTIAL SUBSURFACE UTILITIES AND TO SEARCH FOR THE PRESENCE OF UNDERGROUND STRUCTURES (USTS, GASOMETER AND OTHER REMNANTS OF THE FORMER MGP), THE ADVANCEMENT OF EIGHT SOIL BORINGS, THE SCREENING OF SOIL FOR THE PRESENCE OF ORGANIC VAPOR WITH A PHOTOIONIZATION DETECTOR (PID) AND THE COLLECTION AND CHEMICAL ANALYSIS OF SOIL SAMPLES.

REMOVED IN THE PAST TO FACILITATE THE CONSTRUCTION OF THE FORMER GASWORKS BUILDING, GASOMETER AND UST. THE SURFICIAL GEOLOGY AT THE SITE IS IDENTIFIED AS UNDIFFERENTIATED THIN DRIFT WHICH IS DESCRIBED AS AREAS OF MANY BEDROCK OUTCROPS AND/OR NEAR-SURFACE BEDROCK WHERE THE SURFICIAL MATERIALS HAVE NOT BEEN MAPPED. properties.SUMMARY:
THE RESULTS OF A PHASE I ESA COMPLETED FOR THE SITE WERE PRESENTED IN A REPORT DATED SEPTEMBER 3, 2019. THE ASSESSMENT IDENTIFIED POTENTIAL ISSUES OF ENVIRONMENTAL CONCERN AS A RESULT OF HISTORICAL LAND USE AS A RAILYARD. UP TO AS MANY AS NINE RAIL SPURS OPERATED ON THE SITE FROM AS FAR BACK AS 1870. BLACK COLORED SURFACE SOIL IN MANY AREAS OF THE SITE INDICATES THE LIKELY PRESENCE OF POTENTIALLY HAZARDOUS SUBSTANCES INCLUDING COAL ASH, METALS, AND POLY-AROMATIC HYDROCARBONS (PAHS) ASSOCIATED WITH RAILROAD OPERATIONS. HISTORICAL SITE USE AS A RAILYARD WAS IDENTIFIED AS A RECOGNIZED ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITION (REC) IN CONNECTION WITH THE SITE. 

IN 1995, A 1,000 GALLON HEATING OIL UNDERGROUND STORAGE TANK (UST) WAS ABANDONED IN PLACE AT THE 370 DANFORTH STREET RESIDENCE LOCATED NORTH OF AND TOPOGRAPHICALLY UPGRADIENT RELATIVE TO THE SITE. A UST SITE ASSESSMENT REPORT WAS NOT FOUND DURING THE COURSE OF THIS PHASE I ESA. ANY UNDOCUMENTED HISTORIC SPILLS OR RELEASES ASSOCIATED WITH THIS TANK AND UNDERGROUND PIPING COULD HAVE IMPACTED THE SITE AND WAS, THEREFORE, CONSIDERED TO BE A REC IN CONNECTION WITH THE SITE.

BASED ON THESE RESULTS, IT WAS RECOMMENDED THAT A PHASE II ESA BE CONDUCTED CONSISTING OF OBTAINING BOTH SOIL AND GROUNDWATER SAMPLES FOR FIELD SCREENING AND LABORATORY ANALYSIS. THE PURPOSE OF THIS PHASE II ESA WAS TO IDENTIFY AND CHARACTERIZE CONTAMINANTS THAT MAY BE PRESENT IN THE SOIL AND GROUNDWATER

properties.SUMMARY:
ON FEBRUARY 19, 2019, AN ESTIMATED 175 GALLONS OF FUEL OIL WAS RELEASED ONTO THE CONCRETE BASEMENT FLOOR OF THE SITE BUILDING FROM AN ABOVEGROUND FUEL OIL TANK AS A RESULT OF AN IMPROPERLY INSTALLED OIL FILTER. MEDEP AND THEIR SUBCONTRACTOR RESPONDED TO THE SPILL THAT EVENING AND MEDEP SPILL #P-144-2019 WAS ASSIGNED. PETROLEUM PRODUCT WAS REMOVED FROM THE FLOOR USING SORBENT MATERIALS, AND OIL-IMPACTED HOMEOWNER BELONGINGS AS WELL AS BUILDING MATERIALS WERE REMOVED AND PROPERLY DISPOSED OFF-SITE.

FOLLOWING THE INITIAL CLEANUP ACTIONS, SITE REMEDIATION ACTIVITIES WERE IMPLEMENTED. REMEDIATION ACTIVITIES INCLUDED REMOVAL OF THE CONCRETE FLOOR AND PETROLEUM-CONTAMINATED SOILS BENEATH THE FLOOR IN THE SPILL AREA. CONFIRMATORY SOIL SAMPLES SUGGESTED THE MAJORITY OF THE CONTAMINATION WAS REMOVED. HOWEVER, CONTAMINATED SOIL WAS NOT REMOVED IN CERTAIN AREAS BENEATH THE BUILDING FOUNDATION IN ORDER TO MAINTAIN STRUCTURAL STABILITY OF THE RESIDENCE. A SUB-SLAB DEPRESSURIZATION SYSTEM (SSDS) WAS
CONSTRUCTED TO MINIMIZE CONTAMINANT VAPOR INTRUSION INTO THE RESIDENCE. THE CONCRETE FLOOR WAS SUBSEQUENTLY REPAIRED AND SEALED WITH A CONCRETE SEALANT COMPOUND.

properties.DESCRIPTION:
THE SITE CONSISTS OF SEVERAL COMMERCIAL STRUCTURES, ASPHALT PAVED AREAS, UNPAVED AREAS, AND VEGETATED/LANDSCAPED AREAS IN THE SOUTHERN PORTION. THE CENTRAL AND NORTHERN PORTIONS OF THE SITE ARE OCCUPIED BY WETLANDS AND AN OVERHEAD ELECTRICAL TRANSMISSION RIGHT-OF-WAY. THE SITE STRUCTURES CONSIST OF A MAIN BUILDING (IDENTIFIED AS BUILDING 1), A SECONDARY BUILDING (IDENTIFIED AS BUILDING 2), TWO SALT SHEDS, AN OFFICE TRAILER, AND A WOODEN SHED. BUILDING 1 IS USED AS AN OFFICE SPACE, VEHICLE MAINTENANCE GARAGE, AND STORAGE OF PARTS AND OILS. THE REMAINING STRUCTURES ARE USED FOR STORAGE AND/OR OFFICE SPACE. THE SITE STRUCTURES ARE REPORTEDLY HEATED BY NATURAL GAS.
BUILDING 1 WAS FORMERLY HEATED BY THE EXISTING DIESEL UNDERGROUND STORAGE TANK (UST) UNTIL 2013. BUILDING 2 WAS FORMERLY HEATED BY A 2,000-GALLON WASTE OIL ABOVEGROUND STORAGE TANK LOCATED WITHIN THE STRUCTURE UNTIL 2016. FOUR USTS WERE INSTALLED AT THE SITE IN APPROXIMATELY 1972 AND REMOVED IN 1995. THE USTS INCLUDED ONE 4,000-GALLON WASTE OIL UST AND ONE 6,000-GALLON GASOLINE UST LOCATED SOUTHWEST OF BUILDING 1, AND ONE 10,000-GALLON GASOLINE UST AND ONE 10,000-GALLON DIESEL UST LOCATED SOUTHEAST OF BUILDING 1. CURRENT ON-SITE USTS CONSIST OF ONE 10,000-GALLON GASOLINE UST AND ONE 14,000-GALLON DIESEL UST, WHICH WERE INSTALLED IN 1995 IN THE SOUTHERNMOST PORTION OF THE SITE ALONG NORTH STREET.

properties.SUMMARY:
RAY PLUMBING CALLED TO REPORT THE POTENTIAL RELEASE OF POLYCHLORINATED BIPHENYLS (PCBS) OIL IN A RESIDENTIAL HOME DRINKING WATER WELL. THE SOURCE OF THE RELEASE WAS FROM AN OLD WELL THAT CORRODED AND LOST ITS INTERNAL LUBRICATION OIL. SAMPLES FROM THE WELL WERE SENT OUT TO BE TESTED TO DETERMINE THE LEVEL OF PCBS PRESENT. IT WAS DETERMINED THE LEVEL OF PCBS WERE BELOW THAT OF WHICH TO BE CONCERNED. TECHNICAL SERVICES CONDUCTED THE CLEAN-UP WITH ONE OF THEIR PORTABLE TREATMENT TRAILERS. A SURFACTANT WAS USED TO BREAKDOWN AND OIL AND CLEAN THE CASING OF THE WELL. IT IS ESTIMATED THAT 440 GALLONS OF WATER WERE PUMPED THROUGH THE TREATMENT TRAILER IN ORDER TO ACHIEVE A CLEAN DRINKING WATER WELL. THE DRINKING WATER WELL IS NOW CONSIDERED CLEAN FOR REUSE. NO OTHER RECEPTORS WERE IMPACTED.

NO FURTHER ACTION BY THE DIVISION OF RESPONSE SERVICES IS ANTICIPATED AT THIS TIME.

A HOMEOWNER WAS CONCERNED ABOUT THE QUALITY OF HER WELL BOTH DUG AND DRILLED SENT SAMPLES TO THE STATE LAB FOR TESTING.  A TECHNICIAN SMELLED A FUEL SMELL IN THE DUG WELL SAMPLE AND ALERTED THE HOMEOWNER.   I INVESTIGATED THE AREA AND WELL.   THERE WAS NO OBSERVABLE SIGNS OF CONTAMINATION IN THE WELL OR FROM TAPS.   THE DUG WELL WAS USED FOR OUTSIDE TAPS ONLY.  THERE WERE NO LIKELY SCENARIOS FOR CONTAMINATION FROM NEIGHBORING PROPERTY.  I SUSPECT THERE WAS NO FUEL OIL CONTAMINATION, AND ADVISED THE HOMEOWNER.  THE HOMEOWNER REQUESTED WE TEST THE WATER FOR POTENTIAL OIL CONTAMINATION.  THE RESULTS OF THE WATER TEST INDICATED THERE WAS NO PETROLEUM CONTAMINATION. 

NO FURTHER ACTION BY THE DIVISION OF RESPONSE SERVICES IS EXPECTED AT THIS TIME.

I RECEIVED REPORT OF A SMALL OIL SPILL AT THE RETIREMENT HOME IN HARTLAND. I ARRIVED ON SITE AND HELPED THE OIL TECHNICIANS CLEAN UP THE OIL SPILL. UNFORTUNATELY OIL WICKED UNDER THE SILL OF THE ADJOINING INTERIOR WALL AND ONTO THE SHEETROCK. DEAD RIVER HIRED A CONTRACTOR TO REMOVE THE SHEETROCK AND UNDER SILL FOR THE INTERIOR WALL THAT WAS IMPACTED. UNFORTUNATELY EVEN AFTER THE REMOVAL OF THE OIL IMPACTED SURFACES TOOK PLACE, THERE CONTINUED TO BE AN OIL VAPOR IN THE HOME. MORE PROFESSIONAL CLEANING WAS PERFORMED. THE OIL VAPOR WAS EVENTUALLY EVACUATED FROM THE BUILDING WITH VENTILATION AND CLEANING. HOWEVER THE RESIDENCE OF THE HOME COMPLAINED OF CONTINUED VAPOR IN THE SPACE. NO READINGS OF OIL VAPOR WERE DETECTED ON AIR MONITORING INSTRUMENTS. TECHNICAL SERVICES OF THE DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION INSTALLED AND GATHERED A SAMPLE OF THE AIR SPACE BY A SUMA CANISTER. THE RESULTS FROM THIS TEST PROVED THAT NO OIL VAPOR REMAINED IN THE SPACE. NO FURTHER ACTION NEEDED.

properties.SUMMARY:
THE DEPARTMENT WAS NOTIFIED OF A 5 GALLON SPILL OF #2 HEATING OIL RESULTING FROM A CORROSION HOLE IN AN ABOVEGROUND STORAGE TANK (AST).  THE AST IS LOCATED IN THE BASEMENT WITH A CONCRETE FLOOR WITH A PERIMETER DRAIN GOING AROUND IT.  A SUMP PUMP IS ALSO LOCATED IN THE BASEMENT.  THE TWO UNIT BUILDING IS SERVED BY PUBLIC WATER.

UPON THE DEPARTMENT'S ARRIVAL ON SCENE, THE HOMEOWNER HAD CONTACTED DEAD RIVER OIL COMPANY AND THEY WERE IN THE PROCESS OF PUMPING THE OIL FROM THE AST.  DEAD RIVER ALSO RELOCATED THE AST SO THAT THE DEPARTMENT COULD PROCEED WITH THE INVESTIGATION.  TECHNICAL SERVICES WAS REQUESTED TO DRILL HOLES INTO THE FLOOR AS THE CONCRETE APPEARED TO BE THIN AND THE PERIMETER DRAIN WAS BARE SOIL.  TECHNICAL SERVICES FOUND ELEVATED VOLATILE ORGANIC COMPOUNDS (VOCS) BELOW THE FLOOR AND RECOMMENDED REMOVING THE PORTION OF THE FLOOR UNDER THE AST.

AN AREA OF APPROXIMATELY 12 FEET BY 14 FEET AND EIGHT INCHES DEEP WAS DUG AND A VENTILATION SYSTEM WAS INSTALLED FOR THE REMAINING SOIL.  TECHNICAL SERVICES WILL CONTINUE TO MONITOR THE VENTILATION SYSTEM.

NO FURTHER ACTION REQUIRED OF RESPONSE SERVICES AT THIS TIME.

properties.DESCRIPTION: HOME
properties.SUMMARY:
THE DEPARTMENT WAS NOTIFIED OF A 5 GALLON SPILL OF #2 HEATING OIL RESULTING FROM A CORRODED FILTER BASKET.  THE LEAK SPILLED ONTO A CONCRETE FLOOR AND PUDDLED UNDER THE FURNACE.  THE BURNER TECHNICIAN REPLACED THE FILTER BASKET AND THE DEPARTMENT BEGAN THE CLEAN-UP.  THE PROPERTY IS SERVED BY A DRILLED DRINKING WATER WELL, APPROXIMATELY 300 FEET IN DEPTH.

SORBENT PADS WERE USED TO COLLECT THE FREE PRODUCT AND THE FLOOR WAS WASHED WITH A RAM FAN EXHAUSTING THE BASEMENT. THE DIVISION OF TECHNICAL SERVICES VISITED THE PROPERTY AND DRILLED A SERIES OF HOLES INTO THE CONCRETE FLOOR TO DETERMINE THE EXTENT OF THE SPILL BELOW THE SLAB.  VAPORS, AS MEASURED WITH A PHOTOIONIZATION DETECTOR, WERE HIGH ENOUGH TO JUSTIFY THE INSTALLATION OF A PETROLEUM MANAGEMENT FAN AND SEALING THE FLOOR.  THE DEPARTMENT HIRED ALLSTATE ENVIRONMENTAL SERVICES TO REPLACE THE CONCRETE BLOCKS BELOW THE FURNACE, WATER PRESSURE TANK, AND HOT WATER TANK.  THEY ALSO WASHED THE FLOOR AGAIN AND APPLIED RADON SEAL TO THE FLOOR FOLLOWED BY A PRIMER AND SEALANT.  TECHNICAL SERVICES INSTALLED A PETROLEUM MANAGEMENT FAN TO EXHAUST THE VAPORS BELOW THE FLOOR.

NO FURTHER ACTION REQUIRED OF RESPONSE SERVICES AT THIS TIME.

properties.DESCRIPTION: HOME
properties.SUMMARY:
ON 03/30/2020 AN OIL SPILL WAS DISCOVERED IN THE BASEMENT OF A RESIDENTIAL HOME AT 10 CANNON HILL RD. IN LIMERICK, ME. THE SPILL OCCURRED DUE TO A CORROSION HOLE IN THE BOTTOM OF A TANK NO LONGER IN USE. THE TANK HAD NOT BEEN IN USE SINCE SOMETIME IN 2018, WHEN THE FURNACE WAS CONDEMNED AND THE HOMEOWNER SWITCHED TO PROPANE HEAT. 

IT IS LIKELY THAT THE TANK HAD A SLIGHT LEAK OVER AN EXTENDED PERIOD OF TIME AS HOMEOWNER/TENANTS RARELY ENTERED THE BASEMENT. AFTER HAVING SPRAY FOAM INSULATION INSTALLED IN THE BASEMENT, RESIDENTS BEGAN TO SMELL OIL. IT IS BELIEVED THAT THE TANK WAS AGITATED DURING THE SPRAY FOAM APPLICATION PROCESS, RESULTING IN A LARGER LEAK. 

JP CARROLL FUEL COMPANY WAS CALLED TO REMOVE THE FURNACE AND TANK. JP CARROLL DISCOVERED THE ACTIVE LEAK. THE BURNER TECH ON SCENE STOPPED THE LEAK AND USED ABSORBENT PADS TO COLLECT FREE PRODUCT. AT THIS TIME, JP CARROLL CALLED MAINE DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION (MDEP) TO REPORT THE SPILL. THE REMAINING OIL WAS PUMPED FROM THE DAMAGED TANK. ONCE EMPTY, THE TANK WAS CLEANED, CUT, AND REMOVED BY JP CARROLL. JP CARROLL, WHO ALSO REMOVED THE OLD FURNACE. MOVING FORWARD, THE HOME WILL NOT HAVE A NEW OIL TANK INSTALLED AND WILL USE PROPANE HEAT. 

ALLSTATE ENVIRONMENTAL WAS HIRED FOR CLEANUP AND REMEDIATION. MDEP ENGINEER DON WHITE WAS INVOLVED IN REMEDIATION. 

DUE TO A LOSS OF OIL THROUGH VARIOUS OPENINGS IN THE CONCRETE FLOOR, IT WAS DECIDED TO REMOVE 2 SECTIONS OF FLOOR APPROXIMATELY 1.5'X10' AND 2.5'X5'. THE TWO SECTIONS OF CONCRETE CONNECTED TO A 6'X6' DEPRESSION IN THE FLOOR WITH A CONCRETE BOTTOM APPROXIMATELY 10" BELOW THE REST OF THE FLOOR. THIS DEPRESSION SERVED AS A GRAVITY DRAINING SUMP THAT DRAINS THROUGH A CLAY PIPE TO AN OUTFALL IN THE CORNER OF THE BASEMENT. THE OUTFALL PIPE IN THE CORNER OF THE BASEMENT DAYLIGHTS IN THE ROADSIDE DRAINAGE DITCH. REMOVING THE 1.5'X10' SECTION OF FLOOR EXPOSED THE CLAY PIPE AND ALLOWED FOR REMOVAL. DUE TO SEDIMENT BLOCKING THE CLAY PIPE, OIL WAS CONTAINED IN THE BASEMENT. NO EVIDENCE OF OIL WAS FOUND OUTSIDE THE HOME. THE 2.5'X5' SECTION OF FLOOR WAS REMOVED ENDING WHERE THE DAMAGED TANK SAT. FREE PRODUCT WAS DISCOVERED BELOW THE CONCRETE WHERE THE TANK SAT. 

ALL FREE PRODUCT WAS REMOVED AS WELL AS CONTAMINATED WATER FOUND SUB SLAB AND IN THE 6'X6' DEPRESSION IN THE FLOOR USING A VACUUM TRUCK. CONTAMINATED SOIL AND CONCRETE WERE REMOVED. REMAINING CONCRETE WAS THOROUGHLY WASHED AND RINSED. OPENINGS IN THE FLOOR, INCLUDING THE 6'X6' DEPRESSION WERE BACKFILLED WITH CRUSHED STONE. A SUB SLAB DEPRESSURIZATION SYSTEM (SSDS) WAS INSTALLED WITH PIPING EXTENDING TO ALL EXCAVATED AREAS. TO CREATE AIR SPACE FOR THE SSDS TO FUNCTION PROPERLY, A NEW SUMP WAS INSTALLED TO DRAW DOWN THE GROUND WATER. ALL WATER PUMPED FROM THE SUMP WILL DISCHARGE OUTSIDE AFTER PASSING THROUGH A CARBON FILTER. ALL PIPING AND EXCAVATED AREAS WERE COVERED IN CRUSHED STONE, A PLASTIC VAPOR BARRIER, AND LASTLY NEW CONCRETE. WATER DISCHARGED FROM NEWLY INSTALLED SUMP IS RUN THROUGH A CARBON FILTER BEFORE DISCHARGING TO THE DRAINAGE DITCH NEAR THE ROAD. THIS CARBON FILTER IS EXPECTED TO BE TEMPORARY AND WILL BE MONITORED BY MDEP TECH SERVICES ENGINEER DON WHITE MOVING FORWARD.

THIS HOME AS WELL AS NEIGHBORING PROPERTIES ARE ON PUBLIC WATER, THEREFORE, THERE IS NO SIGNIFICANT THREAT TO DRINKING WATER. GIVEN OIL WAS NOT OBSERVED OUTSIDE OF THE HOME, THERE IS LIKELY NO THREAT TO SURROUNDING PROPERTIES OR ENVIRONMENT. 

NO FURTHER ACTION FROM MDEP RESPONSE SERVICES AT THIS TIME.

PAPER ATTACHMENT

properties.DESCRIPTION:
THE SITE IS LOCATED IN A RESIDENTIAL AREA OF GARDINER AND IS IDENTIFIED BY THE CITY OF GARDINER ASSESSOR¿S OFFICE AS MAP 32, LOTS 23 AND 23A, WHICH CORRESPOND TO 150 AND 152 DRESDEN AVENUE, RESPECTIVELY. THE SITE ENCOMPASSES APPROXIMATELY 5.09 ACRES AND IS LOCATED ON THE EASTERN SIDE OF DRESDEN AVENUE,
APPROXIMATELY 500 FEET NORTH OF THE DRESDEN AVENUE AND COTTAGE STREET INTERSECTION.

THE SITE IS IMPROVED WITH THREE BUILDINGS IDENTIFIED AS THE HORIZON CLINIC PROGRAM BUILDING, THE FAMILY MEDICINE BUILDING, AND THE BOILER HOUSE. THE HORIZON CLINIC PROGRAM BUILDING WAS INITIALLY CONSTRUCTED CIRCA 1920S AND HAS UNDERGONE IMPROVEMENTS, RENOVATIONS AND ADDITIONS OVER THE YEARS TO ITS CURRENT STATE CONSISTING OF TWO FLOORS AND A BASEMENT ENCOMPASSING A FOOTPRINT OF APPROXIMATELY 14,050 SQUARE FEET. THE FAMILY MEDICINE BUILDING WAS CONSTRUCTED IN 1977 CONSISTING OF A GROUND FLOOR AND WALK OUT BASEMENT ENCOMPASSING A FOOTPRINT OF APPROXIMATELY 6,300 SQUARE FEET. THE BOILER HOUSE WAS CONSTRUCTED CIRCA 1920 AND CONSISTS OF TWO FLOORS AND A WALKOUT BASEMENT ENCOMPASSING A FOOTPRINT OF APPROXIMATELY 850 SQUARE FEET. A GARAGE BAY AND WORKSHOP AREA ARE LOCATED AT THE EASTERN PORTION OF THE BOILER HOUSE BASEMENT. ACCESS TUNNELS AND/OR PIPE CHASES CONNECT THE HORIZON CLINIC PROGRAM BUILDING,
BOILER HOUSE AND FAMILY MEDICINE BUILDING IN AN EAST-WEST DIRECTION. 

REMAINING PORTIONS OF THE SITE CONSIST OF ASPHALT PAVED ROADS, WALKWAYS AND PARKING LOTS ALONG WITH SOME LANDSCAPED AREAS AND WOODED LAND. THE SITE IS SERVICED BY PUBLIC WATER AND SEWER UTILITIES WITH A SEWER EASEMENT TRANSECTING THE SITE IN AN EAST-WEST ORIENTATION. THREE PROPANE ABOVEGROUND STORAGE TANKS
(ASTS) ARE LOCATED SOUTH OF THE FAMILY MEDICINE BUILDING AND ONE ADDITIONAL PROPANE STORAGE TANK IS LOCATED ADJACENT TO THE NORTHEAST CORNER OF THE FAMILY MEDICINE BUILDING. HEAT FOR THE SITE BUILDINGS IS CURRENTLY PROVIDED BY PROPANE-FIRED BOILER UNITS.
properties.SUMMARY:
THIS PHASE II ESA WAS DESIGNED TO CHARACTERIZE THE SITE FOR PROPOSED RESIDENTIAL REUSE, TO IDENTIFY POTENTIAL EXPOSURE RISKS TO CONSTRUCTION/UTILITY WORKERS DURING FUTURE REDEVELOPMENT AND/OR UTILITY WORK AT THE SITE, AND TO DETERMINE IF REMEDIATION OR MITIGATION MEASURES ARE NECESSARY TO ELIMINATE POTENTIAL
HEALTH AND/OR ENVIRONMENTAL RISKS. 

THE SCOPE OF WORK FOR THE PHASE II ESA INCLUDED THE ADVANCEMENT OF SOIL BORINGS, COLLECTION OF SURFICIAL AND SUBSURFACE SOIL SAMPLES, INSTALLATION OF TEMPORARY GROUNDWATER MONITORING WELLS, ADVANCEMENT OF CONCRETE CORINGS, AND THE LABORATORY ANALYSIS OF SOIL AND GROUNDWATER SAMPLES. A GEOPHYSICAL SURVEY WAS CONDUCTED PRIOR TO PHASE II FIELD ACTIVITIES TO EVALUATE THE EXTENT OF OIL PIPING THAT WAS OBSERVED EXITING THE BOILER HOUSE BUILDING THROUGH A PIPE CHASE. IN ADDITION, A HAZARDOUS BUILDING MATERIALS INVENTORY (HBMI) WAS PERFORMED IN CONJUNCTION WITH THE PHASE II ESA ACTIVITIES. THE HBMI WAS IMPLEMENTED TO CONFIRM FINDINGS AND EVALUATE DATA GAPS ASSOCIATED WITH PREVIOUS ASSESSMENTS OF BUILDING MATERIALS
ASSOCIATED WITH THE SITE BUILDINGS.

THE PHASE II ESA IDENTIFIED PETROLEUM CONTAMINATED SOIL AND GROUNDWATER IN ONE SOIL BORING LOCATED IN THE PARKING LOT AREA TO THE NORTH OF THE HORIZON CLINIC PROGRAM BUILDING. PETROLEUM CONTAMINANTS IN THIS AREA ARE PRESUMED TO BE ASSOCIATED WITH RELEASES FROM A 1,000-GALLON #2 FUEL OIL UST FORMERLY LOCATED AT
146 DRESDEN AVENUE. ARSENIC CONCENTRATIONS EXCEEDING BACKGROUND CONDITIONS AND THE APPLICABLE MEDEP REMEDIAL ACTION GUIDELINES (RAGS) WERE DETECTED IN TWO SURFICIAL SOIL SAMPLES COLLECTED FROM THE LAWN AREA SURROUNDING THE HORIZON CLINIC PROGRAM BUILDING. THE ELEVATED CONCENTRATIONS OF ARSENIC
ARE PRESUMED TO BE ASSOCIATED WITH HISTORIC COAL COMBUSTION AT THE SITE AND/OR IMPORTED FILL MATERIAL.

THE HAZARDOUS BUILDING MATERIALS INVENTORY (HBMI) CONDUCTED AS PART OF THIS PHASE II ESA IDENTIFIED ASBESTOS-CONTAINING MATERIAL (ACM) AND LEAD-BASED PAINTED SURFACES IN SITE BUILDINGS, ALONG WITH POLYCHLORINATED BIPHENYL (PCB)-CONTAINING FLUORESCENT LIGHT BALLASTS AND MERCURY-CONTAINING FLUORESCENT
LIGHT TUBES. THESE MATERIALS WILL NEED TO BE PROPERLY ABATED AND/OR REMOVED IF DISTURBED DURING FUTURE SITE REDEVELOPMENT. IN ADDITION, THE HBMI IDENTIFIED PCBS IN EXPANSION JOINT CAULKING ASSOCIATED WITH THE NORTHERN PORTION OF THE HORIZON CLINIC PROGRAM BUILDING. ADDITIONAL ASSESSMENT AND REMEDIAL ACTION
MAY BE REQUIRED IN REGARDS TO THE PCB-CONTAINING CAULKING IF THE CAULKING IS TO BE DISTURBED BY FUTURE BUILDING RENOVATION.

RESPONSE SERVICES WAS INFORMED OF AN ILLEGAL RELEASE OF OIL TO THE ROAD SURFACE AS DUST CONTROL. ONCE ONSITE RESPONSE SERVICES FOUND OIL STAINED SOILS ON THE ROAD SURFACE FOR AN ESTIMATED 240 FEET. A STRONG ODOR OF FUEL AND USED MOTOR OIL WAS NOTED. MR. GUPTILL WAS INFORMED OF THE COMPLAINT AT WHICH TIME HE STATED THAT HE HAD SPRAYED CALCIUM CHLORIDE ON THE ROAD AS DUST CONTROL. A SAMPLE WAS TAKEN OF THE ROAD SURFACE AND FIELD SCREENING OF THE SAMPLE WAS CONDUCTED ONSITE. RESULTS OF THE SCREENING INDICATED A STRONG POSITIVE FOR OIL PRESENCE. 

RESPONSE SERVICES WAS ALLOWED TO INSPECT THE SMALL SPRAY TANK MOUNTED ON MR. GUPTILL'S ALL-TERRAIN VEHICLE USED TO APPLY THE "DUST CONTROL". UPON VISUAL INSPECTION, A BLACK OILY SOLUTION WITH A STRONG FUEL SMELL WAS FOUND IN THE BOTTOM OF THE TANK. MR. GUPTILL WAS INFORMED OF THE PRESENCE OF OIL ON THE ROAD SURFACE AND THE NEED TO CLEAN IT UP TO THE DEPARTMENTS STANDARD. AT THIS TIME RESPONSE SERVICES WAS VERBALLY EJECTED FROM THE PROPERTY.

THE TOWN OF PATTEN WAS INFORMED THAT THE RELEASE OF OIL ON THE ROAD SURFACE WAS CONFIRMED, AND THAT MR. GUPTILL REFUSED TO TAKE RESPONSIBILITY FOR THE RELEASE. THE TOWN FILED A POLICE REPORT CONCERNING THE ILLEGAL DISCHARGE OF OIL TO TOWN PROPERTY.

RESPONSE SERVICES HIRED SMALLWOOD CONSTRUCTION TO REMOVE SOILS AND REGRADE THE ROAD.

THE SITE HAS BEEN TURNED OVER TO THE DEPARTMENTS ENFORCEMENT UNIT AND THE COST RECOVERY UNIT.

NO FURTHER ACTION SHOULD BE REQUIRED OF RESPONSE SERVICES AT THIS TIME.

IT IS NOT KNOWN WHEN THE FIRST BUILDING WAS CONSTRUCTED ON THE PROPERTY, BUT 1906 TOPOGRAPHIC MAPPING INDICATES A BUILDING WAS PRESENT AT APPROXIMATELY THE CURRENT LOCATION OF THE FORMER RESIDENTIAL STRUCTURE ON NATTS POINT. THE U.S. COAST GUARD OWNED THE PROPERTY IN THE 1940S AND STARTED TO CONSTRUCT A COMMUNICATIONS STATION, BUT STOPPED AT THE END OF WORLD WAR II. AT LEAST TWO BUILDINGS WERE CONSTRUCTED ON SITE AT THAT TIME. THE REMAINING BUILDINGS AT THE SITE WERE CONSTRUCTED SHORTLY AFTER 1955 WHEN MATTHEW VANLOON PURCHASED THE PROPERTY FROM THE GOVERNMENT AND STARTED THE STERLING NET & TWINE CO. SINCE THEN TO APPROXIMATELY 2010 THE WESTERN PORTION OF THE PROPERTY WAS USED FOR THE STERLING NET & TWINE CO. BUSINESS, WHILE THE EASTERN PORTION WAS USED RECREATIONALLY AND POTENTIALLY FOR AGRICULTURE (BLUEBERRY FIELD). THERE IS MUCH SOLID WASTE (NETS, ROPE, TWINE, CARDBOARD, EMPTY PLASTIC BUCKETS, AND EMPTY STEEL DRUMS) IN AND AROUND THE STERLING NET & TWINE BUILDINGS AT THE WESTERN END OF THE SITE.

I RECIEVED A REPORT FROM A CONTRACTOR THAT A BURNER MALFUNCTION CAUSED A LEAK IN A BASEMENT.   THE REPAIR WAS MADE TO THE BURNER AND THE LEAK WAS STOPPED.   HOWEVER ACCORDING TO THE CONTRACTOR THE LEAK HAD BEEN GOING ON FOR A FEW DAYS UNTIL THE OWNER WAS ABLE TO GET SOMEONE TO MAKE THE REPAIR.  THE LEAK WAS REPORTED AS SMALL AND NO DRAINS INVOLVED.   WHEN I ARRIVED I DISCOVERED THAT THE LEAK WAS LARGER THAN ORIGIONALLY THOUGHT.  

OIL IMPACTED A LARGE AREA OF THE BASEMENT WHICH ALSO HAD A GREAT DEAL OF UNWANTED HOUSEHOLD MATERIAL.  PART OF THE BASEMENT WAS FLOODED.  THERE WAS A SUMP PUMP THAT APPEARED TO BE OCCATIONALLY WORKING AND PUMPING THE OILLY WATER INTO A STREAM, THEN TO THE OCEAN.   THE HOME WAS SERVED BY A DUG WELL IN THE BASEMENT THAT WAS POTENTIALLY IMPACTED.   A FAMILY OF FOUR WITH TWO YOUNG CHILDREN LIVING AT THE HOME AND THE VAPORS WERE UNACCEPTABLE.

ACCES WAS GAINED TO THE BULKHEAD AND HOUSEHOLD GOODS AND DEBRIS WAS BAGGED UP AND REMOVED.  CLEAN HARBORS WAS CALLED TO PUMP THE OIL AND WATER FROM THE BASEMENT, REMOVE THE REST OF THE DEBRIS AND CLEAN THE FLOOR.  THE VAPORS IN THE BASEMENT AFTER THAT TASK WAS COMPLETED WAS ESSENTIALLY ZERO.

SIERRA PEAKS CORPORATION OPERATED EXCLUSIVELY WITHIN THE BUILDING IDENTIFIED AS BUILDING 400, (THE "SITE BUILDING") LOCATED AT 5 COLCORD AVENUE IN CAMDEN, MAINE (THE "SITE"). THE SITE
BUILDING IS PART OF A LARGER COMPLEX OF BUILDINGS OCCUPYING A COMMON PARCEL OF LAND ASSOCIATED WITH THE STREET ADDRESS OF 5 COLCORD AVENUE. THE COMMON PARCEL OF LAND INCLUDES ADDITIONAL BUILDINGS IDENTIFIED AS BUILDING 300 AND BUILDING 500, AS WELL AS TWO METAL-SIDED STORAGE SHED STRUCTURES. 

THE SITE BUILDING IS A SINGLE-STORY BRICK BUILDING CONSTRUCTED WITH CONCRETE SLAB-ON-GRADE FOUNDATION, OCCUPYING A FOOTPRINT OF APPROXIMATELY 11,500 SQUARE FEET. A FORMER BOILER ROOM WITH SEPARATE ENTRANCE IS LOCATED ON THE SOUTH SIDE OF THE SITE BUILDING. THE SITE BUILDING WAS HISTORICALLY CONNECTED TO THE OTHER BUILDINGS (BUILDINGS 300 AND 500) ON THE COMMON PARCEL OF LAND THROUGH A SERIES OF UNDERGROUND UTILITY
CONDUIT TUNNELS. THESE UTILITY TUNNELS HAVE SINCE BEEN ABANDONED AND BUILDINGS AT THE 5 COLCORD AVENUE ADDRESS CURRENTLY OPERATE INDEPENDENTLY FROM EACH OTHER. MUNICIPAL SEWER AND WATER UTILITIES ARE AVAILABLE TO THE SITE AND SURROUNDING PROPERTIES.
properties.SUMMARY:
THE SITE BUILDING AS WELL AS BUILDINGS 300 AND 500 WERE DEVELOPED ON THE COMMON PARCEL OF LAND IN 1950 AS A MANUFACTURING FACILITY FOR TIBBETTS INDUSTRIES INC (TIBBETTS). OPERATIONS INCLUDED THE MANUFACTURE AND ASSEMBLY OF MINIATURE ELECTRO-ACOUSTIC TRANSDUCERS, TELECOILS, MICROPHONES AND OTHER DEVICES USED FOR HEARING AIDS AND BIOMEDICAL AND SECURITY PRODUCTS. HAZARDOUS MATERIALS, INCLUDING CHLORINATED SOLVENTS AND VARIOUS ALCOHOLS WERE USED AND STORED ON-SITE FOR PARTS CLEANING. WASTE SOLVENTS WERE GENERATED DURING THE MANUFACTURING PROCESS. THE METAL-SIDED STORAGE SHEDS ADJACENT TO BUILDING 500 WERE CONSTRUCTED IN 1980 AND 1981 AND USED FOR HAZARDOUS MATERIAL AND HAZARDOUS WASTE STORAGE. TIBBETTS OPERATED FROM 1950 UNTIL 2007, AT WHICH TIME THEY WERE ACQUIRED BY INTRICON CORPORATION. INTRICON CONTINUED OPERATIONS IN BUILDINGS 300, 400, AND 500 AND OPERATED AT THE SITE UNTIL 2014. IN 2014 THE COMMON PROPERTY WAS SOLD AND ESTABLISHED AS A CONDOMINIUM WITH MULTIPLE TENANTS IN COMMON. RCRA
CLOSURES WERE NOT COMPLETED FOR EITHER TIBBETTS CORPORATION OR INTRICON CORPORATION AT THE TIME THEY CEASED OPERATIONS AT THE SITE.

SIERRA PEAKS PURCHASED THE ELECTRO-ACOUSTIC LINE FROM INTRICON AND BEGAN OPERATIONS IN BUILDING 400 IN JANUARY 2014. DURING SIERRA PEAKS OPERATIONS, SMALL QUANTITIES OF HAZARDOUS SUBSTANCES AND HAZARDOUS WASTE WERE STORED IN THE FORMER BOILER ROOM PORTION OF BUILDING 400. HAZARDOUS WASTES WERE PERIODICALLY TRANSPORTED UNDER MANIFEST TO A LICENSED DISPOSAL FACILITY.

FOUR UNDERGROUND STORAGE TANKS (USTS) CONTAINING FUEL OIL WERE HISTORICALLY REGISTERED WITH THE MAINE DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION (MEDEP) (FACILITY I.D. #6776) IN CONNECTION WITH THE COMMON PROPERTY PARCEL. TWO OF THESE USTS (AN 8,000-GALLON FUEL OIL UST AND A 10,000-GALLON FUEL OIL UST)
WERE HISTORICALLY ASSOCIATED WITH THE SITE BUILDING. DUE TO PROXIMITY TO THE SITE BUILDING, THE 8,000-GALLON UST WAS ABANDONED IN PLACE IN 1996. THE 10,000-GALLON UST WAS REMOVED IN 1997. A PHASE II ENVIRONMENTAL SITE ASSESSMENT (ESA) WAS CONDUCTED IN 2007 TO EVALUATE THE FORMER USTS, AND
APPROXIMATELY 323 TONS OF PETROLEUM CONTAMINATED SOIL WAS REMOVED FROM THE AREA OF THE FORMER 10,000-GALLON UST. THE EXCAVATION WAS LIMITED BY PROXIMITY TO VIRGINIA AVENUE.

WOODEN FLOORS ARE IMPROVED THROUGHOUT THE GROUND LEVEL OF THE SITE BUILDING, WHICH WERE ORIGINALLY

THE NORTHERN HALF OF THE BASEMENT IS IMPROVED WITH A POURED CONCRETE FLOOR AND THE SOUTHERN HALF OF THE BASEMENT'S FLOOR IS BARE SOIL/DIRT. AN AUTOMOTIVE SERVICE PIT IS LOCATED AT THE WESTERN PORTION OF THE BUILDING. THE AUTOMOTIVE SERVICE PIT

properties.SUMMARY:

THE SITE PROPERTIES ARE CURRENTLY OWNED BY L&R NORTHPOINT HOLDINGS, LLC (L&R). THE 1 MADISON STREET PROPERTY IS CURRENTLY IMPROVED WITH A 41,000 SQUARE-FEET STEEL-FRAME, STEEL-SIDED, WAREHOUSE-TYPE BUILDING THAT WAS CONSTRUCTED IN 1969 AS THE GENERAL ELECTRIC (GE) VALVE MANUFACTURING BUILDING (BUILDING 25X). THE 110 BREAKWATER ANNEX PROPERTY IS IMPROVED WITH A SINGLE-STORY 8,000 SQUARE FOOT BUILDING THAT WAS REPORTEDLY CONSTRUCTED IN VARIOUS PHASES FROM CIRCA 1963 TO 2017. THE 120 BREAKWATER ANNEX PROPERTY IS CURRENTLY IMPROVED WITH A 12,000 SQUARE-FEET, STEEL-FRAME, STEEL-SIDED, WAREHOUSE-TYPE BUILDING THAT WAS CONSTRUCTED CIRCA 1940 AS THE POWER HOUSE (COAL-FIRED POWER PLANT) FOR
NEW ENGLAND SHIPBUILDING CORPORATION'S (NESC'S) SHIPYARD COMPLEX. THE 149 FRONT STREET PROPERTY IS CURRENTLY IMPROVED WITH AN 8,400 SQUARE-FEET STEEL-FRAME, STEEL-SIDED, WAREHOUSE-TYPE BUILDING THAT WAS CONSTRUCTED CIRCA 1968. THE 159 FRONT STREET PROPERTY IS CURRENTLY IMPROVED WITH A 750 SQUARE-FEET,
SINGLE-STORY, CONCRETE-BLOCK BUILDING THAT WAS CONSTRUCTED CIRCA 1940 AS THE GATE HOUSE (BUILDING NO. 5) FOR NESC'S SHIPYARD COMPLEX.
properties.SUMMARY:
PRIOR TO 1940, A MAJORITY OF THE SITE WAS SUBMERGED AND/OR PARTIALLY SUBMERGED BENEATH CASCO BAY/PORTLAND HARBOR, WITH THE EXCEPTION OF AREAS ALONG FRONT STREET, WHICH WERE IMPROVED WITH RESIDENTIAL DWELLINGS DATING BACK TO THE 1700S. FROM CIRCA 1940 TO 1943, THE U.S. GOVERNMENT ACQUIRED THE SITE PROPERTIES AND BROUGHT FILL TO THE PROPERTIES IN ORDER FOR THE SITE TO BE UTILIZED AS A SHIPYARD MANUFACTURING FACILITY TO MEET THE DEMAND OF WORLD WAR II. FROM CIRCA 1940 UNTIL 1945, THE U.S.
GOVERNMENT CONTRACTED THE TODD-BATH SHIPYARD, WHICH LATER BECAME NESC TO OPERATE THE SHIPYARD. THE SITE WAS KNOWN AS THE TODD-BATH SHIPYARD AND NESC'S "WEST YARD." IN 1946, GREATER PORTLAND PUBLIC DEVELOPMENT COMMISSION (GPPDC) PURCHASED THE SITE FROM THE U.S. GOVERNMENT. GPPDC SUBDIVIDED AND SOLD THE SITE PARCELS TO VARIOUS OWNERS, WHICH HAVE UTILIZED/OCCUPIED THE SITE FOR VARIOUS INDUSTRIAL AND COMMERCIAL BUSINESSES TO THE PRESENT DATE. 

NUMEROUS ENVIRONMENTAL INVESTIGATIONS AND REMEDIAL ACTIVITIES HAVE BEEN COMPLETED THROUGHOUT THE LIBERTY SHIPYARD SITE FROM THE 1980S TO THE 2010S. IN MAY OF 2020, RANSOM COMPLETED AN ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW AND DATA GAPS EVALUATION FOR ENTIRE LIBERTY SHIPYARD SITE UNDER THE CITY'S BROWNFIELDS ASSESSMENT PROGRAM. BASED ON OUR FINDINGS, RANSOM IDENTIFIED THAT SOIL, GROUNDWATER, SOIL VAPOR AND/OR INDOOR AIR HAS BEEN IMPACTED BY HAZARDOUS SUBSTANCES OR PETROLEUM (HSP) AT VARIOUS AREAS AT THE LIBERTY SHIPYARD SITE.

A FITTING AT THE TANK FOR THE PIPING TO THE FILTER FAILED ALLOWING APPROXIMATELY 50 GALLONS TO SPILL ONTO THE CONCRETE FLOOR.  THE FIRE DEPARTMENT LAID DOWN SORBETS.   WHEN I ARRIVED I LAID DOWN MORE SORBENTS AND THEN CLEANED THE FLOOR WITH A DEGREASER.  I ALSO INSTALLED A COUPLE OF DIFFERENT SIZE FANS FOR VENTING OIL VAPORS TO THE OUTDOORS.  THE LARGE FAN WAS OPERATED THE FIRST NIGHT.  THIS LARGE FAN WAS REMOVED A COUPLE OF DAYS LATER.   A SMALL FAN WAS LEFT AT THE SITE FOR SOME TIME FOR WHEN THE OWNERS VISIT.  

MY SECOND VISIT INDICATED VERY LOW LEVELS OF VAPORS IN THE SPILL AREA AND NO VAPORS WERE DETECTED IN THE BASEMENT OR UPSTAIRS.  THE SITE WAS CHECK A COUPLE OF TIMES AFTER HEAVY RAINS TO SEE IF OIL HAD EMERGED ALONG THE STEEP BANK, BACKYARD OF THE HOUSE.  NO OIL WAS OBSERVED.  THE SITE HAS BEEN REFERRED TO PAUL BLOOD OF THE MAINE DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION TECHNICAL SERVICES DUE TO THE OWNER'S WELL BEING NEARBY, 30 FEET UPGRADIENT OF THE SPILL.  

NO FURTHER ACTION BY THE DIVISION OF RESPONSE SERVICES IS EXPECTED AT THIS TIME.

DURING OUR DISCUSSION, IT WAS EXPLAINED TO ME THAT THE ELDERLY HANDY-MAN IS SUFFERING FROM DEMENTIA AND IS NOT SURE WHAT HE ADDED TO THEIR PLUMBING SYSTEM TO WINTERIZED THE SYSTEM. THE HOME OWNER CLAIMS THAT IS SMELLED OF OIL.

I CALLED DEPARTMENT GEOLOGIST, PAUL BLOOD TO ASK FOR ASSISTANCE AND POTENTIAL WATER SAMPLE. MR. BLOOD WAS CORPORATIVE AND QUICK TO GATHER A SAMPLE. THIS SAMPLE CAME BACK POSITIVE FOR OIL. AT THIS POINT MR. BLOOD AND THE DEPARTMENT'S TECHNICAL SERVICES DIVISION IS ASSISTING WITH WATER FILTERS AND LONG TERM SOLUTION TO THE PROBLEM.


NO FURTHER RESPONSE ACTION EXPECTED.

properties.SUMMARY:
MR. GILPATRICK WAS RETURNING BACK TO MAINE AFTER SPENDING THE WINTER IN TEXAS ONLY TO FIND OUT THAT HE WAS OUT OF OIL.  THIS WAS IN APRIL OF 2020.  HE HAD 100 GALLONS DELIVERED AND ARRIVED TO HIS HOUSE TO FIND A SMALL LEAK IN THE BOTTOM OF HIS ABOVEGROUND STORAGE TANK (AST).   A FRIEND INSERTED A SCREW INTO THE HOLE TO STOP THE LEAK.   HE REPLACED THE LEAKING AST WITH A NEW AST AFTER ALL THE OIL WAS CONSUMED.  OIL VAPORS WERE NEVER A PROBLEM IN THE HOUSE, ACCORDING TO MR. GILPATRICK.   

THIS SUMMER THEIR DRINKING WATER STARTED TO HAVE A PETROLEUM TASTE AND SMELL.   DURING MY VISIT I NOTICED A VERY SLIGHT STAIN ON THE CONCRETE UNDER THE NEW AST.   THE STAIN WAS MAYBE A FOOT IN DIAMETER AND WAS DIFFICULT TO SEE.   A 1.5 INCH OPENING WAS OBSERVED BETWEEN THE FOUNDATION WALL AND FLOOR WHICH ALLOWS WATER TO FLOW ALONG THE FOUNDATION WALL.  THE WATER FLOWS TOWARDS THE END OF THE HOUSE WHERE THE DRINKING WATER WELL IS LOCATED, APPROXIMATELY 4 FEET FROM THE OUTSIDE WALL OF THE HOUSE.   THE AST IS LOCATED AT THE OPPOSITE END OF THE BASEMENT HOWEVER IT APPEARS THE OIL THAT LEAKED OUT WENT INTO THIS 1.5 INCH OPENING AND FLOWED TOWARDS THE END OF THE HOUSE WHERE THE DRINKING WATER WELL IS LOCATED.  

BEDROCK IS LOCATED APPROXIMATELY A COUPLE OF FEET BELOW THE GROUND SURFACE.   THE DRINKING WATER WELL HAS APPROXIMATELY 10 FEET OF CASING.  I OBSERVED A SLIGHT SHEEN ON THE WATER INSIDE THE DRINKING WATER WELL AND A NEARBY DUG WELL.  

I REFERRED THIS SITE TO PAUL BLOOD OF MAINE DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION TECHNICAL SERVICES WHO TESTED THE DRINKING WATER.  THE LABORATORY TEST CAME BACK POSITIVE FOR PETROLEUM SO FILTERS WERE INSTALLED IN THE BASEMENT TO REMOVE THE PETROLEUM FROM THE DRINKING WATER.

properties.SUMMARY:
NEW PORTLAND FIRE DEPARTMENT CALLED TO REPORT THAT A DUMP TRUCK HAD CAUGHT FIRE AND RELEASED DIESEL FUEL ONTO THE GROUND. THE HEAT OF THE FIRE HAD MELTED A HOLE IN THE FUEL TANK, LEAVING AN OPENING. THE FIRE DEPARTMENT SPRAYED WATER ONTO THE FIRE, RESULTING IN AN OVERFLOW OF THE FUEL TANK AND RELEASE OF DIESEL FUEL. MOST OF THE SPILLED PRODUCT WAS CONTAINED TO THE ROAD AND RECOVERED WITH SORBENTS. A SMALL QUANTITY OF FUEL WAS RECOVERED FROM THE FUEL TANK.

THE RESPONSIBLE PARTY WAS ABLE TO USE PERSONAL EQUIPMENT TO CONDUCT THE SOIL REMEDIATION. THE CONTAMINATED SOIL WAS REMOVED AND DISPOSED OF AT THE HARTLAND TOWN LANDFILL. WELL WATER SAMPLES OF THE AREA ARE BEING CONSIDERED FOR TESTING DUE TO CLOSE PROXIMITY OF THE SPILL.

NO FURTHER ACTION BY THE DIVISION OF RESPONSE SERVICES IS ANTICIPATED AT THIS TIME.

properties.SUMMARY: THE ABOVEGROUND TANK AT THIS LOCATION WAS OVERFILLED.  THE MAJORITY OF SPILLED PRODUCT SPRAYED INTO THE UTILITY ROOM. A SMALL QUANTITY OF OIL WAS RELEASED OUT THE VENT ONTO A WOODEN DECK AND SNOW.  CONTAMINATED MATERIALS WERE BAGGED AND REMOVED FROM THE PREMISES INTO A CONSTRUCTION DUMPSTER ALREADY ON SITE.  SORBENT MATERIALS WERE THEN USED TO RECOVER ANY REMAINING STANDING OIL AND THE FLOOR WAS WASHED WITH A CLEANER/DEGREASER.  A LARGE CRACK IN THE MIDDLE OF THE FLOOR WHERE THE SPILL OCCURRED ALLOWED OIL TO PENETRATE THE SLAB AND A GAP BETWEEN THE SLAB AND FOUNDATION ALSO PROVED TO BE EMITTING VAPORS.  TO MANAGE THIS ISSUE, THE CRACKS WERE SEALED WITH AN EPOXY AND SUB SLAB VENTILATION FAN WAS INSTALLED.   OUTSIDE THE UTILITY ROOM WAS A BASEMENT DENTIST'S OFFICE WITH TREATMENT AND STAFF AREAS.  A LACK OF WINDOWS LIMITED VENTILATION SO PORTABLE AIR SCRUBBERS WERE PROVIDED TO EXCHANGE THE AIR IN THE PRACTICE.  THE SCRUBBERS WERE EFFECTIVE AND THE PRACTICE WAS REOPENED AFTER A VOLUNTARY TWO DAY CLOSURE.

properties.SUMMARY: A COMPLAINT HAS BEEN FILED WITH THE MAINE DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION (DEP) OF THE POSSIBLE DUMPING OF USED OIL AT 263 AND 273 SMITHFIELD ROAD. THE COMPLAINANT EXPRESSED A CONCERN OIL DUMPING ACTIVITIES COULD HAVE AN IMPACT ON A WETLANDS AREA NEAR THE NORTHEAST CORNER OF THE COMPLAINANT'S PROPERTY AND THE ADJOINING PROPERTY TO THE NORTH. ON THE MORNING OF NOVEMBER 21ST, 2022, DEP PERSONNEL ARRIVED AT 250 SMITHFIELD ROAD IN BELGRADE TO INVESTIGATE THE ALLEGED USED OIL DUMPING ON THE ADJACENT PROPERTIES AT 263 AND 273 SMITHFIELD ROAD. THE COMPLAINANT HAS PERIODICALLY WITNESSED USED OIL BEING DRAINED FROM EQUIPMENT STRAIGHT TO THE GROUND LEAVING OIL STAINS ON THESE PROPERTIES NEAR THE EASTSIDE OF SMITHFIELD ROAD. SEE AREA HIGHLIGHTED IN ATTACHED MAP. FAINT STAINS WERE NOTED DURING THE VISIT IN THE LOCATION THE COMPLAINANT HAD WITNESSED THE DUMPING, THEY FURTHER STATED THEY HAVE WITNESSED THE OWNER OF THE PROPERTY COVER THE FRESH OIL STAINS WITH GRAVEL AND USE HEAVY EQUIPMENT TO PUSH THE CONTAMINATED MATERIALS AWAY FROM SMITHFIELD ROAD TO THE EAST. WHILE ON-SITE DEP PERSONNEL ATTEMPTED TO FIND VISIBLE EVIDENCE OF OIL CONTAMINATION IN AREAS ADJACENT TO THE OIL DUMPING LOCATION. WATER IN THE WETLANDS AREA WAS MOSTLY COVERED IN A THIN LAYER OF ICE HAMPERING THE ABILITY TO IDENTIFY A PETROLEUM SHEEN ON THE WATER, AND OIL STAINING IN SOIL WAS NOT OBSERVED IN AREAS OTHER THAN THE OIL DUMPING ZONE. ONE SOIL SAMPLE WAS COLLECTED FROM THE WEST SIDE OF SMITHFIELD ROAD NEAR THE NORTHEAST CORNER OF THE COMPLAINANT'S PROPERTY. THE SAMPLE LOCATION WAS DETERMINED TO BE IN A LOCATION THAT HAD THE POSSIBILITY TO BE IMPACTED DUE TO THE OIL DUMPING IN CERTAIN SURFACE WATER RUNOFF CONDITIONS.

A 10000 GALLON FIBERGLASS TANK AND ASSOCIATED PIPING WERE REMOVED AND REPLACED IN THE SAME LOCATION. A PREVIOUS RELEASE DOCUMENTED IN SPILL ID B-566-1995 DESCRIBES CONTAMINATION DISCOVERED IN THE TANK BASIN THAT WAS LEFT IN PLACE DUE TO THE LACK OFSENSITIVE RECEPTORS IN THE AREA. THIS HISTORIC CONTAMINATION WAS LIKELY THE REASON FOR THE LAB SAMPLES RETURNING RESULTS ABOVE THE LABORATORY REPORTING LIMITS DURING THE OCTOBER 2022 SITE ASSESSMENT.

THIS UNDERGROUND STORAGE TANK (UST) SITE ASSESSMENT WAS CONDUCTED FOR THE REMOVAL OF THREE USTS (TANKS #7, 9 AND 10) AND ASSOCIATED UNDERGROUND PIPING AT DOC¿S PLACE LOCATED AT 782 NORTH MAIN STREET IN PRESQUE ISLE.

SIX SOIL SAMPLES (SS02, SS13, SS17, SS20, SS30 AND SS34) WERE COLLECTED FOR LABORATORY ANALYSIS OF VOLATILE PETROLEUM HYDROCARBONS (VPH) AND/OR EXTRACTABLE PETROLEUM HYDROCARBONS (EPH). AS SUMMARIZED ON THE ATTACHED SOIL SAMPLE RESULTS (TABLE I, APPENDIX), EPH WAS DETECTED IN SS17
AND SS20, BUT BELOW MEDEP CHAPTER 691 NOTIFICATION LEVELS. VPH WAS NOT DETECTED IN SOIL SAMPLES ABOVE THE LABORATORY REPORTING LIMIT.

UST AND ASSOCIATED VENTS, PIPING AND DISPENSER REMOVED FROM SITE AND NOT REPLACED. NO CONTAMINATION ABOVE MAINE NOTIFICATION LEVELS DETECTED WITH A PID DURING EXCAVATION. TWO LAB SAMPLES RETURNED LEVELS BELOW LAB REPORTING LIMITS.

THE FORMERLY ABANDONED TANKS WERE IDENTIFIED DURING MUNICIPAL REDEVELOPMENT OF TWOMBLY ROAD.

PID CONCENTRATION TEST RESULTS  WERE BELOW THE DEP NOTIFICATION LEVELS FOR ALL SAMPLES.

ONE SOIL SAMPLE [LS-6 (6-8¿)] WAS SUBMITTED FOR LABORATORY ANALYSIS OF VOLATILE PETROLEUM HYDROCARBONS (VPH) BY MASSACHUSETTS DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION (MASSDEP)  LS-6 (6-8¿), IS A DISCRETE SOIL SAMPLE COLLECTED FROM THE BASE OF THE UST EXCAVATION BENEATH TANK-2.  NO VPH COMPOUNDS WERE DETECTED IN THE SOIL SAMPLES ABOVE THE LABORATORY DETECTION LIMITS, WHICH ARE BELOW THE SOIL NOTIFICATION LEVELS AND THE APPLICABLE RAGS.

properties.SUMMARY:
ON 7/31/2023, DOWNEAST ENERGY REPORTED THAT A CUSTOMER HAD A LEAKING OIL LINE ON THEIR HOME HEATING OIL TANK. MAINE DEP RESPONDED TO THE SCENE AND MET WITH A DOWNEAST ENERGY TECHNICIAN AND THE TENANT OF THE PROPERTY. THE SKIRTING OF THE TRAILER HAD ALREADY BEEN REMOVED AND A VISIBLE STAIN WAS OBSERVED UNDER THE FUEL LINE. THE TECHNICIAN HAD ALREADY FIXED THE LINE AND THERE WAS NO FURTHER THREAT OF A DISCHARGE. THE TENANT ESTIMATED THAT 50 GALLONS COULD HAVE BEEN LOST BASED ON THE LAST TIME SHE LOOKED AT THE TANKS GAUGE. AIR QUALITY MONITORING WAS DONE INSIDE THE RESIDENCE WITH A PHOTOIONIZATION DEVICE, WHICH DID NOT REVEAL ANY HIGH VAPOR LEVELS. THE PROPERTY OWNER WAS CONTACTED AND A MEETING ABOUT CLEAN-UP OPTIONS TOOK PLACE. THE OWNER ELECTED TO CHOOSE OPTION ONE AND HAVE MAINE DEP LEAD THE CLEAN-UP. THEY ALSO APPLIED TO THE MAINE GROUND AND SURFACE WATERS CLEAN-UP AND RESPONSE FUND TO HELP WITH THE COST OF THE CLEAN-UP. 

MAINE DEP CONTRACTED CLEAN HARBORS TO VACTOR OUT THE CONTAMINATED SOIL UNDER THE TRAILER. THE SOIL REMOVAL WAS DIRECTED BY MAINE DEP UTILIZING OIL IN SOIL SHAKE TESTS TO DETERMINE THE PRESENCE OF OIL. THE EXCAVATION QUICKLY HAD CLEAN SHAKE TESTS ON ALL FOUR WALL, BUT LEDGE WAS FOUND AT THE BOTTOM OF THE EXCAVATION AROUND TWO FEET DOWN. A REFERRAL WAS MADE TO MAINE DEP TECHNICAL SERVICES GEOLOGISTS, WHO TOOK A SOIL SAMPLE FROM THE TOP OF THE LEDGE. A DRINKING WATER WELL, THAT SUPPLIED MULTIPLE TRAILERS, WAS IN THE PROXIMITY TO THE SPILL. TECHNICAL SERVICES TOOK A SAMPLE OF THE WELL WATER AND PLANNED TO TEST IT QUARTERLY. THE EXCAVATION WAS BACKFILLED AND THE CONTAMINATED MATERIAL WAS TAKEN TO JUNIPER RIDGE LANDFILL FOR DISPOSAL.

properties.DESCRIPTION: 139 OREGON RD IS LOCATED IN THE NORTHERN PORTION OF ISLESBORO. THE SITE IS APPROXIMAITLY 400 FEET SOUTHWEST OF MEADOW POND. THE PROPERTY CONSISTS OF A HOUSE WITH AN ATTACHED 2 CAR GARAGE. THERE IS A DETACHED GARAGE WEST OF THE DRIVEWAY. WATER FOR THE SITE IS PROVIDED BY A BEDROCK WELL LOCATED NEAR THE SOUTHEAST CORNER OF THE HOUSE NEAR THE SHORT DRIVEWAY. THE CURRENT WELL WAS DRILLED IN 2020, THE WELL IS LISTED AS BEING COMPLETED TO 160 FEET WITH 29 FEET OF CASING. THE DRILLERS ENCOUNTERED 15 FEET OF OVERBURDEN. EVIDENCE OF THE SEPTIC SYSTEM WAS NOTED NEAR THE WEST EDGE OF THE DRIVEWAY NEAR THE GARAGE.
properties.SUMMARY: ACCIDENTAL FAILURE OF A COPPER LINE IN THE DETACHED GARAGE BUILDING RELEASED AN ESTIMATED 100 GALLONS OF FUEL OIL ONTO THE WOOD FLOOR OF THE BUILDING. OIL LEAKED THROUGH THE FLOOR AND OUT THE SIDE AND FRONT OF THE BUILDING CONTINUEING ALONG SIDE THE ATTACHED GARAGE AND HOUSE FLOWING TOWARD A SMALL DRAINAGE DITCH THAT EMPTIES INTO MEADOW POND. EVIDENCE OF THE OIL MADE IT AS FAR AS THE NORTHEAST CORNER OF THE HOUSE. NO EVIDENCE OF OIL ENTERED THE DRAINAGE TO MEADOW POND. ACCORDING TO THE RESIDENT THE AREA THE SPILL IMPACTED CAN BE SOFT AND MARSHY, DURING THE SITE VISIT THE CONDITIONS IN THE AREAS IMPACTED BY THE RELEASE WERE SATURATED.  CLEAN HARBORS USED A VAC TRUCK TO REMOVE OIL REMAINING ON THE SURFACE OF THE SATURATED GROUND. TEST PITS DUG DURING THE CLEAN UP INDICATE GROUNDWATER IS ABOUT 1 FOOT BELOW THE SURFACE. THE RESIDENT STATED THAT IN THE NEAR FUTURE THERE WERE PLANS TO LANDSCAPE THE AREA TO PROVIDE PROPER DRAINAGE. NATE THOMPSON ASKED IF THAT WERE TO HAPPEN THAT HE SHOULD CONTACT THE DEP TO HAVE A REPRESENTATIVE ON HAND TO DETERMINE IF THE SOILS NEED TO BE REMOVED FROM THE SITE.
SITE WAS CREATED AT THE REQUEST OF COLLEEN HENDRICKS FOR A SELF-TESTER RELATED TO THE PFAS INVESTIGATION

properties.SUMMARY:
ON FEBRUARY 20TH, 2024, CN BROWN REPORTED A RELEASE OF #2 HOME HEATING OIL AT A RESIDENCE IN BENTON, MAINE.

THE SPILL WAS CAUSED BY AN OVERFILL.  CN BROWN BLAMED THE RELEASE ON THE ORIENTATION OF THE TANK, WHICH WAS FOUND TO BE TILTED, PURPORTEDLY CAUSING THE WHISTLE TO CONTINUE TO FUNCTION DESPITE THE TANK BEING FULL.  THIS LED TO OIL LEAKING OUT OF THE SEAMS OF THE PIPING AT THE TOP OF THE TANK, DRIPPING DOWN ONTO THE CONCRETE FLOOR.  RESPONSE ATTEMPTED MULTIPLE TIMES TO CONTACT THE OWNER OF THE PROPERTY WITHOUT SUCCESS.  THE PROPERTY OWNER REPORTEDLY STATED TO CN BROWN THAT HE WAS NOT INTERESTED IN ANY HELP FROM THE DEPARTMENT.  CN BROWN DID SUPPLY RESPONSE WITH THEIR SPILL REPORT ON THE INCIDENT AND STATED THE SPILL WAS CLEANED UP. 

ON FEBRUARY 26TH, THE HOMEOWNER, MR. FULLER, REACHED BACK TO RESPONSE AND STUART BLANCHARD VISITED THE SITE ON THE 27TH.  THE INTERIOR PORTION OF THE SPILL WAS LARGELY CLEANED UP WITH SORBENTS, HOWEVER MR. FULLER ALSO NOTED THAT FUEL HAD COME OUT OF THE VENT PIPING AS WELL.  RESPONSE HAND EXCAVATED BELOW THE VENT, DIGGING DOWN APPROXIMATELY 6" BELOW GRADE AND FOUND THE OIL HAD PENETRATED SIGNIFICANTLY DEEPER.  GIVEN THE SPILL OCCURRED WITHIN 50-75' OF THE MR. FULLER'S DRILLED WELL, IT WAS DETERMINED A MORE THOROUGH CLEANUP WAS WARRANTED.

MORSE'S ENTERPRISES WAS HIRED TO CONDUCT A CLEANUP AT THE SITE AND ALL CONTAMINATED SOIL WAS SUCCESSFULLY EXCAVATED AND TAKEN TO WASTE MANAGEMENT'S FACILITY IN NORRIDGEWOCK FOR PROPER DISPOSAL.  

THE SITE WAS REFERRED TO THE DIVISION OF TECHNICAL SERVICES TO ASSESS THE POTENTIAL THREAT TO THE HOMEOWNER'S WELL.

TECHNICAL SERVICES CONDUCTED INITIAL SAMPLING 3/5/24

THIS CAUSED THE OIL TO SPRAY ONTO THE SIDING OF THE HOUSE AND ONTO THE SOIL BELOW. (RESPONDER'S NOTES)

MAINE DEP WAS ALERTED TO A TRACTOR TRAILER ACCIDENT IN LIVERMORE. A VEHICLE DRIVING IN THE OPPOSITE LANE TRIED TO RUN HEAD ON INTO THE TRACTOR TRAILER. THE DRIVER OF THE TRACTOR TRAILER WAS ABLE TO AVOID THE VEHICLE MOSTLY BY ONLY SIDE SWIPING THEM AND THE GOING OFF THE ROAD AND DAMAGING ITS FUEL TANK. THE TRACTOR TRAILER HAD NO LOAD ON THE BACK AND WAS ONLY CARRYING ABOUT 50 GALLONS OF DIESEL. THE LIVERMORE FIRE DEPARTMENT DEPLOYED A BUNCH OF BOOM AND PADS TO TRY AND CONTAIN THE SPILL. I ARRIVED ON SCENE THE FOLLOWING MORNING AND CALLED EPI TO COME FOR A CLEAN UP OF THE STAINED SNOW AND ICE. WE SCRAPPED UP WHAT WE COULD FROM THE ROAD DOWN TO ANOTHER HOME AT THE END OF THE ROAD. THAT NIGHT WE HAD A LOT OF RAIN AND THEN MELTED SOME OF THE TRAPPED PRODUCT ON THE ROAD AND I WAS CALLED BY THE HOMEOWNER AT THE END OF THE ROAD. I RESPONDED BACK OUT THE NEXT DAY AND HAND SCRAPPED MORE STAINED ICE. THE SITE WAS THEN REFERRED TO TECHNICAL SERVICES FOR A WELL THAT WAS CLOSE TO WHERE THE SPILL WAS.

THIS ALLOWED THE NEWLY DELIVERED OIL TO FLOW OUT OF THE OLD LINE ONTO THE FLOOR AROUND THE TANK AND AT THE FURNACE. THE FLOOR WAS VISIBLY STAINED, AND 1 DRAIN HOLE IN THE CONCRETE WAS POTENTIALLY AFFECTED BY THE RELEASE.  AN ACTIVE SUMP WAS IDENTIFIED NEAR THE FURNACE; HOWEVER NO SIGNS OF OIL COULD BE OBSERVED AT THE TIME OF THE INITIAL RESPONSE.  MORSE'S ENTERPRISES WAS HIRED TO CONDUCT A CLEANUP AT THE SITE.

ON 07/18/2025, THE MAINE DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION (MEDEP) RECEIVED REPORT OF AN OIL SPILL AT FIRST NATIONAL BANK IN DAMARISCOTTA. THE SPILL OF AN ESTIMATED 75 GALLONS OF HEATING OIL WAS THE RESULT OF A CORROSION HOLE IN THE BOTTOM OF AN ABOVE-GROUND STORAGE TANK.

SOIL WAS DISPOSED OF AT WASTE MANAGEMENT CROSSROADS LANDFILL. THE DAMAGED TANK WAS ALSO REMOVED AND PROPERLY DISPOSED OF. DUE TO THE LOCATION OF THE SPILL, OIL VAPORS WERE ABLE TO MIGRATE INTO THE OFFICE BUILDING.

properties.SUMMARY:
ON OCTOBER 14TH, 2025, THE MAINE DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION (MDEP) RECEIVED A REPORT OF A LEAKING K-1 HEATING OIL LINE AT A RESIDENCE IN MADISON, MAINE. STUART BLANCHARD RESPONDED TO THE SITE.  THE LEAK HAD BEEN DISCOVERED BY BOB'S CASH FUEL AND REPORTED IMMEDIATELY TO THE DEPARTMENT.  BOB'S CASH FUEL HAD BEEN HIRED TO SERVICE THE SYSTEM AND DISCOVERED SOME FORCE HAD ACTED UPON THE FUEL LINE, SEVERING IT.  A STICK HAD BEEN SHOVED INTO THE LINE, MOSTLY STOPPING THE LEAK BUT FOR A VERY SLOW DRIP.  UPON TALKING WITH THE HOMEOWNER, THEY CLAIMED THEY WERE UNAWARE OF ANY LEAK AND THOUGHT THE TANK HAD BEEN EMPTY BUT ADMITTED THAT SOMEONE HAD BEEN WORKING IN THE YARD AROUND THE TANK SOMETIME IN THE PREVIOUS MONTH AND THAT THAT INDIVIDUAL MAY HAVE ACCIDENTALLY DAMAGED THE FUEL LINE, CAUSING THE SPILL  

THE RELEASE LEFT A SMALL STAIN IN THE GROUND, APPROXIMATELY 2-FEET IN DIAMETER.  MORSE'S ENTERPRISES WERE HIRED TO CONDUCT A CLEANUP AT THE SITE.

properties.SUMMARY: ON NOVEMBER 8TH, 2025, THE MAINE DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION (MDEP) RECEIVED A REPORT OF A #2 HEATING OIL RELEASE IN A CRAWL SPACE/BASEMENT IN GREENE, MAINE. STUART BLANCHARD RESPONDED TO THE SITE.  THE TANK WAS FOUND TO BE SITUATED IN THE MUD IN A PARTIALLY EXCAVATED CRAWL SPACE, SURROUNDED BY A HAND DUG FROST WALL FOUNDATION.  THE TANK WAS CONFIRMED TO BE EMPTY BY THE HOMEOWNER'S OIL COMPANY AND HAD EVIDENTLY COMPLETELY FAILED THROUGH EITHER CORROSION IN THE TANK AND/OR A FAILURE AT THE FILTER, SPILLING ITS CONTENTS TO THE STANDING WATER IN THE BASEMENT.  THE BASEMENT WAS FOUND TO BE PARTIALLY FLOODED, WITH RED FREE PRODUCT ON THE SURFACE. REPUBLIC SERVICES WAS HIRED TO DEWATER THE BASEMENT AND RECOVER AS MUCH FREE PRODUCT AS POSSIBLE.  APPROXIMATELY 1500 GALLONS OF OIL AND WATER WERE REMOVED AND TAKEN BY REPUBLIC FOR LATER DISPOSAL.  MORSE'S ENTERPRISES WERE HIRED THE FOLLOWING MONDAY, NOVEMBER 10TH, TO SET UP A TEMPORARY WATER FILTRATION SYSTEM TO KEEP THE SPACE DEWATERED AND APPROPRIATELY TREAT THE LIQUID BEING DISCHARGED.  REPUBLIC RETURNED TO THE SITE WITH A VACTOR TRUCK TO REMOVE ALL CONTAMINATED DEBRIS AND EXCAVATE AS MUCH CONTAMINATED SOIL OUT OF THE BASEMENT AS POSSIBLE.
